# Webex RoomOS xAPI: Commands, Configurations, Statuses & Events Reference

This document is the authoritative developer reference for Cisco RoomOS Collaboration Devices (Room Kit, Room Bar, Board Pro, Desk Pro, Codec EQ, etc.), detailing all xAPI Commands, Configurations, Statuses, and Events.

## RoomOS xAPI Developer Guide & Usage Methods

RoomOS devices expose the xAPI hierarchy through multiple interfaces. Below is how to use these APIs across Cloud REST, Node.js JSXAPI, and On-Device CLI/Macros.

#### 1. Webex Cloud REST API (`https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/`)
You can execute any RoomOS xCommand or query any xStatus over the Cloud REST API without local network access to the device:

- **Execute a Command (`POST /v1/xapi/command/{commandPath}`)**  
  *Required OAuth Scope:* `spark:xapi_commands`  
  ```http
  POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.Volume.Set
  Authorization: Bearer <WEBEX_ACCESS_TOKEN>
  Content-Type: application/json

  {
    "deviceId": "<your_device_id>",
    "arguments": {
      "Level": 70
    }
  }
  ```

- **Query Device Status (`GET /v1/xapi/status`)**  
  *Required OAuth Scope:* `spark:xapi_statuses`  
  ```http
  GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<your_device_id>&name=Audio.Volume
  Authorization: Bearer <WEBEX_ACCESS_TOKEN>
  ```

#### 2. Node.js JSXAPI Library (`jsxapi`)
For full-duplex WebSocket or SSH integrations:
```javascript
const jsxapi = require('jsxapi');
const xapi = jsxapi.connect('ssh://admin:password@device.ip');

// Execute Command
xapi.Command.Audio.Volume.Set({ Level: 70 });

// Query Status
xapi.Status.Audio.Volume.get().then(volume => console.log('Current volume:', volume));

// Listen to Event / Status changes
xapi.Status.RoomAnalytics.PeopleCount.Current.on(count => console.log('People in room:', count));
```

#### 3. CLI / SSH & Macro Syntax (On-Device)
In the RoomOS device Macro Editor or CLI:
```bash
# Execute Command
xCommand Audio Volume Set Level: 70

# Set Configuration
xConfiguration Video Input AirPlay Mode: On

# Query Status
xStatus Audio Volume
```

## 1 xCommand

### 1.1 xCommand AirPlay KeyEvent Back

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/AirPlay.KeyEvent.Back`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

If AirPlay is enabled, you can use the AirPlay KeyEvent commands to control audio and video playback, and to navigate the AirPlay menus (AirPlay Remote Control) on the video device. Refer to the Video Input AirPlay Mode setting on how to enable AirPlay. Use this command to navigate back.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/AirPlay.KeyEvent.Back`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand AirPlay KeyEvent Back [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.AirPlay.KeyEvent.Back.(...)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.11 xCommand Audio Diagnostics Advanced Run

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.Diagnostics.Advanced.Run`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This command sends out a noise signal sequentially on all audio output connectors and measures the room impulse response (RIR) between the output and the microphones. If a RIR is detected, the detected number of microphones (input), the detected number of output connectors, and the detected delay between the output and input is reported back. Example: xCommand Audio Diagnostics Advanced Run Volume: 50 MeasurementLength: 1 Result returned -> OK *r AdvancedRunResult (status=OK): *r AdvancedRunResult HdmiSpeakersDelay: "100 ms" *r AdvancedRunResult NumHdmiSpeakersDetected: 2 *r AdvancedRunResult NumMicsDetected: 1 ** end

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.Diagnostics.Advanced.Run`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio Diagnostics Advanced Run [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.Diagnostics.Advanced.Run.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Channel` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 13 (`Integer`) | The channel number, from left to right, of the selected output. |
| `MeasurementLength` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 10 (`Integer`) | The length of the measurement in number of seconds. In a noisy environment a longer measurement duration will give a more reliable and robust result. |
| `Output` | No | `Literal` | Literal | The output where the test signal should be directed. All: Measure the RIR on all outputs. HDMI: Measure the room impulse response (RIR)  of the device connected to the HDMI output. Headset: Measure the RIR of the headset (only available on video devices that have a headset). Internal: Measure the RIR of the internal loudspeaker (only available on video devices that have an internal loudspeaker). Line: Measure the RIR of the device connected to the Line output (only available on video devices that have a Line output). |
| `Volume` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 50 (`Integer`) | The volume of the test signal. In a noisy environment a higher volume gives more reliable and robust results. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.12 xCommand Audio Diagnostics AecReverb Reset

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.Diagnostics.AecReverb.Reset`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Reset the acoustic echo cancellation. This command is useful when making changes in the acoustical treatment of the room. All previous adaptations are cleared and a new measurement of the reverberation time is made. This is not allowed during a call.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.Diagnostics.AecReverb.Reset`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio Diagnostics AecReverb Reset [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.Diagnostics.AecReverb.Reset.(...)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.13 xCommand Audio Diagnostics AecReverb Run

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.Diagnostics.AecReverb.Run`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The command uses the acoustic echo canceller to give an estimate of the reverberation time in the room. This is done transparently, without interrupting the normal operation of the device.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.Diagnostics.AecReverb.Run`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio Diagnostics AecReverb Run [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.Diagnostics.AecReverb.Run.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `PlayMusic` | No | `Literal` | Literal | When On the command will play some music in order to give the echo canceller a proper signal to adapt to. In some cases, this may give a better estimate of the reverberation time. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.14 xCommand Audio Diagnostics MeasureDelay

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.Diagnostics.MeasureDelay`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This command measures the audio delay/latency in a device that is connected to the video device. A typical use case it to measure the delay in a TV connected to the video device via the HDMI connector. If the delay in a TV is too high, the real-time experience of a video call will be substantially degraded. If the delay is more than 50 ms we recommend the user to find a TV setting that has shorter delay. Typical TV settings that can reduce the delay are: Gaming Mode and PC Mode. This command will measure the delay between output and input (microphone). This means that if you are using an external acoustic echo canceller or audio mixer, this command will also measure the delay of these devices.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.Diagnostics.MeasureDelay`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio Diagnostics MeasureDelay [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.Diagnostics.MeasureDelay.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `MeasurementLength` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 10 (`Integer`) | The length of the measurement in number of seconds. In a noisy environment a longer measurement duration will give a more reliable and robust result. |
| `Output` | No | `Literal` | Literal | All: Measure the maximum delay of all outputs. HDMI: Measure the delay of the device connected to the HDMI output. Headset: Measure the delay of the headset (only available on video devices that have a headset). Internal: Measure the delay of the internal loudspeaker (only available on video devices that have an internal loudspeaker). Line: Measure the delay of the device connected to the Line output (only available on video devices that have a Line output). |
| `Volume` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 50 (`Integer`) | The volume of the test signal. In a noisy environment a higher volume gives more reliable and robust results. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.16 xCommand Audio Equalizer Update

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.Equalizer.Update`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

There are 8 audio equalizers; each one has 6 adjustable filter sections. Each section is a second-order filter, which can be configured to modify the signal passing through the selected equalizer. This command sets the equalizer parameters for the selected EqualizerId and Section. Codec EQ: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.Equalizer.Update`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio Equalizer Update [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.Equalizer.Update.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Enabled` | No | `Literal` | Literal | True: The modifications set for the section will be applied to the signal. False: No modifications will be applied to the signal. |
| `EqualizerId` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 8 (`Integer`) | The unique equalizer to which the modified settings apply. |
| `FilterType` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | The shape of the curve. highpass: Attenuate signals below a given frequency. highshelf: Amplify or attenuate signals above a given frequency. lowpass: Attenuate signals above a given frequency. lowshelf: Amplify or attenuate signals below a given frequency. none: Straight pass through of the signal (the same as Enabled: False). peaking: Amplify or attenuate signals around a given frequency. |
| `Frequency` | Yes | `String` | String | The frequency in Hertz [Hz] around which the filter is tuned. A number in the range 20 – 20 000. |
| `Gain` | Yes | `String` | String | The gain in deciBels [dB] applied to either the entire curve or a selected part of the curve, depending on the filtertype. A number in the range -100 to 20. |
| `Q` | Yes | `String` | String | This describes the "sharpness" of the filter. A lower value means a smoother curve. A number in the range 0.1 to 50. |
| `Section` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 6 (`Integer`) | Each audio equalizer has 6 adjustable filter sections. Each section is a second-order filter, which can be configured to modify the signal passing through the selected equalizer. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.17 xCommand Audio LocalInput Add

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalInput.Add`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Create a virtual local input, and generate an identifier for it (InputId). A local input is associated with a set of input connectors, and you can specify the following: a name for the local input, how to mix the signals from the associated input connectors, the use of Automatic Gain Control (AGC) and mute, whether to make a mono or stereo signal, and whether to use direct mode to bypass input processing. The maximum number of local input modules is 8. You get an error message if you exceed the limit. This command is used by the Audio Console. If you don't use Audio Console, note that you must create a macro to make the audio chain definitions persistent over a reboot. Codec EQ: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalInput.Add`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio LocalInput Add [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.LocalInput.Add.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AGC` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: Adjusts the gain continuously to maintain a constant sound level (default). Off: No automatic gain control. |
| `Channels` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 2 (`Integer`) | 1: Mixes the input signals into a mono signal (default). 2: Mixes the input signals into a stereo signal. |
| `Direct` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: Bypass input processing such as acoustic echo cancellation and noise reduction, regardless of the configuration for each connected input connector. Bypassing the input processing reduces the audio input delay, which is useful when doing local sound reinforcement. Off: All regular input processing is performed, according to the configuration of each connector (default). |
| `InputId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | A unique identifier for the local input. If you don't specify an InputID, the device will automatically create one for you. We recommend that you specify the InputId yourself in case you must refer to the local input at a later stage. |
| `MixerMode` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Auto: If one input signal is dominating, the signal on the other connectors are attenuated with 20 dB each. Fixed: The input signals all have the same weight, and consequently they are mixed together with equal gains (default). GainShared: If one or some of the input signals dominate, the rest of the input signals are attenuated by a few dB so that the total gain of the mixed signal remains the same all the time. Auto and GainShared are intended for the microphone inputs; Fixed is recommended for Line and HDMI inputs. |
| `Mute` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: Mutes the mix of input signals (default). Off: No muting. |
| `Name` | No | `String` | String | Choose a name that describes the local input. If you don't specify a name, the string will be empty. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.18 xCommand Audio LocalInput AddConnector

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalInput.AddConnector`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Attach an input connector to the local input given by the input ID. You must specify both the connector's type and number (ConnectorType, ConnectorId) to uniquely identify the connector. A connector can only be attached to one local input. Run xStatus Audio Input LocalInput to get an overview of all local inputs. This command is used by the Audio Console. If you don't use Audio Console, note that you must create a macro to make the audio chain definitions persistent over a reboot. Codec EQ: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalInput.AddConnector`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio LocalInput AddConnector [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.LocalInput.AddConnector.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ConnectorId` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 8 (`Integer`) | Select a connector. The connectors' numbers are printed on the codec connector panel. |
| `ConnectorType` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Select the type of the physical connector, device, or session to receive audio from. ARC: The ARC (Audio Return Channel) on the corresponding HDMI output. AirPlay: An active AirPlay session. Ethernet: An audio device (Cisco Table Microphone Pro / Cisco Microphone Array) on the codec's internal network. HDMI: An HDMI input. Microphone: An analog microphone input. USBInterface: A microphone or audio interface connected to a USB connector. WebView: The embedded web browser. |
| `InputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the local input. It was generated when the local input was created with the xCommand Audio LocalInput Add command. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.32 xCommand Audio LocalInput Update

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalInput.Update`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Update the settings of the local input given by the input ID. Run xStatus Audio Input LocalInput to get an overview of all local inputs. This command is used by the Audio Console. If you don't use Audio Console, note that you must create a macro to make the audio chain definitions persistent over a reboot. Codec EQ: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalInput.Update`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio LocalInput Update [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.LocalInput.Update.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AGC` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: Adjust the gain continuously to maintain a constant sound level). Off: No automatic gain control. |
| `Channels` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 2 (`Integer`) | 1: Mix the input signals into a mono signal. 2: Mix the input signals into a stereo signal. |
| `Direct` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: Bypass input processing such as acoustic echo cancellation and noise reduction, regardless of the configuration for each connected input connector. Bypassing the input processing reduces the audio input delay, which is useful when doing local sound reinforcement. Off: All regular input processing is performed, according to the configuration of each connector. |
| `InputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier for the local input. It was generated when the local input was created with the xCommand Audio LocalInput Add command. |
| `MixerMode` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Auto: If one input signal is dominating, the signal on the other connectors are attenuated with 20 dB each. Fixed: The input signals all have the same weight, and consequently they are mixed together with equal gains. GainShared: If one or some of the input signals dominate, the rest of the input signals are attenuated by a few dB so that the total gain of the mixed signal remains the same all the time. Auto and GainShared are intended for the microphones; Fixed is recommended for Line and HDMI inputs. |
| `Mute` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: Mutes the mix of input signals. Off: No muting. |
| `Name` | No | `String` | String | Choose a name that describes the local input. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.33 xCommand Audio LocalOutput Add

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.Add`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Create a virtual local output and generate an identifier for it (OutputId). A local output is a mix of local inputs and the remote input signals. Use the xCommand Audio LocalOutput ConnectInput command to specify which local inputs to include. The remote input signal (from far-end) is by default automatically added to this local output when in a call.Use the AutoconnectRemote parameter if you want to override the default behavior. A local output is associated with a set of output connectors, which all receive the same signal. The maximum number of local output modules is 6. You get an error message if you exceed the limit. This command is used by the Audio Console. If you don't use Audio Console, note that you must create a macro to make the audio chain definitions persistent over a reboot. Codec EQ: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.Add`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio LocalOutput Add [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.LocalOutput.Add.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AutoconnectRemote` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: The remote input signal is automatically added to the local output when in a call. Off: The remote input signal is not added to the local output. |
| `Channels` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 2 (`Integer`) | 1: Mix the local and remote input signals into a mono signal. 2: Mix the local and remote input signals into a stereo signal. |
| `Loudspeaker` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: Choose On if at least one of the associated connectors are connected to a loudspeaker. This is important because it tells the echo canceler to use this signal as a reference signal. Off: Choose Off if no loudspeaker is connected to the associated connectors. Note that only one of the local outputs should have a loudspeaker connected. |
| `Name` | No | `String` | String | Choose a name that describes the local output. |
| `OutputId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | A unique identifier for the local output. If you don't specify an OutputId, the device will automatically create one for you. We recommend that you specify the OutputId yourself in case you must refer to the output module at a later stage. |
| `VolumeControlled` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: The volume will change according to the level set with the volume controls on the user interface, or with the xCommand Audio Volume commands. If Loudspeaker is On, VolumeControlled is forced to On no matter what you specify here. Off: The volume is neither influenced by the volume controls on the user interface, nor the xCommand Audio Volume commands. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.34 xCommand Audio LocalOutput AddConnector

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.AddConnector`

A connector can only be attached to one local output. Run xStatus Audio Output LocalOutput to get an overview of all local outputs. This command is used by the Audio Console. | `ConnectorType` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Select the type of the physical connector, device, or session to deliver audio to. ARC: The ARC (Audio Return Channel) on the corresponding HDMI input. Ethernet: The AEC reference signal to a digital microphone (Cisco Table Microphone Pro / Cisco Microphone Array). HDMI: An HDMI output. Line: An analog audio line output. USBInterface: An audio interface connected to a USB connector. WebView: The embedded web browser. In WebRTC sessions, WebView [1] is main audio, while WebView [2] is presentation audio. |
| `OutputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the local output. It was generated when the local output was created with the xCommand Audio LocalOutput Add command. |

A connector can only be attached to one local output. Run xStatus Audio Output LocalOutput to get an overview of all local outputs. This command is used by the Audio Console. If you don't use Audio Console, note that you must create a macro to make the audio chain definitions persistent over a reboot. Codec EQ: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.AddConnector`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio LocalOutput AddConnector [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.LocalOutput.AddConnector.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ConnectorId` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 8 (`Integer`) | Select a connector. The connectors' numbers are printed on the codec connector panel. |
| `ConnectorType` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Select the type of the physical connector, device, or session to deliver audio to. ARC: The ARC (Audio Return Channel) on the corresponding HDMI input. Ethernet: An audio device on the codec's internal network. Ethernet [1] is for the AEC reference signal to a digital microphone (Cisco Table Microphone Pro / Cisco Microphone Array). For Room Panorama, Ethernet [2] is for audio to the DNAM IV amplifier. HDMI: An HDMI output. InternalSpeaker: The device's internal speakers. Line: An analog audio line output. USBInterface: An audio interface connected to a USB connector. WebView: The embedded web browser. In WebRTC sessions, WebView [1] is main audio, while WebView [2] is presentation audio. |
| `OutputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the local output. It was generated when the local output was created with the xCommand Audio LocalOutput Add command. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.39 xCommand Audio LocalOutput ConnectInput

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.ConnectInput`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Connect a local or remote input to a local output by giving their IDs as parameters. A local input can be connected to any number of local outputs. Likewise, any number of local inputs can be connected to each local output. Note that the remote input signal (from far-end) is automatically added to all local outputs when a call is made, and automatically disconnected when the call is ended. Run xStatus Audio Output LocalOutput to get an overview of all local outputs, xStatus Audio Input LocalInput to get an overview of all local inputs, and xStatus Audio Input RemoteInput to see the remote input details. This command is used by the Audio Console. If you don't use Audio Console, note that you must create a macro to make the audio chain definitions persistent over a reboot. Codec EQ: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.ConnectInput`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio LocalOutput ConnectInput [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.LocalOutput.ConnectInput.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `InputGain` | No | `Integer` | -54 to 15 (`Integer`) | Set the gain on the input signal. The gain can also be negative (attenuation). The value -54 dB equals Off. |
| `InputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the local or remote input. The local input's ID was generated when the local input was created with the xCommand Audio LocalInput Add command. The remote input's ID was generated automatically when the call was made. |
| `OutputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the local output. It was generated when the local output was created with the xCommand Audio LocalOutput Add command. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.45 xCommand Audio LocalOutput Ethernet Register

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.Ethernet.Register`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Use this command to configure and register an outgoing audio stream to a logical Ethernet audio output connector. This is required for transmission of audio over AES67 from the video device. Once registered, the stream is announced using SAP every 30 seconds on the address set in the Audio Ethernet SAPDiscovery Address setting. To see currently active streams and their parameters, check the Audio Output Connectors Ethernet status.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.Ethernet.Register`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio LocalOutput Ethernet Register [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.LocalOutput.Ethernet.Register.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Channels` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 2 (`Integer`) | The number of channels to transmit in the stream. |
| `ConnectorId` | No | `Integer` | 2 to 4 (`Integer`) | The identifier of the logical Ethernet output connector. If not specified, the first available number is used. Note that Ethernet 1 is a reserved connector. |
| `MediaIP` | Yes | `String` | String | This is the IP address to use for the audio transmission. It must be a valid multicast address. Note that some devices have a specified range of multicast addresses they consider valid. |
| `StreamName` | Yes | `String` | String | A unique name for the audio stream. This name will be visible to other AES67 devices on the network. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.55 xCommand Audio LocalOutput Update

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.Update`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Update the settings of the local output given by the output ID. Run xStatus Audio Output LocalOutput to get an overview of all local outputs. This command is used by the Audio Console. If you don't use Audio Console, note that you must create a macro to make the audio chain definitions persistent over a reboot. Codec EQ: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.Update`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio LocalOutput Update [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.LocalOutput.Update.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AutoconnectRemote` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: The remote input signal is automatically added to the local output when in a call. Off: The remote input signal is not added to the local output. |
| `Channels` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 2 (`Integer`) | 1: Mix the local and remote input signals into a mono signal. 2: Mix the local and remote input signals into a stereo signal. |
| `Loudspeaker` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: Choose On if at least one of the associated connectors are connected to a loudspeaker. This is important because it tells the echo canceler to use this signal as a reference signal. Off: Choose Off if no loudspeaker is connected to the associated connectors. Note that only one of the local outputs should have a loudspeaker connected. |
| `Name` | No | `String` | String | Choose a name that describes the local output. |
| `OutputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the local output. It was generated when the local output was created with the xCommand Audio LocalOutput Add command. |
| `VolumeControlled` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: The volume will change according to the level set by the volume controls on the user interface, or the xCommand Audio Volume commands. If Loudspeaker is On, VolumeControlled is forced to On no matter what you specify here. Off: The volume is neither influenced by the volume controls on the user interface, nor the xCommand Audio Volume commands. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.56 xCommand Audio LocalOutput UpdateInputGain

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.UpdateInputGain`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Update the gain of a local or remote input that is connected to a local output. Note that the remote input signal (from far-end) is automatically added to all local outputs when a call is made, and automatically disconnected when the call is ended. Run xStatus Audio Output LocalOutput to get an overview of all local outputs, xStatus Audio Input LocalInput to get an overview of all local inputs, and xStatus Audio Input RemoteInput to see the remote input details. This command is used by the Audio Console. If you don't use Audio Console, note that you must create a macro to make the audio chain definitions persistent over a reboot. Codec EQ: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.LocalOutput.UpdateInputGain`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio LocalOutput UpdateInputGain [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.LocalOutput.UpdateInputGain.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `InputGain` | No | `Integer` | -54 to 15 (`Integer`) | Set the gain on the input signal. The gain can also be negative (attenuation). The value -54 dB equals Off. |
| `InputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the local or remote input. The local input's ID was generated when the local input was created with the xCommand Audio LocalInput Add command. The remote input's ID was generated automatically when the call was made. |
| `OutputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the local output. It was generated when the local output was created with the xCommand Audio LocalOutput Add command. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.70 xCommand Audio RemoteOutput ConnectInput

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.RemoteOutput.ConnectInput`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Connect an input to a remote output by giving their IDs as parameters. An input can be connected to any number of remote output gates, and any number of inputs can be connected to one remote output gate. Note that all local inputs are automatically added to all remote output gates when a call is made, and automatically disconnected when the call is ended. Run xStatus Audio Input LocalInput to get an overview of all local inputs. This command is mainly intended for internal use by the Audio Console. It is only applicable during a call. Codec EQ: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.RemoteOutput.ConnectInput`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio RemoteOutput ConnectInput [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.RemoteOutput.ConnectInput.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `InputGain` | No | `Integer` | -54 to 15 (`Integer`) | Set the gain on the input signal. The gain can also be negative (attenuation). The value -54 dB equals Off. |
| `InputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the input. It was either generated when the input was created with the xCommand Audio Local Input Add command, or when the call was set up (remote input). |
| `OutputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the remote output. It was automatically generated when the call was made. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Disconnect an input from a remote output by giving their IDs as parameters. Note that the remote output is automatically removed when the call has ended. Run xStatus Audio Output RemoteOutput to get an overview of the remote outputs, and xStatus Audio Input LocalInput to get an overview of all local inputs. | Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `InputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the input. It was either generated when the input was created with the xCommand Audio Local Input Add command, or when the call was set up (remote input). |
| `OutputId` | Yes | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique identifier of the remote output. It was automatically generated when the call was made. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.SoundsAndAlerts.Ringtone.Stop.(...)`

### 1.82 xCommand Audio SpeakerCheck

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.SpeakerCheck`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Runs a test that you can use to check that all the internal speakers are connected correctly. A test tone will be emitted from each speaker in sequence, from left to right. If the speakers don't play in correct order, reconnect the loudspeaker cables to obtain the correct sequence. All speakers are part of the test sequence, and you must be in the same room as the device to verify that the test sequence plays correctly. The device uses the connected microphones to listen for the test signal, and the result of the test is returned in the API.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.SpeakerCheck`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio SpeakerCheck [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.SpeakerCheck.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `MeasurementLength` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 5 (`Integer`) | Test signal duration for each speaker in seconds. |
| `Volume` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 30 (`Integer`) | Test signal level. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.83 xCommand Audio Volume Decrease

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.Volume.Decrease`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Decrease the volume on the video device. By default, the volume is decreased by 5 steps (each step is 0.5 dB). Use the Steps parameter if you want to override the default behavior. Note that Desk series, Board Pro, Board Pro G2, Room Bar, Room Bar Pro, Room Kit, Room Kit Mini, and Room 55 have several audio units: built-in loudspeakers, headsets, and handset. This command affects only one unit at a time. You can use the optional Device parameter to specify which audio unit to address. The most recently selected unit is chosen if you don't specify a unit (see xStatus Audio SelectedDevice). Also refer to xCommand Audio Select.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.Volume.Decrease`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio Volume Decrease [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.Volume.Decrease.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Steps` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 10 (`Integer`) | Choose the number of steps to decrease the volume with. One step is 0.5 dB. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.102 xCommand Audio VuMeter Start

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Audio.VuMeter.Start`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Start a VU meter to measure the audio signal level on the specified connector. You must specify both the connector's type and number (ConnectorType, ConnectorId) to uniquely identify the connector and behavior. The VU meter measures the input level for frequencies below 20 kHz. You can monitor the measured signal levels on the device's local web interface (Settings > Audio and Video), or you can use the xFeedback and xEvents commands.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Audio.VuMeter.Start`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Audio VuMeter Start [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Audio.VuMeter.Start.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ConnectorId` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 1 (`Integer`) |  |
| `ConnectorType` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal |  |
| `IncludePairingQuality` | No | `Literal` | Literal | The device can measure the pairing quality (value 0 to 100). With no other ultrasound sources in the same room this value will be high, but if there are other ultrasound sources in the same room the value will be low. If using the device's local web interface to monitor the signal levels, you must check Show Pairing Rate to see the pairing quality. |
| `IntervalMs` | No | `Integer` | 10 to 1000 (`Integer`) | Specifies the update interval in milliseconds of the VuMeter values. The values can be specified in 10 ms steps. |
| `Source` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Determines whether the VU meter should measure the audio signal level before or after acoustic echo cancellation processing (AEC). | `ConnectorType` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Select Microphone for analaog microphones and USBMicrophone for USB microphones. |

You can use the Bluetooth Streaming commands to control audio streaming from a device (for example, mobile phone or laptop) that is connected to the video device via Bluetooth. Use this command to skip to the next audio track on the connected device. Prerequisite: Turn on Bluetooth on the video device, and for first-time pairing, also make it discoverable to other devices. This is done from the Settings panel on the video device's user interface. Then initiate a connection to the video device from the Bluetooth settings panel on the connected device.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Bluetooth.Streaming.Next`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Bluetooth Streaming Next [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Bluetooth.Streaming.Next.(...)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.128 xCommand Bookings List

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Bookings.List`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

List the stored bookings for the device. The list of booking details is received from the management system. All parameters are optional and can be used to limit the search result. If no parameters are set, past, present and future bookings are all listed. To avoid listing bookings from yesterday and before, use DayOffset = 0.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Bookings.List`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Bookings List [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Bookings.List.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AccountType` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Shows only the specified account’s type. This is mainly useful for a hot desk device, which may have a shared (room) or personal account. |
| `DayOffset` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 365 (`Integer`) | Which day to start the search from (today: 0, tomorrow: 1, …). |
| `Days` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 365 (`Integer`) | Number of days to retrieve bookings from. |
| `Limit` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 65534 (`Integer`) | Max number of bookings to list. |
| `Offset` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | Offset number of bookings for this search. |
| `ScheduleType` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Shows either ongoing meetings, or upcoming meetings. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.130 xCommand Bookings Put

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Bookings.Put`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This API has special terms and conditions, please refer to the "About the API – Terms and Conditions" section in the API guide. Replaces the list of stored bookings. This is a multiline command, with details of the stored bookings as payload. The meeting information is provided in JSON format. For example: {  "Bookings": [   {    "Id": "1",    "Number": "number@example.com",    "Organizer": {     "Name": "John Smith"    },    "Protocol": "WebRTC",    "MeetingPlatform": "MicrosoftTeams",    "Time": {     "Duration": 60,     "EndTimeBuffer": 50,     "StartTime": "2024-06-04T08:40:42.300000000Z"    },    "Title": "Booking Title"   }  ] }  The JSON structure supports the following fields: { { "Id", "id" }, { "MeetingId", "MyMeeting" }, { "Agenda", "MyAgenda" }, { "Title", "MyBookingTitle" }, { "Privacy", "Private/Public" }, { "Protocol", "SIP/H323/ISDN/IP/Spark/WebRTC/None" }, { "MeetingPlatform", "GoogleMeet/MicrosoftTeams/Zoom/Webex/Other/None" }, { "MetaInfo", "...." }, { "Time", {    { "StartTime", "2020-06-10T09:31:42Z"},    { "Duration", 60 },    { "StartTimeBuffer", 300 },    { "EndTimeBuffer", 0 }, }}, { "Organizer", {    { "Name", "John Smith" },    { "Email", "johnsmith@example.com" },    { "Id", "" }, }}, { "Number", "number@example.com" }, { "CallType", "Audio/Video" }, { "Encryption", "On/Off" } }  The required fields are: Id, Title, Number, Protocol, Organizer/Name, Time/StartTime, and Time/Duration. StartTime: The meeting start time in UTC/Zulu time. Duration: The meeting duration in minutes. StartTimeBuffer: The number of seconds before the meeting start time that people can join the meeting. EndTimeBuffer: The number of seconds longer than the scheduled hours (StartTime + Duration) that the meeting can last. Number: The the number that will be dialed. MeetingPlatform: The service that hosts the meeting. This is used to show a visual indication (for example, Microsoft Teams icon) in the user interface. We support only Microsoft Teams and Google Meet if the Protocol is WebRTC; for other protocols we support all the available meeting platform options.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Bookings.Put`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Bookings Put [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Bookings.Put.(...)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.135 xCommand Call FarEndControl Camera Move

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Call.FarEndControl.Camera.Move`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Move the far end camera (the remote camera). This command can be issued from a device that is participating in a call and can be used to control the camera of another device within the same call. Speakertrack must be disabled on the far end camera. Once the Move command is issued, the far end camera will continue to move in the specified direction until the stop command (ref: xCommand FarEndControl Camera Stop) is issued. For on-premises and CMS, this command accesses the camera of the active speaker. For cloud, this command accesses the camera of the specified participant. An additional constraint is that you cannot control the camera of a cloud-based personal mode device. This is for privacy reasons (i.e., home office).

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Call.FarEndControl.Camera.Move`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Call FarEndControl Camera Move [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Call.FarEndControl.Camera.Move.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The CallId is a unique number used to address an active call. You can get the callId during the call, by running xStatus Call from one of the devices participating in the call. |
| `ParticipantId` | No | `String` | String | (Cloud only) The ParticipantId is a unique number used to address a participant in a call. ParticipantId is ignored for on-premises or CMS, as these always control the camera of the active speaker. The ParticipantId is not needed if there are only 2 participants in a call, as it is implied. To see the ParticipantIds for participants in a call, you can run the xCommand Conference ParticipantList Search. Scan the list for the participant and use the subfield, "ParticipantId". During the call, you can  run the xCommand Call FarEndControl RequestCapabilities to check if Far End Camera Control is supported. |
| `Value` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Select the action for how to move the camera. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.136 xCommand Call FarEndControl Camera Stop

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Call.FarEndControl.Camera.Stop`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Stop the far end camera after the xCommand FarEndControl Camera Move has been issued. This command can be issued from a device that is participating in a call and can be used to control the camera of another device within the same call. Speakertrack must be disabled on the far end camera. For on-premises and CMS, this command accesses the camera of the active speaker. This is for privacy reasons (i.e., home office).

- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Call FarEndControl Camera Stop [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Call.FarEndControl.Camera.Stop.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The CallId is a unique number used to address an active call. You can get the callId during the call, by running xStatus Call from one of the devices participating in the call. |
| `ParticipantId` | No | `String` | String | (Cloud only) The ParticipantId is a unique number used to address a participant in a call. ParticipantId is ignored for on-premises or CMS, as these always control the camera of the active speaker. The ParticipantId is not needed if there are only 2 participants in a call, as it is implied. To see the ParticipantIds for participants in a call, you can run the xCommand Conference ParticipantList Search. Scan the list for the participant and use the subfield, "ParticipantId". During the call, you can  run the xCommand Call FarEndControl RequestCapabilities to check if Far End Camera Control is supported. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.137 xCommand Call FarEndControl RequestCapabilities

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Call.FarEndControl.RequestCapabilities`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Send a request to find out what capabilities a far end camera has for remote control. This command can be issued from a device that is participating in a call and can be used to control the camera of another device within the same call. For on-premises and CMS, this command accesses the camera of the active speaker. For cloud, this command accesses the camera of the specified participant. An additional constraint is that you cannot control the camera of a cloud-based personal mode device. This is for privacy reasons (e.g.., home office).

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Call.FarEndControl.RequestCapabilities`

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The CallId is a unique number used to address an active call. You can get the callId during the call, by running xStatus Call from one of the devices participating in the call. |
| `ParticipantId` | No | `String` | String | (Cloud only) The ParticipantId is a unique number used to address a participant in a call. ParticipantId is ignored for on-premises or CMS, as these always control the camera of the active speaker. The ParticipantId is not needed if there are only 2 participants in a call, as it is implied. To see the ParticipantIds for participants in a call, you can run the xCommand Conference ParticipantList Search. Scan the list for the participant and use the subfield, "ParticipantId". During the call, you can  run the xCommand Call FarEndControl RequestCapabilities to check if Far End Camera Control is supported. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.138 xCommand Call FarEndControl RoomPreset Activate

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Call.FarEndControl.RoomPreset.Activate`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

While in a call, this command is used to activate a preset on the far end device. The preset covers the far end device's camera positions and input video switcher settings. The preset must be stored on the far end device beforehand, either by using the xCommand Preset Store command locally on the far end device, or by using the xCommand FarEndControl Preset Store command from a remote device. Note: The far end device's xConfiguration Conference FarEndControl Mode setting must be switched On for the FarEndControl commands to work.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Call.FarEndControl.RoomPreset.Activate`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Call FarEndControl RoomPreset Activate [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Call.FarEndControl.RoomPreset.Activate.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The CallId is required to identify the far end device only when in a Multipoint call. The CallId is returned when issuing the xCommand Dial command. During a call you can run the xStatus Call command to see the CallId. |
| `ParticipantId` | No | `String` | String | (Cloud only) The ParticipantId is a unique number used to address a participant in a call. ParticipantId is ignored for on-premises or CMS, as these always control the camera of the active speaker. The ParticipantId is not needed if there are only 2 participants in a call, as it is implied. To see the ParticipantIds for participants in a call, you can run the xCommand Conference ParticipantList Search. Scan the list for the participant and use the subfield, "ParticipantId". During the call, you can  run the xCommand Call FarEndControl RequestCapabilities to check if Far End Camera Control is supported. |
| `PresetId` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 15 (`Integer`) | The ID of the preset that is stored on the far end device. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.157 xCommand Camera InstallationTilt Ramp

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Camera.InstallationTilt.Ramp`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Start to move the camera module (physically) in the specified direction. The camera motor moves the camera module in the given direction at slow speed until a new command, either changing the direction or stopping the movement, is issued. The camera movement always stops when reaching the end of its range. The main purpose of this command is to be able to readjust the physical camera tilt after the device is installed for the first time. For ordinary camera view pan-tilt-zoom (digital), use the Camera Ramp command.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Camera.InstallationTilt.Ramp`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Camera InstallationTilt Ramp [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Camera.InstallationTilt.Ramp.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Tilt` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Start or stop the camera tilt motor which moves the camera module up or down. Down: Start tilting the camera module downward. Up: Start tilting the camera module upward. Stop: Stop tilting the camera module. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.159 xCommand Camera PositionSet

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Camera.PositionSet`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the camera position. The value range for the different parameters (pan, tilt, zoom, roll) depends on the camera type. If you enter a value that isn't within the supported range for your camera, the closest allowed value will be applied. Also, if the combination of the pan, tilt, zoom, and roll values is not possible, the camera automatically adjusts the values to a valid combination. Refer to the Cameras Camera [n] Position Pan/Tilt/Zoom/Roll statuses to see the actual values applied.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Camera.PositionSet`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Camera PositionSet [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Camera.PositionSet.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CameraId` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 1 (`Integer`) | The ID of the camera preset you want to reset. |
| `Focus` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65535 (`Integer`) | Focus the camera near or far. |
| `Lens` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Some cameras have more than one lens. This parameter selects which lens to set the position for. |
| `Pan` | No | `Integer` | -17000 to 17000 (`Integer`) | Move the camera to the left or right. The unit is 1/100 degree, that is 100 corresponds to 1 degree. A positive value moves the camera to the left, and a negative value moves the camera to the right. Left and right refers to when looking from the back of the camera out into the room. This is the opposite of what is seen when looking at the camera lens from the room. |
| `Tilt` | No | `Integer` | -9000 to 9000 (`Integer`) | Move the camera up or down. The unit is 1/100 degree, that is 100 corresponds to 1 degree. A positive value tilts the camera up, and a negative value tilts the camera down. |
| `Zoom` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 12000 (`Integer`) | Zoom in or out. The unit is HFOV (horizontal field of view) in 1/100 degree, that is 100 corresponds to 1 degree. A low value corresponds to maximum zoom and the largest value corresponds to minimum zoom (full wide). |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.166 xCommand Camera Preset ActivateDefaultPosition

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Camera.Preset.ActivateDefaultPosition`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Sets the cameras to their default position, if one is defined. The default position is defined by xCommand Camera Preset Store or by xCommand Camera Preset Edit. Only one default position can be defined per camera. This command has no effect on speaker tracking. If speaker tracking is on, it will continue from the preset position.

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CameraId` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 1 (`Integer`) | The ID of the camera preset you want to activate. If CameraId is not specified, all cameras will be set in their respective default position, if one is defined. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.173 xCommand Camera Preset Store

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Camera.Preset.Store`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Store the current position (pan and tilt), zoom and focus of the chosen camera. The camera is identified by the CameraId parameter. Note that the xCommand Camera Preset commands applies to an individual camera. The xCommand Camera Preset commands are useful when you want to handle multiple camera positions individually per camera, rather than working with complete sets of camera positions. The individual camera presets are not available for far end control.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Camera.Preset.Store`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Camera Preset Store [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Camera.Preset.Store.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CameraId` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 1 (`Integer`) | Select the camera for which to store the preset position. |
| `DefaultPosition` | No | `Literal` | Literal |  |
| `ListPosition` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 35 (`Integer`) | The new camera preset's position in the list returned by the xCommand Camera Preset List command. |
| `Name` | No | `String` | String | The name of the new camera preset. It will be used in the list returned by the xCommand Camera Preset List command. |
| `PresetId` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 35 (`Integer`) | The ID of this camera preset. If not set explicitly, the codec will assign a preset ID automatically. |
| `TakeSnapshot` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Allow or disallow snapshot of the preview. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.175 xCommand Camera Ramp

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Camera.Ramp`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Move the camera in a specified direction. The camera moves at specified speed until a stop command is issued. In a daisy chain, you must know the CameraId for the camera you want to address. Be aware that pan and tilt can be operated simultaneously, but no other combinations. In the latter case only the first operation specified is executed. For example, if you try to run both zoom and pan at the same time, only zoom is executed. NOTE: You must run a stop command to stop the camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Camera.Ramp`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Camera Ramp [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Camera.Ramp.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CameraId` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 1 (`Integer`) | Select the camera. |
| `Focus` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Focus the camera Far or Near, followed by Stop. |
| `Pan` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Move the camera to the Left or Right, followed by Stop. |
| `PanSpeed` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 24 (`Integer`) | Set the pan speed. |
| `Tilt` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Move the camera Up or Down, followed by Stop. |
| `TiltSpeed` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 24 (`Integer`) | Set the tilt speed. |
| `Zoom` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Zoom the camera In or Out, followed by Stop. |
| `ZoomSpeed` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 15 (`Integer`) | Set the zoom speed. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.176 xCommand Camera Ramp

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Camera.Ramp`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Move the camera in a specified direction. The camera moves at specified speed until a stop command is issued. In a daisy chain, you must know the CameraId for the camera you want to address. Be aware that pan and tilt can be operated simultaneously, but no other combinations. In the latter case only the first operation specified is executed. For example, if you try to run both zoom and pan at the same time, only zoom is executed. NOTE: You must run a stop command to stop the camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Camera.Ramp`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Camera Ramp [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Camera.Ramp.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CameraId` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 15 (`Integer`) | Select the camera. |
| `Focus` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Focus the camera Far or Near, followed by Stop. |
| `Pan` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Move the camera to the Left or Right, followed by Stop. |
| `PanSpeed` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 24 (`Integer`) | Set the pan speed. |
| `Tilt` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Move the camera Up or Down, followed by Stop. |
| `TiltSpeed` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 24 (`Integer`) | Set the tilt speed. |
| `Zoom` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Zoom the camera In or Out, followed by Stop. |
| `ZoomSpeed` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 15 (`Integer`) | Set the zoom speed. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.185 xCommand Cameras Background ForegroundParameters Set

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Cameras.Background.ForegroundParameters.Set`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Used in Immersive Share mode. Set the size, position, and opacity of the image in the foreground. You can also set the composition of the shared pictures to show the full camera video in either the foreground or background. The command is only relevant if you are using the HDMI or USB-C input as a virtual background for your self-view image.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Cameras.Background.ForegroundParameters.Set`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Cameras Background ForegroundParameters Set [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Cameras.Background.ForegroundParameters.Set.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Composition` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Blend: Render the foreground part of the camera input on top of the PC input. This is the typical view of a floating person, whose background is transparent, placed over the presentation video. The PC input is rendered in full screen and the X, Y, Scale parameters control the position of the camera input. CameraPip: Render the camera input as Picture-In-Picture on top of the PC input. This will show the entire camera image, including the background, as a rectangle placed over the presentation video. The PC input is rendered in full screen and the X, Y, Scale parameters control the position of the camera input. VideoPip: Render the PC input as Picture-In-Picture on top of the camera input. This will show the presentation video in a rectangle that is placed over the full camera view, including background. The camera input is rendered in full screen and the X, Y, Scale parameters control the position of the PC input. |
| `Opacity` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 100 (`Integer`) | The opacity of the foreground picture. 100 means that the picture is opaque, the lower the value the more you can see of the background through the picture, and 0 means that you will only see the background. |
| `Scale` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 100 (`Integer`) | The size of the foreground picture relative to the background (in percent). 100 is full size, 1 is no self-view picture. |
| `X` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 10000 (`Integer`) | The position (horizontally) of the center of the foreground picture. 0 is the left edge, 5000 is center, and 10000 is the right edge. |
| `Y` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 10000 (`Integer`) | The position (vertically) of the center of the foreground picture. 0 is the top edge, 5000 is center, and 10000 is the bottom edge. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.193 xCommand Cameras PresenterTrack Set

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Cameras.PresenterTrack.Set`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the presenter tracking mode. This command applies only when using the device with a PTZ 4K or Precision 60 camera for presenter tracking. The command takes effect only if the PresenterTrack feature is enabled, refer to the Cameras PresenterTrack Enabled setting.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Cameras.PresenterTrack.Set`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Cameras PresenterTrack Set [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Cameras.PresenterTrack.Set.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Mode` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Off: Turn off presenter tracking. Follow: Turn on presenter tracking. This is the default mode when the feature is activated from the user interface. Presenter tracking is automatically turned off when camera moves to a different preset, when another camera is selected, or when standby is activated. Diagnostic: Turn on diagnostic mode in order to troubleshoot presenter tracking, or to see exactly what happens on the device screen. In diagnostics mode there are several activities on the screen. The screen will show the overview image, and the rectangles/squares listed below will be visible:   * RED: The trigger zone.   * LIGHT BLUE: The cropped image of the presenter. Visible only when a head is being tracked.   * GREEN: Indicates that a head is detected and that it is tracked.   * GREEN BLINKING FILLED: Indicates a positive head detection. If the tracked individual does not get a valid head-read the square becomes red.   * RED BLINKING FILLED: Indicates a false head detection. After some seconds the tracking stops.   * BLUE: A head is detected, but the head is not tracked. Background: This setting is used by the codec's internal scripts. Turns on presenter tracking with no cropping of the image. Setup: This setting is used by the codec's web interface to show the trigger zone on the device screen when setting up the PresenterTrack feature. Persistent: This setting is used by the codec's internal scripts. Turns on presenter tracking in persistent mode. Persitent mode is automatically turned off when camera moves to a different preset. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.203 xCommand Cameras SpeakerTrack Diagnostics Start

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Cameras.SpeakerTrack.Diagnostics.Start`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Starts diagnostics on the camera's tracking, so that you can see which speakers, groups, and frames are detected.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Cameras.SpeakerTrack.Diagnostics.Start`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Cameras SpeakerTrack Diagnostics Start [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Cameras.SpeakerTrack.Diagnostics.Start.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Tracking` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: Displays diagnostics from both cameras simultaneously. In this mode the tracking is determined by who is talking in the room identical to SpeakerTrack's standard behavior. Off: Displays diagnostics from one camera at a time. Diagnostics is switched from one camera to the other in 15 seconds intervals, and camera related diagnostics are shown for the active camera. Both cameras stay in full wide position. Use Tracking: Off when you wish to see the tracking diagnostics from one camera at a time. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.207 xCommand Cameras SpeakerTrack Set

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Cameras.SpeakerTrack.Set`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This command allows you to select from the various available camera modes.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Cameras.SpeakerTrack.Set`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Cameras SpeakerTrack Set [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Cameras.SpeakerTrack.Set.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Behavior` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Manual: The camera is controlled manually. The pan-tilt-zoom values are kept unchanged when leaving a call. BestOverview: The camera will adjust automatically so you are always in the center of the frame. The default framing mode is Best overview. Closeup: The camera will follow the person speaking. Current: The framing mode is kept unchanged when leaving a call. Dynamic: The camera will analyze the room and dynamically pick the most suitable camera mode. Frames: The camera will zoom and show people individually or in smaller groups. GroupAndSpeaker: Remote participants will see two views at the same time: a group overview and a close-up of the active speaker. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.224 xCommand Conference AdmitAll

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Conference.AdmitAll`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Lets into the call or meeting all participants who are waiting in the virtual lobby. Available for Hosts and Cohosts of Webex meetings. The device must either be registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for Devices. Participants waiting to be admitted have the status "waiting" in the result from the Conference ParticipantList Search command (*r ParticipantListSearchResult Participant [n] Status = "waiting").

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Conference.AdmitAll`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Conference AdmitAll [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Conference.AdmitAll.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The CallId is a unique number used to address an active call. The CallId is returned when the Dial or Webex Join commands are run. During the call you can run xStatus Call to see the CallId. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.225 xCommand Conference Call AuthenticationResponse

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Conference.Call.AuthenticationResponse`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This command is only available for Webex registered devices. The command gives a response to an authentication request based on the Conference Call[n] AuthenticationRequest status.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Conference.Call.AuthenticationResponse`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Conference Call AuthenticationResponse [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Conference.Call.AuthenticationResponse.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | Unique identifier of the call. During a call you can run the xStatus Call command to see the CallId. |
| `ParticipantRole` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Guest: Join as guest. Guests have no special privileges. User this also Webex Webinar attendees. Host: Join as host. The host has privileges that allow them to manage the meeting. Panelist: Join as panelist. In Webex Webinars, panelists can participate in the presentation. |
| `Pin` | No | `String` | String | PIN code. The PIN must be entered with a trailing '#'. A PIN code must be provided if joining as host, panelist, or as guest, when the Conference Call[n] AuthenticationRequest status indicates that a PIN code is required for that role. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.226 xCommand Conference DoNotDisturb Activate

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Conference.DoNotDisturb.Activate`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This command switches on the Do Not Disturb mode, and the Timeout parameter allows you to control when it is switched off again. When Do Not Disturb is switched on, all incoming calls are rejected and registered as missed calls. The calling side receives a busy signal.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Conference.DoNotDisturb.Activate`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Conference DoNotDisturb Activate [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Conference.DoNotDisturb.Activate.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Timeout` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 20160 (`Integer`) | Set the number of minutes before Do Not Disturb is switched off. If not set, Do Not Disturb times out as configured in the Conference DoNotDisturb DefaultTimeout setting. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

| `ParticipantId` | Yes | `String` | String | Unique identifier of a participant in the call. To see the ParticipantIds for participants in a call, you can run the xCommand Conference ParticipantList Search. |
| `ParticipantRole` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | The new role you want to assign to the participant identified by the ParticipantId parameter; or the role that you want to revoke from the participant. Refer to the State parameter. |

### 1.245 xCommand Conference ParticipantList Search

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Conference.ParticipantList.Search`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Returns details about the participants in the call. The results can be filtered by specifying additional parameters.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Conference.ParticipantList.Search`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Conference ParticipantList Search [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Conference.ParticipantList.Search.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | Unique identifier of the call. During a call you can run xStatus Call to see the CallId. |
| `Limit` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | Limit the number of participants in the result. For example, if the limit is set to 10, the result set will contain only 10 entries even if the total number of hits is larger. |
