### 1.255 xCommand Conference SendEmailInvitation

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Conference.SendEmailInvitation`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Sends a request to the meeting platform (backend) to forward a meeting invitation by e-mail to the addresses specified in the Address parameters. It is the meeting platform that will decide the content and send the e-mail, not the device. A successful response to this command means that the backend has received and understood the request from the device. The device doesn't receive feedback whether the e-mail has been sent or received successfully. This command only applies to devices that are registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices with the Webex optimized experience enabled.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Conference.SendEmailInvitation`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Conference SendEmailInvitation [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Conference.SendEmailInvitation.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Address` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | The e-mail address of a recipient. You can add up to 10 Address parameters, each with one e-mail address. |
| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | Unique identifier of the call. During a call you can run xStatus Call to see the CallId. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.256 xCommand Conference SimultaneousInterpretation SelectLanguage

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Conference.SimultaneousInterpretation.SelectLanguage`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Simultaneous interpretation allows Webex meeting participants to listen to the meeting in their preferred language. The available languages depend on what the host of the meeting assigns, and are chosen during meeting set up. The language name and codes are then passed on in the data object (DTO) that is used to transfer meeting-related information from the Webex meeting backend to the meeting participants.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Conference.SimultaneousInterpretation.SelectLanguage`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Conference SimultaneousInterpretation SelectLanguage [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Conference.SimultaneousInterpretation.SelectLanguage.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | Unique identifier of the call. During a call you can run the xStatus Call command to see the CallId. |
| `LanguageCode` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | Select the code for the language you want the device to play back. You can find the available language names and language codes in the Conference Call[n] SimultaneousInterpretation Languages[n] LanguageCode and Language Name statuses. |
| `StreamId` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 1 (`Integer`) |  |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.267 xCommand HttpClient Allow Hostname Add

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/HttpClient.Allow.Hostname.Add`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Adds an HTTP(S) server to the list of allowed servers (hosts). The HttpClient Allow Hostname commands let you set up and maintain a list of up to ten allowed hosts. As long as the list is not empty, you can send HTTP(S) requests only to the servers in the list. The check against the list is performed both when using insecure (HTTP) and secure (HTTPS) transfer of data.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/HttpClient.Allow.Hostname.Add`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand HttpClient Allow Hostname Add [params]`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Expression` | Yes | `String` | String | Regular expression that matches a host name or IP address of an HTTP(S) server. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.271 xCommand HttpClient Delete

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/HttpClient.Delete`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Sends an HTTP(S) Delete request to the server that is specified in the Url parameter. You can use the AllowInsecureHTTPS parameter to specify whether or not to validate the server's certificate before sending data over HTTPS. This parameter has no effect unless the xConfiguration HttpClient AllowInsecureHTTPS is set to On. The command returns the HTTP status code along with the data returned from the server (HTTP headers and body). This is not available when using cloud APIs.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/HttpClient.Delete`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand HttpClient Delete [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.HttpClient.Delete.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AllowInsecureHTTPS` | No | `Literal` | Literal | If set to True the device skips the certificate validation process, and sends data to the server anyway. If set to False, the server certificate is checked, and data is not sent to the server if the certificate validation fails. |
| `Header` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | An HTTP header field. You can add up 20 Header parameters in one command, each holding one HTTP header field. |
| `ResponseSizeLimit` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 1048576 (`Integer`) | The maximum payload size (bytes) of the response to this request. If the response payload is larger than this maximum size, the command returns a status error with a message saying that the maximum file size is exceeded. However, this has no effect on the server side; the request was received and processed properly by the server. |
| `ResultBody` | No | `Literal` | Literal | None: The body of the HTTP response (if any) is not included in the command result. PlainText: The body of the HTTP response is included in the command result as plain text. If the response contain non-printable letters, the command returns a status error with a message saying that non-printable data was encountered. Base64: The body of the HTTP response is Base64 encoded before it is included in the command result. |
| `Timeout` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 30 (`Integer`) | Timeout period in seconds. If the request is not completed during this period, the API will return an error. |
| `Url` | Yes | `String` | String | The URL that the request will be sent to: <Protocol> + <Host name or IP address of an HTTP(S) server> + <Path>. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand HttpClient Post [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.HttpClient.Post.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AllowInsecureHTTPS` | No | `Literal` | Literal | If set to True the device skips the certificate validation process, and sends data to the server anyway. If set to False, the server certificate is checked, and data is not sent to the server if the certificate validation fails. |
| `Header` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | An HTTP header field. You can add up 20 Header parameters in one command, each holding one HTTP header field. |
| `ResponseSizeLimit` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 1048576 (`Integer`) | The maximum payload size (bytes) of the response to this request. If the response payload is larger than this maximum size, the command returns a status error with a message saying that the maximum file size is exceeded. However, this has no effect on the server side; the request was received and processed properly by the server. |
| `ResultBody` | No | `Literal` | Literal | None: The body of the HTTP response (if any) is not included in the command result. PlainText: The body of the HTTP response is included in the command result as plain text. If the response contain non-printable letters, the command returns a status error with a message saying that non-printable data was encountered. Base64: The body of the HTTP response is Base64 encoded before it is included in the command result. |
| `Timeout` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 30 (`Integer`) | Timeout period in seconds. If the request is not completed during this period, the API will return an error. |
| `Url` | Yes | `String` | String | The URL that the request will be sent to: <Protocol> + <Host name or IP address of an HTTP(S) server> + <Path>. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

If the response payload is larger than this maximum size, the command returns a status error with a message saying that the maximum file size is exceeded. However, this has no effect on the server side; the request was received and processed properly by the server. |

PlainText: The body of the HTTP response is included in the command result as plain text. ### 1.280 xCommand Logging ExtendedLogging Start

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Logging.ExtendedLogging.Start`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Start running continuous extended logging for the specified duration.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Logging.ExtendedLogging.Start`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Logging ExtendedLogging Start [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Logging.ExtendedLogging.Start.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Duration` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 600 (`Integer`) | Specify the length of time to perform the extended logging (in seconds). |
| `PacketDump` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Enable or disable the logging of packet data. These are stored in separate .pcap files. Full: Log all data for three minutes. FullRotate: Log all data for an hour, but with a size limit as specified in PacketDumpRotateSize. Limited: Log a limited set of data. This does not include data from the RTP port range, where media files are transmitted. None: Do not log packet data. |
| `PacketDumpRotateSize` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Specify the rotation size of the packet dump log file. When the file reaches this size, the file will be closed and logging will continue in a new file. Files older than the two newest log files will be deleted. PacketDumpRotateSize can only be supplied together with FullRotate and will default to Normal. Large:  Enable large file size (150 MB). Normal:  Enable normal file size (12 MB). |
| `RenderingDump` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Enable or disable limited rendering dump. The rendering dump includes changes that cause rendering to the screen. The output is written to osd.log and has formatting that shows which elements of the UI have caused rendering. It is written in batches of one second. Limited: Enable limited rendering dumping. None: No rendering dump logs will be updated. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

| `RemovePacketDump` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Delete or keep the packet dump log file. True: Automatically delete the packet dump log file. False: Do not delete the packet dump log file. |
| `RemoveRenderingDump` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Delete or keep the rendering dump log file. True: Automatically delete the rendering dump log file. False: Do not delete the packet rendering log file. |

### 1.282 xCommand Logging SendLogs

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Logging.SendLogs`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Send logs to the Webex cloud. These logs can help diagnose and fix issues with the device. The command returns a log ID, which an administrator or TAC engineer can use to identify and download the logs. For the command to work, the device must either be registered to the Webex cloud service or registered to an on-premises service and linked to Webex Edge for Devices. Additionally, for devices linked to Webex Edge for Devices, the xConfiguration Logging CloudUpload Mode must be set to On.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Logging.SendLogs.(...)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.306 xCommand Network Ping

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Network.Ping`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Ping is a network administration utility used to test the reachability of a host on a network and to measure the round-trip time for messages sent from the source to the destination. It operates by sending Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) echo request packets to the target host and waits for an ICMP echo reply. This process helps determine if the remote host is active or inactive, measures latency, and detects packet loss.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Network.Ping`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Network Ping [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Network.Ping.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Hostname` | Yes | `String` | String | Host name or IP address |
| `Packets` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 20 (`Integer`) | Specifies packets count |
| `Timeout` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 60 (`Integer`) | Specifies timeout in seconds. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.308 xCommand Network SNMP USM User Add

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Network.SNMP.USM.User.Add`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Creates a user (username and passwords) that a network management system can use to communicate with the video device using SNMP v3, User-based Security Model (USM). All USM users have equal access rights (read, read-write, or none), refer to the NetworkServices SNMP Mode setting. Authentication and privacy are always on. That is, the device supports only the authPriv security level and the privacy protocol is always AES (Advanced Encryption Standard). This command has no effect on SNMP v2c; authentication for SNMP v2c is configured with the NetworkServices SNMP CommunityName setting.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Network.SNMP.USM.User.Add`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Network SNMP USM User Add [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Network.SNMP.USM.User.Add.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AuthenticationPassword` | Yes | `String` | String | The authentication password for this USM user. It is used when authenticating the network management system. The authentication password is stored as a localized hashed value on the device (refer to the AuthenticationProtocol parameter). |
| `AuthenticationProtocol` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | The authentication hash function that will be applied before storing the authentication password on the device. The device only supports the listed hash functions (from the SHA-2 family); neither MD nor SHA-1 is supported. |
| `Name` | Yes | `String` | String | The name of the USM user. |
| `PrivacyPassword` | No | `String` | String | The privacy password for this USM user. It is used for the data encryption. The privacy password is stored as a localized hashed value (AES-128) on the device. If a privacy password is not set explicitly in this parameter, it will be the same as the authentication password (with hash function as specified in the Authentication Protocol paramter). |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.311 xCommand Network Traceroute

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Network.Traceroute`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Traceroute is a network diagnostic tool used to discover the path that packets take from a source device to a destination host across an IP network. It helps identify each hop (router or device) along the route and measures the transit delay of packets at each hop, which is useful for troubleshooting routing issues and network performance problems.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Network.Traceroute`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Network Traceroute [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Network.Traceroute.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Hops` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 50 (`Integer`) | Specifies maximum number of hops. |
| `Hostname` | Yes | `String` | String | Host name or IP address |
| `Timeout` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 5 (`Integer`) | Specifies timeout in seconds. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.312 xCommand Network Wifi Configure

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Network.Wifi.Configure`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Configures the device to connect to a specific Wi-Fi network. Auto connect is only available if Wi-Fi is enabled on the device. You must unplug the Ethernet cable before you can connect to Wi-Fi. The device supports access points with WPA2-only, WPA3-only, and WPA2/WPA3 transition modes for Personal or Enterprise, with SHA-128, SHA-256, or Fast Transition (802.11r) key management.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Network.Wifi.Configure`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Network Wifi Configure [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Network.Wifi.Configure.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AllowMissingCA` | No | `Literal` | Literal | The policy for allowing a Wi-Fi connection with missing Certificate Authentication (CA). False: Not allowed. True: Allowed |
| `AnonymousIdentity` | No | `String` | String | The anonymous identity, if applicable. |
| `Connect` | No | `Literal` | Literal | The behavior after saving the configuration. Auto: Connect to the Wi-Fi network immediately. Later: Connect to the Wi-Fi network later. |
| `Identity` | No | `String` | String | The username for the Wi-Fi connection, if applicable. |
| `Password` | No | `String` | String | The password for the Wi-Fi connection, if applicable. |
| `SSID` | Yes | `String` | String | The SSID for the Wi-Fi connection. |
| `Type` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | The encryption type and authentication method for the Wi-Fi connection. We support the following types: None: Open network (not secured) Personal: WPA2 (PSK) or WPA3 (SAE) Personal, with CCMP128 (AES) cipher. Enterprise-Fast: WPA2 or WPA3 Enterprise, with Flexible Authentication via Secure Tunneling (EAP-FAST). Enterprise-Peap: WPA2 or WPA3 Enterprise, with PEAP (Protected EAP) with EAP-MSCHAPv2 or EAP-GTC). Enterprise-Tls: WPA2 or WPA3 Enterprise, with EAP Transport Layer Security (EAP-TLS). Enterprise-Ttls: WPA2 or WPA3 Enterprise, with EAP Tunneled Transport Layer Security (EAP-TTLS). The following types are deprecated but are still available for backwards compatibility: Open, Wpa2-psk, Wpa2-eap-fast, Wpa2-eap-peap, Wpa2-eap-tls, Wpa2-eap-ttls. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.335 xCommand Peripherals TouchPanel Configure

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Peripherals.TouchPanel.Configure`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

A Room Navigator can operate in different modes: As standard user interface for the video device (controller), as a room booking device (room scheduler), or to display a persistent web app. The information, buttons, and controls displayed on the Room Navigator screen depend on the mode. You can also add information whether the Room Navigator is in the same room as the device, or if it is outside the room. Information about the location is useful when collecting and processing sensor data from the unit, for example, temperature and air quality. Controller + InsideRoom, RoomScheduler + OutsideRoom, and PersistentWebApp + OutsideRoom are the most common combinations. In most cases the mode and location of the Room Navigator are entered in the startup wizard when setting up the device for the first time. The intended use of this command is when you want to make changes to these parameters after the first-time setup.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Peripherals.TouchPanel.Configure`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Peripherals TouchPanel Configure [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Peripherals.TouchPanel.Configure.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ID` | Yes | `String` | String | A unique ID for the Room Navigator that is connected to the device, typically its MAC address. Refer to the Peripherals ConnectedDevice [n] ID status. |
| `Location` | No | `Literal` | Literal | InsideRoom: The Room Navigator is in the same room as the video device. OutsideRoom: The Room Navigator is outside the room. |
| `Mode` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Controller: The Room Navigator is the standard user interface of the video device. PersistentWebApp: A third-party web application (persistent web app) is running on the Room Navigator (only available if the Room Navigator is connected to the device over the network). RoomScheduler: The Room Navigator is used for room booking. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.343 xCommand Phonebook Contact Add

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Phonebook.Contact.Add`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Add a new contact to the local phonebook. The command returns the ContactId, which is a unique string that identifies the contact; typically, the format is "localContactId-n". You can add several contact methods (each with different Number, CallRate, CallType, Device, and Protocol) to a contact using the xCommand Phonebook ContactMethod Add command. Only the first contact method will appear in the Favorites list on the touch controller. All contact methods are available on the other UIs.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Phonebook.Contact.Add`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Phonebook Contact Add [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Phonebook.Contact.Add.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CallRate` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 6000 (`Integer`) | Set the call rate (kbps) to use when calling this contact. |
| `CallType` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select a call type (audio or video). By selecting Auto, the device will decide the call type automatically. |
| `Device` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select the value that describes the current contact method. This makes it easier to find the correct entry when there are multiple contact methods for the same person. |
| `FolderId` | No | `String` | String | The unique identifier for the folder that you want to store the contact in. The identifier will be returned by an xCommand Phonebook Search command. It was also returned when the xCommand Phonebook Folder Add command was issued to make the folder. |
| `ImageURL` | No | `String` | String | Currently not in use. |
| `Name` | Yes | `String` | String | The name of the contact. |
| `Number` | No | `String` | String | The number or video address of the contact. |
| `Protocol` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select a call protocol from the list. Spark is used for devices that are using the Webex infrastructure. |
| `Tag` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Tag the contact as a Favorite, or untag an already tagged contact. |
| `Title` | No | `String` | String | The title of the contact. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

| `CallType` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select a call type (audio or video). By selecting Auto, the device will decide the call type automatically. |
| `ContactId` | Yes | `String` | String | The unique identifier for the contact that you want to add a contact method to. The identifier will be returned by an xCommand Phonebook Search command. It was also returned when the xCommand Phonebook Contact Add command was issued to make the contact. |
| `Device` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select the value that describes the current contact method. This makes it easier to find the correct entry when there are multiple contact methods for the same person. |
| `Number` | Yes | `String` | String | The number or video address of the contact. |
| `Protocol` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select a call protocol from the list. Spark is used for devices that are using the Webex infrastructure. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.352 xCommand Phonebook Search

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Phonebook.Search`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The search command lets you search in both the local and corporate phonebooks. A search gives a ResultSet. The total number of folders and contacts (TotalRows) is always included in the result set when searching the local phonebook. When searching a corporate phonebook the total number of folders and contacts may not be included. Whether it is included or not depends on the backend corporate phonebook service (for example, Webex, CUCM, VCS, or TMS) and its version.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Phonebook.Search`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Phonebook Search [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Phonebook.Search.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ContactMethodLimit` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 10 (`Integer`) | Limit the number of records in the result set to this number. For example, if the limit is set to 2, the ResultSet will contain only 2 entries even if the total number of hits is larger. |
| `ContactType` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Search all contact types, or limit the search to folders or individual contacts. |
| `FolderId` | No | `String` | String | Search only in the specified folder. The FolderId (string) is listed in the ResultSet of a search result containing folders. |
| `Limit` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | Limit the number of records in the result set to this number. The maximum limit is 100 for corporate phonebooks (PhonebookType: Corporate) if the device is registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices. Otherwise, the maximum limit is 1000. For Webex, note that the limit applies to each type of result (for example, "person" or "room"). That is, if you set the limit to 20, the result set may contain up to 20 persons plus 20 rooms. Also refer to the SearchFilter parameter. |
| `Offset` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | Get records starting with this offset in a search. The default value is 0. Offset is used together with Limit to support paging. |
| `PhonebookId` | No | `String` | String | The identifier of the phonebook server that will be searched. See the xConfiguration Phonebook Server ID setting. |
| `PhonebookType` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Define whether to search the local phonebook or the corporate phonebook. |
| `Recursive` | No | `Literal` | Literal | This parameter will only have effect when searching the local phonebook. The setting determines whether a local phonebook search should be limited to the given FolderId, or also recursively search in its subfolders. If not specified, the search will be recursive. When issuing the command without specifying any parameters, all folders, contacts and contact methods in the local phonebook will be returned. |
| `SearchField` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Currently not in use. |
| `SearchFilter` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Filter search results by choosing the type of results you want to see. This parameter is available only for devices that are registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices. All: Search in all directories. People: Filter results to include only people. Pmr: Filter results to include only Personal Meeting Rooms. Rooms: Filter results to include only rooms/devices. |
| `SearchString` | No | `String` | String | Search for entries containing this string (the entry doesn't have to begin with the string). If no FolderId is specified, all folders / phonebook directories will be searched. |
| `Tag` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Limits the search to contacts that have been tagged as favorite or the untagged contacts. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.353 xCommand Presentation Start

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Presentation.Start`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Open a media stream from the selected presentation source. You can combine multiple presentation sources in a single presentation video stream (the maximum number of different input sources depend on the type of video device) by adding multiple ConnectorId or PresentationSource parameters in the same command. The order in which you place them in the command determines the order in which the sources show up on the screen. You cannot use a mix of identifier types in the same command; use either ConnectorId or PresentationSource.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Presentation.Start`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Presentation Start [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Presentation.Start.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ConnectorId` | No | `IntegerArray` | 1 to 3 (`IntegerArray`) | Select the video input source to be used for presentation, identified by connectorId. |
| `Instance` | No | `Literal` | Literal | You can have multiple presentations running simultaneously, as instances. The instance number is set automatically or can be specified by you. This number can then be used to stop a specific presentation. |
| `Layout` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select the layout of the presentation if the stream is composed of multiple input sources. Equal: The presentations are shown in same-sized images. There can be a maximum of four images on screen. Prominent: The first presentation source is shown as a large image, and the next presentation sources are shown as smaller images placed below. |
| `PresentationSource` | No | `LiteralArray` | LiteralArray | Select the video source to be used for presentation. n: The video input source to be used for presentation, identified by source number. Miracast: Wireless sharing using Miracast. Airplay: Wireless sharing using AirPlay. DirectShare: For future use. None: None can only be used when you have multiple PresentationSource parameters in the same command, and at least one of the other PresentationSource parameters have a value different from None. None means that a black frame is inserted in the composed stream. Remote: Wireless sharing from a Webex app that is paired with the device. WebView: Allows content from a web view to be used as the video source for presentation. |
| `SendingMode` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select whether the presentation is shown local and/or remote. LocalRemote: The presentation is shown both local and remote. LocalOnly: The presentation is shown locally. |
| `WebViewId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique ID for the Web View. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

None means that a black frame is inserted in the composed stream. Remote: Wireless sharing from a Webex app that is paired with the device. WebView: Allows content from a web view to be used as the video source for presentation. |
| `SendingMode` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select whether the presentation is shown local and/or remote. LocalRemote: The presentation is shown both local and remote. LocalOnly: The presentation is shown locally. |
| `WebViewId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique ID for the Web View. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.360 xCommand Presentation Start

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Presentation.Start`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Open a media stream from the selected presentation source. You can combine multiple presentation sources in a single presentation video stream (the maximum number of different input sources depend on the type of video device) by adding multiple ConnectorId or PresentationSource parameters in the same command. The order in which you place them in the command determines the order in which the sources show up on the screen. You cannot use a mix of identifier types in the same command; use either ConnectorId or PresentationSource.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Presentation.Start`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Presentation Start [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Presentation.Start.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ConnectorId` | No | `IntegerArray` | 1 to 12 (`IntegerArray`) | Select the video input source to be used for presentation, identified by connectorId. |
| `Instance` | No | `Literal` | Literal | You can have multiple presentations running simultaneously, as instances. The instance number is set automatically or can be specified by you. This number can then be used to stop a specific presentation. |
| `Layout` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select the layout of the presentation if the stream is composed of multiple input sources. Equal: The presentations are shown in same-sized images. There can be a maximum of four images on screen. Prominent: The first presentation source is shown as a large image, and the next presentation sources are shown as smaller images placed below. |
| `PresentationSource` | No | `LiteralArray` | LiteralArray | Select the video source to be used for presentation. n: The video input source to be used for presentation, identified by source number. Miracast: Wireless sharing using Miracast. Airplay: Wireless sharing using AirPlay. DirectShare: For future use. None: None can only be used when you have multiple PresentationSource parameters in the same command, and at least one of the other PresentationSource parameters have a value different from None. None means that a black frame is inserted in the composed stream. Remote: Wireless sharing from a Webex app that is paired with the device. WebView: Allows content from a web view to be used as the video source for presentation. |
| `SendingMode` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select whether the presentation is shown local and/or remote. LocalRemote: The presentation is shown both local and remote. LocalOnly: The presentation is shown locally. |
| `WebViewId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The unique ID for the Web View. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.368 xCommand Provisioning CUCM ExtensionMobility Login

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Provisioning.CUCM.ExtensionMobility.Login`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Sign-in command for the Extension Mobility service. You sign in to the Extension Mobility service with a username (UserId) and pin code (Pin). The username and pin code are set up in CUCM. CUCM also supports multiple profiles for a user. If you, for a user that has multiple profiles, submit a login command with only username and pin code, CUCM will send a list of available profiles back to the device. Then the device will create corresponding ExtensionMobilityProfileSelection Profile events, so that a new login command, which contains the Profile parameter in addition to the username and pin code, can be submitted.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Provisioning.CUCM.ExtensionMobility.Login`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Provisioning CUCM ExtensionMobility Login [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Provisioning.CUCM.ExtensionMobility.Login.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Pin` | Yes | `String` | String | A valid pin code for the user, as set up in CUCM. |
| `Profile` | No | `String` | String | A valid profile for the user, as set up in CUCM. This parameter applies only if the user has multiple profiles. |
| `UserId` | Yes | `String` | String | A valid username, as set up in CUCM. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.374 xCommand Provisioning Service Fetch

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Provisioning.Service.Fetch`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Add or update the customization template that details the custom elements of the device. Examples of custom elements are: branding images, macros, favorites, sign-in banner, and in-room control panels.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Provisioning.Service.Fetch`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Provisioning Service Fetch [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Provisioning.Service.Fetch.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Checksum` | No | `String` | String | The checksum is used to ensure the integrity of the downloaded customization template. When using HTTP, it is mandatory to add a checksum. When using HTTPS, it is mandatory to add a checksum only if you are downloading the template from a server that presents an unsigned certificate, or a self-signed certificate that is not in the CA list of the device (not trusted). |
| `ChecksumType` | No | `Literal` | Literal | The algorithm that is used to calculate the checksum. |
| `Mode` | No | `Literal` | Literal | If the mode is set to Add, all items listed in the uploaded file are added to the existing customization template. If the mode is set to Replace, the newer customization template that is uploaded, is compared against the previously uploaded template. Items that are not present in the newer file are removed. In both cases, items with the same name are overwritten. |
| `Origin` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Specifies whether the customization template is used for provisioning or for another purpose. When the value is Provisioning, the configurations (xConfiguration) in the template are ignored, and the provisioning system (CUCM or TMS) can set configurations like they normally do. CUCM always acts as if this parameter is set to Provisioning. Note that some configurations may be specific to one device, and you may end up with devices that you cannot reach if you provision those configurations to more than one device. |
| `URL` | Yes | `String` | String | The URL of the customization template. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.379 xCommand RoomAnalytics RoomInUse Set

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/RoomAnalytics.RoomInUse.Set`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Allows an external integration to contribute room-in-use state to RoomAnalytics. This is intended for third-party occupancy sources such as door sensors, PIR sensors, controllers, or automation systems. The external occupancy input is additive to native RoomOS room-in-use detection. It complements the device's built-in logic rather than replacing it, and xStatus RoomAnalytics RoomInUse remains the final effective room-in-use state. If ID is provided, the input is tracked as an identified occupancy sensor and exposed in xStatus RoomAnalytics OccupancySensor. If ID is omitted, the command still works as anonymous occupancy input and no OccupancySensor status entry is created. Sending InUse starts or refreshes the timeout for that source. Sending NotInUse clears that source immediately. The system supports up to 16 identified occupancy sensors at a time. Examples: xCommand RoomAnalytics RoomInUse Set State: InUse ID: door Duration: 600 xCommand RoomAnalytics RoomInUse Set State: NotInUse ID: door xCommand RoomAnalytics RoomInUse Set State: InUse Duration: 300

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/RoomAnalytics.RoomInUse.Set`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand RoomAnalytics RoomInUse Set [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.RoomAnalytics.RoomInUse.Set.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Duration` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 3600 (`Integer`) | The duration, in seconds, that an InUse contribution remains active unless refreshed by sending InUse again for the same source, or cleared by sending NotInUse. |
| `ID` | No | `String` | String | A stable unique identifier for the external occupancy source, for example a MAC address or another integrator-defined device ID. If omitted, the command updates anonymous occupancy input and does not create or update a tracked OccupancySensor status entry. |
| `State` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | InUse: The external source contributes that the room is in use. NotInUse: The external source is cleared immediately and no longer contributes room-in-use state. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `RoomControl`

### 1.384 xCommand RoomPreset Store

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/RoomPreset.Store`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Store the connector selections for all video input sources and the current position (pan and tilt), zoom and focus values for all cameras. Note that information about all video input sources, and pan, tilt, zoom and focus values for all cameras are included in the same preset. The device may hold 15 such predefined video input presets. These presets are available for far end control. That is, they are referred in the PresetId parameter of the FarEndControl Preset Activate command. In contrast, the Camera Preset commands applies to individual cameras only. Those presets are not available for far end control.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Description` | No | `String` | String | Enter a description of the camera preset. |
| `PresetId` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 15 (`Integer`) | The ID of this preset. |
| `Type` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Not applicable. If you want to ensure that a preset only affects camera positions we recommend that you select Camera. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.388 xCommand Security Certificates CSR Create

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Security.Certificates.CSR.Create`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Create a PKCS#10 CSR (Certificate Signing Request) and store the Private Key waiting to be "Linked". The command parameters determine the subject name of the CSR. The output is in PEM-encoded format. Only one CSR/Private Key pair can be active at any given time, so subsequent invocation will overwrite the current pair.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Security.Certificates.CSR.Create`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Security Certificates CSR Create [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Security.Certificates.CSR.Create.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CommonName` | Yes | `String` | String | Adds "/CN=" to the CSR Subject Name. |
| `CountryName` | No | `String` | String | Adds "/C=" to the CSR Subject Name. |
| `LocalityName` | No | `String` | String | Adds "/L=" to the CSR Subject Name. |
| `OrganizationName` | No | `String` | String | Adds "/O=" to the CSR Subject Name. |
| `OrganizationalUnit` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | Adds up to 5 "/OU=" parameters to the CSR Subject Name. |
| `SanDns` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | Adds up to 5 Dns parameters to the CSR Subject Alternative Name. |
| `SanEmail` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | Adds up to 5 Email parameters to the CSR Subject Alternative Name. |
| `SanIp` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | Adds up to 5 Ip parameters to the CSR Subject Alternative Name. |
| `SanUri` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | Adds up to 5 Uri parameters to the CSR Subject Alternative Name. |
| `StateOrProvinceName` | No | `String` | String | Adds "/ST=" to the CSR Subject Name. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

List the ciphers supported by various services (domains). Result: Name: Name of this domain.   * Syslog-TLS: Used for logging over TLS.   * HTTPS server: Used by the device's own web server.   * HTTPS client: Used for all https client traffic from the device.   * Pairing: Used for peripheral pairing to touch devices and microphones/amplifiers.   * SIP TLS: Used for direct IP SIP connections, SIP connections to CUCM or to VCS or other SIP proxies when transport is TLS. Cipherlist: The actual cipher list string sent to the TLS library. Ciphers: A space-separated list of ciphers by their TLS standard name.

### 1.417 xCommand SerialPort PeripheralControl Send

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/SerialPort.PeripheralControl.Send`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Send data via a serial connection to a third-party peripheral that is connected to the device. We refer to this as outbound serial control; see the SerialPort Outbound Mode setting for more information about the feature.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/SerialPort.PeripheralControl.Send`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand SerialPort PeripheralControl Send [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.SerialPort.PeripheralControl.Send.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `PortId` | No | `Literal` | Literal | The port to send the data over. |
| `ResponseTerminator` | No | `String` | String | A character or string that indicates that the rest of the response received from the peripheral will be ignored. If a ResponseTerminator is specified, then any response received from the peripheral serial port after the Send command is issued will be buffered. The command will return up-until the first occurrence of the ResponseTerminator character or string. If a ResponseTerminator is not specified, either the complete response will be returned, or it will be cut when the full ResponseTimeout period expires. The ResponseTerminator parameter is ignored if a ResponseTimeout parameter is not included in the command. |
| `ResponseTimeout` | No | `Integer` | 50 to 5000 (`Integer`) | The maximum number of milliseconds (ms) to wait for a response from the peripheral. If a ResponseTimeout is specified, the device listens for a response from the peripheral either the full ResponseTimeout period or until it receives the first occurrence of the character string specified in the ResponseTerminator parameter. If a ResponseTimeout is not specified, the device terminates the command session immediately after the text-payload transmission is completed. Any response from the peripheral is discarded. |
| `Text` | Yes | `String` | String | The text to send to the peripheral. You can add characters using "\" notation for special characters and "\x{ASCIIHEXCODE}" for hex characters. Examples: "Power:on\r" or "Power:on\x0D" for a command that ends with carriage return; "Power:on\n" or "Power:on\x0A" for a command that ends with a new line. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.422 xCommand Standby ResetTimer

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Standby.ResetTimer`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Reset the standby delay timer or set a temporary standby delay. If the device is in standby mode when the timer is set, the device is brought out of standby mode before starting the countdown. If you don't specify a Delay, the standby delay timer is reset, and the device goes into standby after the period that is given by the Standby Delay setting (xConfiguration Standby Delay). If you do specify a Delay, the device goes into standby when it has been idle for the specified period. Next time, the standby delay is as configured in the Standby Delay setting again.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Standby.ResetTimer`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Standby ResetTimer [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Standby.ResetTimer.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Delay` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 480 (`Integer`) | Set the delay in minutes. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

Reset the codec to factory default settings. The call logs are deleted and all device parameters are reset to default values. All files that have been uploaded to the codec are deleted. Option key(s) are not affected. Use the parameter Keep in order to choose which configurations and files to keep when you factory reset the device. As a default the device restarts after the factory reset, but other behaviors can be forced by selecting a different TrailingAction.

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/SystemUnit.FactoryReset`

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Confirm` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Include to confirm your choice. |
| `Keep` | No | `LiteralArray` | LiteralArray | Select which configurations and files to keep when you factory reset the device. Certificates: Client and CA certificates. HTTP: xConfiguration NetworkServices HTTP Mode xConfiguration NetworkServices HTTPS Server MinimumTLSVersion xConfiguration NetworkServices HTTPS StrictTransportSecurity xConfiguration NetworkServices HTTPS VerifyClientCertificate xConfiguration NetworkServices HTTPS VerifyServerCertificate LocalSetup: xConfiguration Audio DefaultVolume xConfiguration Audio SoundsAndAlerts RingVolume xConfiguration Time Zone xConfiguration UserInterface Language xCommand Camera Preset Store Network: xConfiguration Network 1 * xConfiguration NetworkServices Wifi Allowed xConfiguration NetworkServices Wifi Enabled Provisioning: xConfiguration Provisioning Mode RemoteSupportUser: The remote support user (if any). SerialPort: xConfiguration SerialPort Mode xConfiguration SerialPort BaudRate xConfiguration SerialPort LoginRequired Webex: xConfiguration Spark ServiceOverrides GdsBaseUrl xConfiguration Spark ServiceOverrides U2CBaseUrl |
| `TrailingAction` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select Shutdown or NoAction to override the default behavior (Restart). WaitForUpgrade: the device waits for up to 20 minutes for the software upgrade to complete before rebooting to complete reset. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Platform` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | CODECPRO: The platform is set to Codec Pro. ROOM70S: For Codec Plus and Room 70, the platform is set to Room 70 Single. For Codec Pro and Room 70 G2, the platform is set to Room 70 Single G2. ROOM70D: For Codec Plus and Room 70, the platform is set to Room 70 Dual. For Codec Pro and Room 70 G2, the platform is set to Room 70 Dual G2. |

### 1.459 xCommand UserInterface Branding Fetch

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.Branding.Fetch`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Fetches an image file from a URL and stores the file on the device. Supply the URL first. The following image formats are supported: BMP, GIF, JPEG, and PNG. The maximum image size is 16 megapixel, and the maximum file size is 8 MByte. The Type parameter determines what kind of image it is. If it is a background image, it is automatically applied. This command issues an HTTP request, so it is included in the HTTP requests count. The maximum number of concurrent requests is limited.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.Branding.Fetch`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand UserInterface Branding Fetch [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.UserInterface.Branding.Fetch.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Checksum` | No | `String` | String | Specify the checksum for the image file that is to be fetched. The checksum is used to ensure the integrity of the downloaded image file. When using HTTP, it is mandatory to add a checksum. When using HTTPS, it is mandatory to add a checksum only if you are downloading the template from a server that presents an unsigned certificate, or a self-signed certificate that is not in the CA list of the device (not trusted). |
| `ChecksumType` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Specify the algorithm that is used to calculate the checksum. |
| `CustomId` | No | `String` | String | Specify a custom identifier for this image. You can get the CustomId for the images used by using xStatus UserInterface Branding CustomId. |
| `Type` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Specify the usage type for this image. Background: Fetch a background image (wallpaper) that can be displayed when the device is active. Branding: Fetch a logo that can be displayed when the device is active. HalfwakeBackground: Fetch a background image (wallpaper) that can be displayed when the device is in the halfwake state. HalfwakeBranding: Fetch a logo that can be displayed when the device is in the halfwake state. SchedulerBackground: Fetch a background image (wallpaper) that can be displayed on a Room Navigator in scheduler mode. SchedulerBranding: Fetch a logo that can be displayed on a Room Navigator in scheduler mode. WorkspaceAvatar: Fetch an avatar that can be displayed in the room status icon on a Room Navigator in scheduler mode. |
| `URL` | Yes | `String` | String | Specify the URL of the image file. URL must be the first parameter. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.460 xCommand UserInterface Branding Get

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.Branding.Get`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The command returns the image file that is specified in the Type parameter, given that such a file is stored on the device. The file is Base64 encoded. The format is JPG for background images and PNG for logos, regardless of the format of the originally uploaded file. Background images are stored in three sizes, one for the main screen, one for the touch controller or scheduler, and one for the web interface illustrations. Use the Size parameter to choose which one to get. Logos have only one size.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.Branding.Get`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand UserInterface Branding Get [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.UserInterface.Branding.Get.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Size` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Large: The size of the image that is displayed on the main screen. Small: The size of the image that is displayed on the touch controller. Thumbnail: The size of the image that is used in the web interface illustrations. |
| `Type` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Background: Return the background image (wallpaper) that is displayed when the device is active. Branding: Return the logo that is displayed when the device is active. HalfwakeBackground: Return the background image (wallpaper) that is displayed when the device is in the halfwake state. HalfwakeBranding: Return the logo that is displayed when the device is in the halfwake state. SchedulerBackground: Return the background image (wallpaper) that is displayed on a Room Navigator in scheduler mode. SchedulerBranding: Return the logo that is displayed on a Room Navigator in scheduler mode. WorkspaceAvatar: Return the avatar that is displayed in the room status icon on a Room Navigator in scheduler mode. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.Branding.Upload`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Uploads an image file to the device. The following image formats are supported: BMP, GIF, JPEG, and PNG, and the maximum image size is 16 megapixels. The file must be Base64 encoded, and the maximum file size is 8 MByte. The Type parameter specifies the usage of the image. If it is a background image, it is automatically applied. This is a multiline command.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.Branding.Upload`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand UserInterface Branding Upload [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.UserInterface.Branding.Upload.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CustomId` | No | `String` | String | Specify a custom identifier for this image. You can get the CustomId for the images used by using xStatus UserInterface Branding CustomId. |
| `Type` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Background: Upload a background image that can be used when the device is active. Branding: Upload a logo that can be displayed when the device is active. HalfwakeBackground: Upload a background image (wallpaper) that can be displayed when the device is in the halfwake state. HalfwakeBranding: Upload a logo that can be displayed when the device is in the halfwake state. SchedulerBackground: Upload a background image (wallpaper) for a Room Navigator in scheduler mode. SchedulerBranding: Upload a logo for a Room Navigator in scheduler mode. WorkspaceAvatar: Upload an avatar (for the  room status icon)that can be displayed on a Room Navigator in scheduler mode. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

| `Option.5` | No | `String` | String | The text to appear on feedback option 5. |

| `Title` | No | `String` | String | The title of the message. |

Display a small window on screen with a title and text. Rating stars are provided for the user to select. The message is displayed on screen until the user gives a response, or until the device receives a UserInterface Message Rating Clear command. Use the xFeedback commands to monitor the feedback from the user. Read more about the xFeedback commands in the API introduction section in this guide.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.Message.Rating.Display`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand UserInterface Message Rating Display [params]`

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Duration` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 3600 (`Integer`) | How long (in seconds) the message window is to be displayed on the screen. If empty or set to 0, the message window is displayed until a UserInterface Message Rating Clear command is sent. |
| `FeedbackId` | No | `String` | String | To identify the feedback enter a FeedbackId. |
| `PeripheralId` | No | `String` | String |  |

| `Title` | No | `String` | String | Text shown as the title in the rating display window. This text is displayed in larger font and above the text provided with the Text parameter. If no text is provided for the title, it will be omitted and the rating display window will be smaller. |

### 1.518 xCommand UserInterface ScreenLock AdminInitiateRecovery

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.ScreenLock.AdminInitiateRecovery`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This command applies only to shared mode devices that are registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices. Also, the UserInterface ScreenLock Workspace Allowed setting must be True. The command returns a 6-digit one-time PIN and triggers a prompt on the device itself. The command is typically run from Control Hub by an administrator, and the administrator must provide the user of the device with this one-time PIN. The user of the device needs the one-time PIN to be able to follow the prompt on the device and set the device's actual PIN lock.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.ScreenLock.AdminInitiateRecovery`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand UserInterface ScreenLock AdminInitiateRecovery [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.UserInterface.ScreenLock.AdminInitiateRecovery.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Lifespan` | No | `Integer` | 2 to 10080 (`Integer`) | How many minutes the generated one-time PIN is valid. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.524 xCommand UserInterface WallpaperBundle Set

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.WallpaperBundle.Set`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Select one of the pre-installed wallpaper bundles. The wallpaper bundle is shown when the system is in awake state. A wallpaper bundle may include wallpapers for several setup types. Some bundles are prepared for multi-screen setups, by providing an image that spans several screens, while some bundles include a wallpaper for the touch controller. You must choose a bundle that offers the setup type that match your screen setup. You can see the list of bundles by running the UserInterface WallpaperBundle List command. For standard colored devices, meaning that the fabric is light gray, only the Light and Night wallpaper bundles are supported. The Beige, Blue, Carbon, and Forestgreen wallpaper bundles are only available for the limited edition Desk and Desk minis. The mountain and canyon wallpaper bundles are only available on Room Panorama setups. Note that the UserInterface Wallpaper setting must be set to Auto if you want to use wallpaper bundles.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/UserInterface.WallpaperBundle.Set`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand UserInterface WallpaperBundle Set [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.UserInterface.WallpaperBundle.Set.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Name` | Yes | `String` | String | The name of the wallpaper bundle. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.557 xCommand Video Input SetMainVideoSource

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Video.Input.SetMainVideoSource`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set which input source is the main video source. You can identify the input source by either the physical connector that it is connected to (ConnectorId) or the logical source identifier (SourceId). Also content input via AirPlay or Miracast are available as video sources. You can combine multiple input sources in a single main video stream (the maximum number of different input sources depend on the type of video device) by adding multiple ConnectorIds or SourceIds in the same command. There cannot be a mix of identifier types in the same command; use either ConnectorId or SourceId.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Video.Input.SetMainVideoSource`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Video Input SetMainVideoSource [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Video.Input.SetMainVideoSource.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |

### 1.567 xCommand Video Layout LayoutFamily Set

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Video.Layout.LayoutFamily.Set`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Select which video layout family to use locally. This setting applies only when using a device's built-in MultiSite feature (optional) to host a multipoint video conference.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Video.Layout.LayoutFamily.Set`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Video Layout LayoutFamily Set [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Video.Layout.LayoutFamily.Set.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CustomLayoutName` | No | `String` | String | To use a custom layout, specify this parameter and the layout name. |
| `LayoutFamily` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select a layout family. Auto: The default layout family, as given in the layout database provided by the device, will be used as the local layout. Custom: The name of your custom saved layout. Equal: The Grid layout family will be used as the local layout. Participants are shown in a grid of equal sized videos. If there is shared content it will appear beside the grid. Overlay: Not applicable in this software release. Prominent: The Stack layout family will be used as the local layout. The active speaker, or shared content, will be a large picture, while the other participants will be small pictures across the top. Transitions between active speakers are voice switched. Prominent_L:  The Prominent layout family will be used as the local layout. The active speaker is shown in the upper left part of the screen, and other participants are ranged across the bottom and beside on the right. Single: The Focus layout family will be used as the local layout. The active speaker, or the presentation if present, will be shown in full screen. The other participants are not shown. Transitions between active speakers are voice switched. |
| `Target` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select if the target is the local layout (what users of the current device will see) or the remote layout (what participants at the far end will see). |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.570 xCommand Video Layout StageParticipants Set ById

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Video.Layout.StageParticipants.Set.ById`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Note: This feature is not generally available in RoomOS 11.17 and 11.18. When you are in a Webex meeting you can move participants to be on the stage. This means that they are always visible as a frame in the layout on your screen; and they will be placed inside the largest of the available frames for the layout chosen by the user (or automatically selected). Note that you move the participants only on your local device; it has no effect on what other participants see on their screens. You can move up to four participants to be on stage. If one participant can't be resolved, the entire operation fails, and you won't see any change in state. If participants that haven't yet joined the meeting is moved to stage, the change will happen once they join the meeting. Use this command if you want to identify the participants to put on stage using the participanId as identifier. If you want to use the participants name, use the Video Layout StageParticipants Set ByName command instead. To see the ParticipantIds for participants in a call, you can run the xCommand Conference ParticipantList Search. Scan the list for the participant and use the subfield, "ParticipantId".

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Video.Layout.StageParticipants.Set.ById`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Video Layout StageParticipants Set ById [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Video.Layout.StageParticipants.Set.ById.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ActiveSpeakerIndex` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 8 (`Integer`) | Sets the index of the active speaker frame on stage. |
| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | • The CallId may be used to identify the far end device when in a Multipoint call. The CallId is returned when issuing the xCommand Dial command. You can get the callId during the call, by running xStatus Call from one of the devices participating in the call. |
| `ParticipantId` | Yes | `StringArray` | StringArray | You can add up to 4 participantId parameters in one command. Hence, you can move up to 4 participants to the stage. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 1.571 xCommand Video Layout StageParticipants Set ByName

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Video.Layout.StageParticipants.Set.ByName`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When you are in a Webex meeting you can move participants to be on the stage. Refer to the Video Layout StageParticipants Set ById command for more info about the feature. Use this command if you want to identify the participants to put on stage using their Webex (??) display name as identifier.  You can input a partial name and the device will attempt to resolve a participant based on substring matching. If one participant can't be resolved, the entire operation fails, and there will be no observable change in state.

| `CallId` | No | `Integer` | 0 to 65534 (`Integer`) | The CallId may be used to identify the far end device when in a Multipoint call. The CallId is returned when issuing the xCommand Dial command. You can get the callId during the call, by running xStatus Call from one of the devices participating in the call. |

| `Mode` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Choose whether to replace the existing source on that output rendered full screen or to add it. Using Add, the layout engine will recompose the multiple sources automatically. Replace is the default value. |
| `Output` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 2 (`Integer`) | Choose the output you wish to use for this layout. |

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Video.Matrix.Assign`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Video Matrix Assign [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Video.Matrix.Assign.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Layout` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Select the layout you wish to use for the video composition. Equal: All sources are shown in same-sized images on the output. Prominent: The first source is shown as a large image, and the next sources are shown as smaller images placed below. |
| `Mode` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Choose whether to replace the existing source on that output rendered full screen or to add it. Using Add, the layout engine will recompose the multiple sources automatically. Replace is the default value. |
| `Output` | Yes | `Integer` | 1 to 3 (`Integer`) | Choose the output you wish to use for this layout. |
| `RemoteMain` | No | `IntegerArray` | 1 to 4 (`IntegerArray`) | Add a remote site to the layout. |
| `SourceId` | No | `IntegerArray` | 1 to 9 (`IntegerArray`) | The identifier (ID) of the input source. Input Source [n] has ID n. Run the following API command to find the ID: xStatus Video Input Source. You can use up to four SourceIds in one command. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 1.598 xCommand WebEngine AllowInsecureHttps Add

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/WebEngine.AllowInsecureHttps.Add`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

By default, the web engine does not allow web content loaded from a host with self-signed HTTPS certificate. However, there may be reasons to allow this for select hosts anyway. This could be during the development and test phase of a new web-based service where the integrations are being tested on test servers without proper certificates - or in in-house deployed appliance services where insecure HTTPS connection to the services is considered acceptable. Using this command you can add the fully qualified DNS name or the IP address of these particular services to an "AllowInsecureHttps" list in which the codec will allow these sites to be used on the device even with self-signed HTTPS certificates. Even if the host is on the allow insecure HTTP access allow-list, you must set the AllowInsecureHttps parameter to True in the UserInterface WebView Display command to be able to load a web page with self-signed certificate. Cisco will still recommend that you use signed certificates in all production deployments.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/WebEngine.AllowInsecureHttps.Add`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand WebEngine AllowInsecureHttps Add [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.WebEngine.AllowInsecureHttps.Add.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Hostname` | Yes | `String` | String | The URL or hostname of the web site. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.604 xCommand WebEngine Logging Set

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/WebEngine.Logging.Set`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set what type of messages to add in the web engine log files. The level you set determines how serious an issue must be to be included in the logs. Messages for the set level and up (more serious) are included in the web engine logs. So, if you choose the lowest level (Verbose) the most information is added to the logs; if you choose the highest level (Fatal), only the most serious errors such as software crashes are added. The Verbose log level can be further refined by using the Verbosity parameter. All these log levels are as defined by Chromium.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/WebEngine.Logging.Set`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand WebEngine Logging Set [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.WebEngine.Logging.Set.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Level` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | The log level. The lowest level (most logging) is Verbose, then Info, Warning, Error, and finally the highest level is Fatal (least logging). |
| `Verbosity` | No | `Integer` | -20 to -1 (`Integer`) | Refined log level for Verbose. -1 gives the least logging and -20 the most. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

You can set up a list of web sites that are granted permanent access to the device's camera or microphone, bypassing the default prompt dialog. This may be useful in custom setups, such as kiosk and web apps, as users will not have to allow camera and microphone access via a dialog every time a call is made. | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Device` | Yes | `LiteralArray` | LiteralArray | Choose whether to grant access to the camera or microphone. Add this parameter twice, once for microphone and once for camera, if you want to grant access to both. |
| `Hostname` | Yes | `String` | String | The URL or hostname of the web site. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 1.609 xCommand WebEngine Tracing Start

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/WebEngine.Tracing.Start`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Starts a chromium trace for use with advanced debugging. Please see the chromium documentation. Note that this generates a lot of data, so be mindful of the duration of the trace. Ideally, use the Duration parameter or the WebEngine Tracing Stop command to limit the trace to just a few seconds, to capture exactly the issue and nothing more. The resulting trace data is stored in /run/webengine_traces (requires remote access to the device).

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/WebEngine.Tracing.Start`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand WebEngine Tracing Start [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.WebEngine.Tracing.Start.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CustomCategories` | No | `String` | String | Only used when the Mode parameter is set to Custom. Allows you to manually specify which chromium categories to include in the trace. Accepts a comma-separated list of chromium tracing categories. |
| `Duration` | No | `Integer` | 1 to 1800 (`Integer`) | The duration of the trace recording in seconds. |
| `Mode` | Yes | `Literal` | Literal | Set a predefined set of categories to use in the trace. Each category captures different data. If Custom is chosen, see the CustomCategories parameter. |
| `Systrace` | No | `Literal` | Literal | On: Use the Android Systrace format for the trace file (recommended). Off: Use the legacy format for the trace file. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

Join a WebRTC meeting (for example, Microsoft Teams or Google Meet). WebRTC is only available for devices that are registered to an on-premises service and linked to Webex Edge for Devices, and for devices that are registered to the Webex cloud service.

Personalization: Control Hub provides a permanent personal Webex account on a device that is linked to Webex Edge for Devices. |

This API initiates the Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) process, which automates device registration and configuration without requiring manual entry of an activation code. Once the device's MAC address has been claimed and assigned to a workspace in Cisco Webex Control Hub, invoking this command triggers automatic registration with Webex. The device then applies any preconfigured settings associated with the workspace, streamlining onboarding and reducing manual setup steps.

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `SecurityAction` | No | `Literal` | Literal | Harden: Deactivate all existing local users and macros when registering the device. NoAction: Register the device as it is. No changes to local users and macros. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

Send whiteboards as PDF attachments to a list of email addresses using the locally configured SMTP server. You must include at least one BoardUrl/AttachmentFilenames pair in the command. You may attach more than one whiteboard to the same email, by adding several pairs. Refer to the NetworkServices SMTP settings to find how to set up the device to use an SMTP server.

#### Usage Syntax

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Whiteboard.Email.Send.(...)`
