| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AttachmentFilenames` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | The filename of a whiteboard to be attached to the email. The filename must end with ".pdf". If you are attaching more than one whiteboard, you must add multiple AttachmentFilenames parameters in the same command, one for each file. The number of AttachmentFilenames and BoardUrls must be the same, and each filename corresponds to a url in the same order. |
| `BoardUrls` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | The whiteboard to be attached to the email as a PDF file. The whiteboard is identified by its url, which you can find in the Conference Presentation Whiteboard BoardUrl status. If you are attaching more than one whiteboard, you must add multiple BoardUrls parameters in the same command, one for each whiteboard. |
| `Body` | Yes | `String` | String | The body text of the email to be sent. |
| `Recipients` | No | `StringArray` | StringArray | The list of email addresses to send the email to. You must add at least one recipient. You may add multiple recipients in the same command, if so, add one Recipient parameter for each. |
| `Subject` | Yes | `String` | String | The subject line of the email to be sent. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 1.631 xCommand Zoom Join

**Endpoint:** `XCOMMAND /v1/xapi/command/Zoom.Join`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This command builds the Zoom dial string based on the information in the command's parameters, and in the Zoom DefaultDomain and Zoom DialStringOptions settings. The Zoom meeting to join is identified by a MeetingID provided by Zoom or a BookingID. It's mandatory to include one of these parameters. If using the BookingID, the device will fetch the join information from the booking. If the join information includes a passcode, it will be added to the dial string only if a passcode is not provided in the MeetingPasscode parameter. The domain is always included in the join information, so the Zoom DefaultDomain setting will be ignored. The Zoom DialStringOptions setting is ignored if the uri fetched from the join information has a format other than <meetingid>@<domain>. If using the MeetingID, the domain and dial string options are always fetched from the Zoom DefaultDomain and Zoom DialStringOptions settings. See "https://support.zoom.us/hc/en-us/articles/202405539-SIP-H-323-Room-Connector-Dial-Strings" for more information about Zoom's dial string format.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `POST https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/command/Zoom.Join`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xCommand Zoom Join [params]`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Command.Zoom.Join.(...)`

#### Parameters

| Name | Required | Type | Range / Valuespace | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `BookingID` | No | `String` | String | Unique identifier of the booking. It's the Id that is returned by the Bookings List command. |
| `DialCode` | No | `String` | String | When provided, it will be added on the end of the authority host like so: <meetingID.<passcode>.<options>.<hostkey>..<dialcode>@zoomcrc.com If the DialCode is not provided, the trailing .<dialcode> is omitted from the uri. |
| `Domain` | No | `String` | String | When provided, it will be used in place of the configured domain. |
| `HostKey` | No | `String` | String | The key that is required to join the meeting as host. |
| `MeetingID` | No | `String` | String | The meeting number of the zoom meeting. Typically provided in the calendar invite or in the meeting link. |
| `MeetingPasscode` | No | `String` | String | The passcode for the meeting. Typically provided in the calendar invite or in the meeting link. |
| `TrackingData` | No | `String` | String | A tag or label that will be preserved and stored in the call history. |

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

## 2 xConfiguration

### 2.1 xConfiguration Apps WallpaperBundles HalfwakeImage

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Apps.WallpaperBundles.HalfwakeImage`

In some scenarios, for example when UserInterface Theme Name is set to Night, a colored background will show in half-wake mode. You can turn it off with this setting, to always use a black background.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Apps WallpaperBundles HalfwakeImage: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Apps.WallpaperBundles.HalfwakeImage.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.2 xConfiguration Audio ConnectorSetup

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.ConnectorSetup`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

You can choose whether to set up the audio inputs and outputs manually, or to let the video device do it automatically based on the type of camera you have and which screens are connected. In Auto mode, you cannot add, update, delete or connect audio inputs and outputs manually. Therefore the following API commands do not have any effect: xCommand Audio Setup *, xCommand Audio LocalInput *, and xCommand Audio LocalOutput *. When going from Manual to Auto mode: The existing Audio setup is cleared (xCommand Audio Setup Clear), and the input and output groups are set up according to product defaults. The Audio Output HDMI [n] Mode and Audio Output ARC [1] Mode settings are set to their default value. When going from Auto to Manual mode: The HDMI and ARC output connectors are connected to the main output group. The Audio Output HDMI [n] Mode and Audio Output ARC [1] Mode settings are not changed. AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio ConnectorSetup: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.ConnectorSetup.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.3 xConfiguration Audio DefaultVolume

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.DefaultVolume`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the default volume for the speakers. For all devices except the Desk series, the volume is set to this level when you switch on the device or restart it. Desk devices remember the last audio level set by the user also after a restart. You can use the controls on the user interface or the Audio Volume commands to change the volume both in call and out of call. The Audio Volume SetToDefault command resets the volume to the default value.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio DefaultVolume: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.DefaultVolume.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.4 xConfiguration Audio DefaultVolume

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.DefaultVolume`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the default volume for the speakers. For all devices except the Desk series, the volume is set to this level when you switch on the device or restart it. Desk devices remember the last audio level set by the user also after a restart. You can use the controls on the user interface or the Audio Volume commands to change the volume both in call and out of call. The Audio Volume SetToDefault command resets the volume to the default value.

### 2.5 xConfiguration Audio Ethernet Encryption

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Ethernet.Encryption`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Decide whether to allow unencrypted audio streams on the video device's internal network. Note that the AES67 standard doesn't support encrypted media streams. Therefore, this setting must be set to Optional to allow AES67 audio. Codec EQ, Codec EQX, Room Bar Pro: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Ethernet Encryption: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Ethernet.Encryption.set(<value>)`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the multicast address that the video device will both listen for stream announcements on and announce its own streams on. Only change this setting if required by your peripherals. Codec EQ, Codec EQX, Room Bar Pro: AVIntegrator option required.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Ethernet SAPDiscovery Address: <value>`

The video device supports discovery using SAP (Service Announcement Protocol). Therefore, when enabled, the video device can both discover streams that are announced by peripherals and announce its own streams. Which IP address to listen for and send announcements on, are decided in the Audio Ethernet SAPDiscovery Address setting. Codec EQ, Room Bar Pro: AVIntegrator option required.

### 2.11 xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..6] Channel[1..8] Level

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..6].Channel[1..8].Level`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the gain for the specified channel of an Ethernet input, e.g. a microphone or audio interface. The gain should be adjusted to suit the output level of the connected audio source. The gain can be tuned in steps of 1 dB. If the gain is set too high, the audio signal will be clipped. If the gain is set too low, the audio signal-to-noise ratio will be degraded; however, this is usually preferable to clipping. Note that unprocessed speech signals typically contain significant level variations, making it very important to allow for sufficient signal headroom.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..6] Channel[1..8] Level: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..6].Channel[1..8].Level.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.12 xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..6] Channel[1..8] Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..6].Channel[1..8].Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Disables or enables audio on the specified channel of an Ethernet input. Setting Audio Input Ethernet [n] Mode to Off will override the effect of the individual channel mode settings.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..6] Channel[1..8] Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..6].Channel[1..8].Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Set which mix channel (left or right) this input channel is mixed to. For a single channel mix this setting has no effect.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..6].Channel[1..8].Pan.set(<value>)`

### 2.14 xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..6] Channel[1..8] Zone

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..6].Channel[1..8].Zone`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This command is mainly used for Presenter and Audience room setup. It's mainly used from Control Hub when setting up the feature. During setup we recommend you add information whether the microphone is facing the stage (presenter) or the audience. This information allows for more accurate automatic switching between the local, remote, and hybrid presenter modes. 1: Use this value, when the direction of the microphone is not used. 2: Use this value when the microphone is set up to face the stage area 3: Use this value when the microphone is set up to face the audience.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..6] Channel[1..8] Zone: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..6].Channel[1..8].Zone.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The echo canceller continuously adjusts itself to the audio characteristics of the room, and compensates for any changes it detects in the audio environment. If the changes in the audio conditions are significant, the echo canceller may take a second or two to re-adjust.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..6].EchoControl.Mode.set(<value>)`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video device has built-in noise reduction, which reduces stationary background noise, for example noise from air-conditioning systems, cooling fans etc. In addition, a high pass filter (Humfilter) reduces very low frequency noise. Noise reduction requires that Audio Input Ethernet [n] EchoControl Mode is enabled.

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.20 xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..8] Channel[1..8] Gain

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].Channel[1..8].Gain`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the gain for the specified channel of an Ethernet input, e.g. a microphone or audio interface. The gain should be adjusted to suit the output level of the connected audio source. The gain can be tuned in steps of 1 dB. If the gain is set too high, the audio signal will be clipped. If the gain is set too low, the audio signal-to-noise ratio will be degraded; however, this is usually preferable to clipping. Note that unprocessed speech signals typically contain significant level variations, making it very important to allow for sufficient signal headroom.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..8] Channel[1..8] Gain: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].Channel[1..8].Gain.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.21 xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..8] Channel[1..8] Level

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].Channel[1..8].Level`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the gain for the specified channel of an Ethernet input, e.g. a microphone or audio interface. The gain should be adjusted to suit the output level of the connected audio source. The gain can be tuned in steps of 1 dB. If the gain is set too high, the audio signal will be clipped. If the gain is set too low, the audio signal-to-noise ratio will be degraded; however, this is usually preferable to clipping. Note that unprocessed speech signals typically contain significant level variations, making it very important to allow for sufficient signal headroom.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].Channel[1..8].Level.set(<value>)`

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].Channel[1..8].Mode.set(<value>)`

Set which mix channel (left or right) this input channel is mixed to. For a single channel mix this setting has no effect.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..8] Channel[1..8] Pan: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].Channel[1..8].Pan.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.24 xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..8] Channel[1..8] Zone

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].Channel[1..8].Zone`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This command is mainly used for Presenter and Audience room setup. It's mainly used from Control Hub when setting up the feature. During setup we recommend you add information whether the microphone is facing the stage (presenter) or the audience. This information allows for more accurate automatic switching between the local, remote, and hybrid presenter modes. 1: Use this value, when the direction of the microphone is not used. 2: Use this value when the microphone is set up to face the stage area 3: Use this value when the microphone is set up to face the audience.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..8] Channel[1..8] Zone: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].Channel[1..8].Zone.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.25 xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..8] EchoControl Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].EchoControl.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The echo canceller continuously adjusts itself to the audio characteristics of the room, and compensates for any changes it detects in the audio environment. If the changes in the audio conditions are significant, the echo canceller may take a second or two to re-adjust.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..8] EchoControl Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].EchoControl.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.26 xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..8] EchoControl NoiseReduction

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].EchoControl.NoiseReduction`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video device has built-in noise reduction, which reduces stationary background noise, for example noise from air-conditioning systems, cooling fans etc. In addition, a high pass filter (Humfilter) reduces very low frequency noise. Noise reduction requires that Audio Input Ethernet [n] EchoControl Mode is enabled.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Ethernet[1..8] EchoControl NoiseReduction: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Ethernet[1..8].EchoControl.NoiseReduction.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.52 xConfiguration Audio Input MicrophoneMode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.MicrophoneMode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

If the microphone mode is Focused, the microphones can be combined to focus sound sensitivity. As a result, the noise in the room is suppressed, and you can be heard better when sitting right in front of the device. The voice of people not sitting right in front of the device will be suppressed. If the microphone mode is Wide, the device behaves like any other device. The voice of people sitting beside you will be heard, and also more noise from the room. We recommend that you use Focused mode when you are the only speaker. Use Wide mode when several speakers are in front of the device.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input MicrophoneMode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.MicrophoneMode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[1..3].EchoControl.NoiseReduction.set(<value>)`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Microphone[1..3].Equalizer.Mode`

Enable or disable the equalizer processing for this microphone input.

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[1..3] Equalizer Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[1..3].Equalizer.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.58 xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[1..3] Gain

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Microphone[1..3].Gain`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the gain on the Microphone input connector. The gain should be adjusted to suit the output level of the connected audio source. The gain can be tuned in steps of 1 dB. If the gain is set too high, the audio signal will be clipped. If the gain is set too low, the audio signal-to-noise ratio will be degraded; however, this is usually preferable to clipping. Note that unprocessed speech signals typically contain significant level variations, making it very important to allow for sufficient signal headroom. The maximum input level with 0 dB gain is -18 dBu. Example: If your microphone has a maximum output level of -40 dBu, then you should set the gain to -18 dBu - (-40 dBu) = 22 dB.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[1..3] Gain: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[1..3].Gain.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

This command is mainly used for the Presenter and Audience room setup. It's mainly used from Control Hub when setting up the feature. During setup we recommend you add information whether the microphone is facing the stage (presenter) or the audience. This information allows for more accurate automatic switching between the local, remote, and hybrid presenter modes. 1: Use this value, when the direction of the microphone is not used. 2: Use this value when the microphone is set up to face the stage area 3: Use this value when the microphone is set up to face the audience.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[1..3] Zone: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[1..3].Zone.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[1..4].EchoControl.Dereverberation.set(<value>)`

### 2.65 xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[1..4] EchoControl Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Microphone[1..4].EchoControl.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The echo canceller continuously adjusts itself to the audio characteristics of the room, and compensates for any changes it detects in the audio environment. If the changes in the audio conditions are significant, the echo canceller may take a second or two to re-adjust.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[1..4] EchoControl Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[1..4].EchoControl.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.66 xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[1..4] EchoControl NoiseReduction

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video device has built-in noise reduction, which reduces stationary background noise, for example noise from air-conditioning systems, cooling fans etc. In addition, a high pass filter (Humfilter) reduces very low frequency noise. Noise reduction requires that Audio Input Microphone [n] EchoControl Mode is enabled.

#### Usage Syntax

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[1..4].EchoControl.NoiseReduction.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.71 xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[1..4] MuteOverride

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Microphone[1..4].MuteOverride`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting is only for the analog microphone inputs on Codec Pro. Configure the microphone input to override the main mute state of the system (that is, the mute state controlled with the ordinary mute button(s)). This allows for the microphone input to be unmuted and used as a line input for transmitting presentation sounds, etc. during active video input. Note that the microphone may still be muted if it is associated with an inactive video input and is set to mute on inactive video input. As an example, if one needs to present audio from an analog source, some of the microphone inputs need to be repurposed as line inputs. Without MuteOverride, the sound from these presentation sources will go silent if the presenter mutes the microphone(s) during playback of the presentation.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[1..4] MuteOverride: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[1..4].MuteOverride.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

This information allows for more accurate automatic switching between the local, remote, and hybrid presenter modes. 1: Use this value, when the direction of the microphone is not used. 2: Use this value when the microphone is set up to face the stage area 3: Use this value when the microphone is set up to face the audience.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[1] Zone: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[1].Zone.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.91 xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[2] EchoControl Dereverberation

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Microphone[2].EchoControl.Dereverberation`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video device has built-in signal processing to reduce the effect of room reverberation. Dereverberation requires that Audio Input Microphone [n] EchoControl Mode is enabled.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[2] EchoControl Dereverberation: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[2].EchoControl.Dereverberation.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.92 xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[2] EchoControl Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Microphone[2].EchoControl.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The echo canceller continuously adjusts itself to the audio characteristics of the room, and compensates for any changes it detects in the audio environment. If the changes in the audio conditions are significant, the echo canceller may take a second or two to re-adjust.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[2] EchoControl Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[2].EchoControl.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.93 xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[2] EchoControl NoiseReduction

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Microphone[2].EchoControl.NoiseReduction`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video device has built-in noise reduction, which reduces stationary background noise, for example noise from air-conditioning systems, cooling fans etc. In addition, a high pass filter (Humfilter) reduces very low frequency noise. Noise reduction requires that Audio Input Microphone [n] EchoControl Mode is enabled.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[2] EchoControl NoiseReduction: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[2].EchoControl.NoiseReduction.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.94 xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[2] Gain

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.Microphone[2].Gain`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the gain on the Microphone input connector. The gain should be adjusted to suit the output level of the connected audio source. The gain can be tuned in steps of 1 dB. If the gain is set too high, the audio signal will be clipped. If the gain is set too low, the audio signal-to-noise ratio will be degraded; however, this is usually preferable to clipping. Note that unprocessed speech signals typically contain significant level variations, making it very important to allow for sufficient signal headroom. The maximum input level with 0 dB gain is -18 dBu. Example: If your microphone has a maximum output level of -40 dBu, then you should set the gain to -18 dBu - (-40 dBu) = 22 dB.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input Microphone[2] Gain: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.Microphone[2].Gain.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.116 xConfiguration Audio Input USBMicrophone[1] EchoControl Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Input.USBMicrophone[1].EchoControl.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The device's echo canceller continuously adjusts itself to the audio characteristics of the room and compensates for any changes it detects in the audio environment. If the changes in the audio conditions are significant, the echo canceller may take a second or two to re-adjust. The AEC reference signal is always sent from the device to the USB microphone. Whether echo cancellation is performed in the device or in external equipment doesn't matter. If performing echo cancellation in external equipment, directional audio should be switched off using the Audio Panning Mode setting.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Input USBMicrophone[1] EchoControl Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Input.USBMicrophone[1].EchoControl.Mode.set(<value>)`

### 2.122 xConfiguration Audio Microphones BeamMix Inputs

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Microphones.BeamMix.Inputs`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The device's internal microphone array consists of two major parts: A near talker sector, covering up to about 1.5 m from the device; and three beams that cover up to about 4 m from the device. The device also supports external analog or digital microphones. This setting is about using the beams and external microphones (analog or digital (Ethernet)) at the same time. In general, we recommend you not to allow the beams and external microphones at the same time, that is, we recommend keeping this setting at Auto. If you choose to allow the beams and external microphones at the same time, be aware that you might get more reverberation.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Microphones BeamMix Inputs: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Microphones.BeamMix.Inputs.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.123 xConfiguration Audio Microphones HdmiPassthrough MuteButton

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Microphones.HdmiPassthrough.MuteButton`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When using the Call from laptop feature (requires that Video Output HDMI Passthrough Allowed is set to True), people can always mute their audio from the meeting app. Use this setting to configure whether to allow muting from the touch controller and external microphones as well. The meeting app must be set up to use the HDMI-to-USB converter (capturing device) as microphone instead of the laptop microphone. Be aware that the touch controller / microphones are not synchronized with the meeting app regarding mute. Therefore, the mute indicators in the room and in the meeting app don't always reflect the true mute state.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Microphones HdmiPassthrough MuteButton: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Microphones.HdmiPassthrough.MuteButton.set(<value>)`

### 2.125 xConfiguration Audio Microphones NearTalkerSector Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Microphones.NearTalkerSector.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The device's internal microphone array consists of two major parts: A near talker sector, covering up to about 1.5 m from the device; and three beams that cover up to about 4 m from the device. This setting is about activating and using the near talker sector.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Microphones NearTalkerSector Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Microphones.NearTalkerSector.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Microphones.NoiseRemoval.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Use this setting to enable or disable the noise removal function on a device, as well as to define the default behavior when the function is enabled. If enabled (Enabled or Manual), there will be buttons on the user interface that allow users to turn background noise removal on and off, and it will also be possible to turn it on and off using API commands.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Microphones.NoiseRemoval.Mode.set(<value>)`

### 2.129 xConfiguration Audio Microphones UsbPassthrough MuteButton

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Microphones.UsbPassthrough.MuteButton`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When using the Call from laptop feature (that is, a laptop meeting app is using the device's camera, microphones, or loudspeakers), people can always mute their sound from the meeting app. Use this setting to configure whether to also allow muting from external microphones and the device itself as well. It is of course a prerequisite that people set up their meeting app to use the device's microphones instead of the laptop microphone. Be aware that the device and microphones are not synchronized with the meeting app regarding mute. Therefore, the mute indicators in the room and in the meeting app don't always reflect the true mute state.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Microphones UsbPassthrough MuteButton: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Microphones.UsbPassthrough.MuteButton.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.132 xConfiguration Audio Output ARC[1] Delay DelayMs

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Output.ARC[1].Delay.DelayMs`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

To obtain lip-synchronization, you can configure each ARC output with an extra delay that compensates for delay in other connected devices, for example TVs and external loudspeakers. The delay that you set here is either fixed or relative to the delay measured on or reported by an external monitor, as defined in the Audio Output ARC [n] Delay Mode setting.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Output ARC[1] Delay DelayMs: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Output.ARC[1].Delay.DelayMs.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Output.ARC[1].Delay.Direct.DelayMs`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

You can apply a dedicated direct delay to the audio output, which will affect all inputs from input groups where the Direct mode is enabled. This configuration is particularly useful for scenarios such as local sound reinforcement and voice lift.

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Output ARC[1] Delay Direct DelayMs: <value>`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

You may add extra delay to an audio ARC output with the Audio Output ARC [n] Delay DelayMs setting. The extra delay added is either a fixed number of milliseconds, or a number of milliseconds relative to the detected delay on or reported by an external monitor.

Choose whether or not to enable the audio return channel (ARC) on the HDMI [n] input connector. The ARC output must be enabled if you want audio playback through the Quad Camera. On Room 70 G2, the Camera is a part of the integrated loudspeaker system. We recommend to leave the ARC output enabled. If you want to disable the complete integrated loudspeaker system, use the Audio Output InternalSpeaker Mode setting.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Output ARC[1] Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Output.ARC[1].Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.137 xConfiguration Audio Output ConnectorSetup

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Output.ConnectorSetup`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

You can choose whether to set up the audio inputs and outputs manually, or to let the video device do it automatically based on the type of camera you have and which screens are connected. In Auto mode, you cannot add, update, delete or connect audio inputs and outputs manually. Therefore the following API commands do not have any effect: xCommand Audio Setup *, xCommand Audio LocalInput *, and xCommand Audio LocalOutput *. When going from Manual to Auto mode: The existing Audio setup is cleared (xCommand Audio Setup Clear), and the input and output groups are set up according to product defaults. The Audio Output HDMI [n] Mode and Audio Output ARC [1] Mode settings are set to their default value. For Codec Pro automatic delay measurement is enabled. When going from Auto to Manual mode: The HDMI and ARC output connectors are connected to the main output group. The Audio Output HDMI [n] Mode and Audio Output ARC [1] Mode settings are not changed. If microphone passthrough is enabled for Codec Pro or Room 70 G2, it will be disconnected. For Codec Pro delay measurement is stopped.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Output ConnectorSetup: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Output.ConnectorSetup.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

When going from Auto to Manual mode: The HDMI and ARC output connectors are connected to the main output group. The Audio Output HDMI [n] Mode and Audio Output ARC [1] Mode settings are not changed. ### 2.142 xConfiguration Audio Output Ethernet[1..2] Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Output.Ethernet[1..2].Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Ethernet [1]: The reference signal, which is required for acoustic echo cancelling (AEC), is sent from the codec to all connected digital microphones (Cisco Table Microphone Pro / Cisco Microphone Array) on this connection. If disabled, AEC will not work. Ethernet [2]: This connection is used by Room Kit EQX and Room Panorama for the audio output from the codec to the DNAM IV amplifier. Other Ethernet [n]: The connection is used for audio output from the codec to third-party audio peripherals, such as loudspeakers, that support the AES67 standard. We recommend you use the embedded Room Kit EQX and Room Panorama audio systems, which requires this setting to be On. If you switch it Off, the internal loudspeakers will not be used, and you need to connect external loudspeakers to the codec.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Output Ethernet[1..2] Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Output.Ethernet[1..2].Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.165 xConfiguration Audio Output InternalSpeaker Mode

Define whether or not to use the device's integrated speakers. For Room Kit EQX, Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, and Room Panorama, the Audio Output HDMI [n] Mode settings for the integrated sreens(s) must be set to On in order to play any audio on the integrated speakers. Also, the Audio Output ARC 1 Mode setting must be On. You can limit the use of the integrated speakers to play only ultrasound.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Output InternalSpeaker Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Output.InternalSpeaker.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.168 xConfiguration Audio Output Line[1..2] Delay DelayMs

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Output.Line[1..2].Delay.DelayMs`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

To obtain lip-synchronization, you can configure each audio line output with an extra delay that compensates for delay in other connected devices, for example TVs and external loudspeakers. The delay that you set here is either fixed or relative to the delay on the HDMI output, as defined in the Audio Output Line [n] Delay Mode setting.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Output Line[1..2] Delay DelayMs: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Output.Line[1..2].Delay.DelayMs.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.169 xConfiguration Audio Output Line[1..2] Delay Direct DelayMs

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Output.Line[1..2].Delay.Direct.DelayMs`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

You can introduce a direct delay to an audio output, which will be applied to all inputs from input groups where Direct mode is activated. This configuration is particularly beneficial for scenarios involving local sound reinforcement and voice lift.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Output Line[1..2] Delay Direct DelayMs: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Output.Line[1..2].Delay.Direct.DelayMs.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Output.Line[1..2].Delay.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

You may add extra delay to an audio line output with the Audio Output Line [n] Delay DelayMs setting. The extra delay added is either a fixed number of milliseconds, or a number of milliseconds relative to the detected delay on the HDMI output (typically introduced by the connected TV).

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Output Line[1..2] Delay Mode: <value>`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the gain on the Line output connector. The gain should be adjusted to fit the audio input level of the connected device. The gain can be tuned in steps of 1 dB. The maximum output level with 0 dB gain is 8 dBu. Example: If the connected audio device has max input level 4 dBu, then you should set the gain to 4 dBu - 8 dBu = -4 dB.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Output Line[1..2] Gain: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Output.Line[1..2].Gain.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

#### Usage Syntax

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Output.USBInterface[1].Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.200 xConfiguration Audio Panning HeadsetAnalog BinauralProcessing

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Panning.HeadsetAnalog.BinauralProcessing`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Disable or enable binaural processing of audio for an analog headset. This is the audio processing technique that achieves natural sounding directional audio.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Panning HeadsetAnalog BinauralProcessing: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Panning.HeadsetAnalog.BinauralProcessing.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.201 xConfiguration Audio Panning HeadsetAnalog Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Panning.HeadsetAnalog.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Disable or enable audio panning to provide directional audio for an analog headset. If directional audio is turned off overall with the Audio Panning Mode setting, you will never get directional audio for the headset even if Audio Panning HeadsetAnalog Mode is set to Auto.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Panning HeadsetAnalog Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Panning.HeadsetAnalog.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Panning.HeadsetUSB.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.204 xConfiguration Audio Panning Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Panning.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

In scenarios where the device knows where in the video stream layout the person speaking is located, the device can playback audio on the loudspeakers closest to that location. You will also get a similar effect when using a headset. This is referred to as directional audio. For example, if the person speaking is placed to the left in the layout, audio will come from the left loudspeaker. Headsets are further addressed in the Audio Panning HeadsetAnalog (only Desk Pro) and Audio Panning HeadsetUSB (only Board Pro, Board Pro G2, and Desk Series devices) settings. This setting is not available for the first generation of Board (non S-series).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Panning Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Panning.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Enables or disables exclusion zone processing for this microphone. This setting is only applicable to the Cisco Ceiling Microphone Pro.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Peripherals Microphone[1..6] ExclusionZone Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Peripherals.Microphone[1..6].ExclusionZone.Mode.set(<value>)`

### 2.209 xConfiguration Audio Peripherals Microphone[1..6] ExclusionZone Zones

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Peripherals.Microphone[1..6].ExclusionZone.Zones`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Specifies which exclusion zones are active for this microphone. The value is a 25-character string where each character represents a zone: use "1" to exclude the zone and "0" to include it. An empty string resets the configuration. The exclusion zone wizard is recommended for setup, but you can edit this value directly for quick changes. This setting is only applicable to the Cisco Ceiling Microphone Pro.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Peripherals Microphone[1..6] ExclusionZone Zones: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Peripherals.Microphone[1..6].ExclusionZone.Zones.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.Peripherals.Microphone[1..6].ID`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The unique MAC address assigned to a Cisco peripheral microphone connected via Ethernet. This value is automatically set when the microphone is connected. If any settings for this microphone are changed, its association is retained even if the microphone is later disconnected.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio Peripherals Microphone[1..6] ID: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.Peripherals.Microphone[1..6].ID.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Allows users to assign a custom label to each peripheral microphone slot. This feature ensures the microphone's ID association is preserved if the microphone is disconnected, without editing any functional changing configurations.

### 2.236 xConfiguration Audio SoundsAndAlerts DTMFFeedback

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.SoundsAndAlerts.DTMFFeedback`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Introduces a configurable option to enable or disable DTMF audio feedback. Previously, the device always played audio feedback when DTMF keys were pressed, whether through the WebUI or Phoenix interface. With this update, customers can choose to turn DTMF audio feedback on or off, in response to requests for greater flexibility.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio SoundsAndAlerts DTMFFeedback: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.SoundsAndAlerts.DTMFFeedback.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.239 xConfiguration Audio USB DevicesWithVideo

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.USB.DevicesWithVideo`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting determines whether USB devices that provide both audio and video interfaces (such as webcams or AV DSP units) can function as audio devices.

#### Usage Syntax

### 2.243 xConfiguration Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.USB.VolumeControl.Capture.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting applies when a USB capture device (e.g. a USB microphone) is connected to the video device. If the USB device has an internal trim setting, you can request the USB device to trim the audio signal level before sending it to the video device. Use the Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Value setting to set how much gain/attenuation to apply.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.USB.VolumeControl.Capture.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.244 xConfiguration Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Value

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.USB.VolumeControl.Capture.Value`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting applies if the Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Mode is set to Active. This is the gain that the video device requests the USB capture device to apply before sending the audio signal to the video device. The actual range that the USB device offers can be found in the Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Max and Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Min statuses. If the requested volume value is outside this range, the closest allowed value will be used. The Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Value status always returns the actual gain applied. Note that the USB device may apply a gain as default. Since the Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Value status always returns the actual gain applied, you may want to check this status before you decide on which gain to request. Example: If you want to request a 6 dB increase to the current level, and the default gain already applied by the USB device is 42 dB, you must set the Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Value setting to 48, that is 42+6 dB.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio USB VolumeControl Capture Value: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.USB.VolumeControl.Capture.Value.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.245 xConfiguration Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.USB.VolumeControl.Playback.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting applies when a USB playback device (e.g. a USB loudspeaker) is connected to the video device. If the USB device has an internal trim setting, you can request the USB device to trim the audio signal level it receives from the video device before any further processing. Use the Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Value setting to set how much gain/attenuation to apply.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.USB.VolumeControl.Playback.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.246 xConfiguration Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Value

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Audio.USB.VolumeControl.Playback.Value`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting applies if the Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Mode is set to Active. This is the gain that the video device requests the USB capture device to apply after receiving the audio signal from the video device. The actual range that the USB device offers can be found in the Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Max and Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Min statuses. If the requested volume value is outside this range, the closest allowed value will be used. The Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Value status always returns the actual gain applied. Note that the USB device may apply a gain as default. Since the Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Value status always returns the actual gain applied, you may want to check this status before you decide on which gain to request. Example: If you want to request a 6 dB increase to the current level, and the default gain already applied by the USB device is 42 dB, you must set the Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Value setting to 48, that is 42+6 dB.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Audio USB VolumeControl Playback Value: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Audio.USB.VolumeControl.Playback.Value.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.272 xConfiguration Cameras Camera ExcludedArea

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera.ExcludedArea`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When set, this configuration instructs the Multi Camera Director to ignore faces that appear in selected areas of a camera's field of view. The format is a list of polygons separated by semicolons. Each polygon is defined by 3 or more coordinate pairs, separated by commas. The coordinates are spherical and expressed in hundredths of degrees. For example, "0,0" would indicate a ray pointing straight out of the camera. "100,100" would indicate a ray pointing one degree to the left and one degree up from the camera. For a motorized camera, the coordinate system is relative to the neutral position of the camera, and does not change when the camera moves. For multi camera setups it is useful to note that the exclusion zones are defined per camera. Example: "1000,500, 500,500, 500,-500, 1000,500; -2000,-1000, -2500,-1000, -2500,-1500, -2000,-1500" This defines two exclusion zones: - The first is from (10°,5°) to (5°,-5°). - The second is from (-20°,-10°) to (-25°,-15°)

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera ExcludedArea: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera.ExcludedArea.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera.ExposureCompensation.Level`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

If you find the camera image always to be too dark (under-exposed) or too bright (over-exposed), you can use this setting to offset the target brightness. The brightness/exposure will continue to be adjusted automatically. This setting has an effect only when the Cameras Camera Brightness Mode is set to Auto.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera ExposureCompensation Level: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera.ExposureCompensation.Level.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.275 xConfiguration Cameras Camera Whitebalance Compensation Level

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera.Whitebalance.Compensation.Level`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Sets the white balance compensation level of the specified camera. If you find the camera image always to be too cold (with blue-ish tint) or too warm (with yellow-ish tint), you can use this setting to offset the default auto white balance. The white balance will continue to be adjusted automatically. Negative values of this setting will make the image appear colder, while positive values will make it appear warmer. The device must be restarted after changing this setting for the change to take effect.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera Whitebalance Compensation Level: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera.Whitebalance.Compensation.Level.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.276 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[1..15] AssignedSerialNumber

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[1..15].AssignedSerialNumber`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The camera ID is the number n in Camera [n]. By default, the camera ID is assigned automatically to a camera. If EDID information is not passed on from the camera to the video device, the camera ID is not persistent after a reboot. This means that a camera may get a new camera ID when the video device is restarted. You should use the Cameras Camera AssignedSerialNumber setting to cater for configurations where the video device does not receive EDID information from multiple cameras. This setting allows you to manually assign a camera ID to a camera by associating the camera ID with the camera's serial number. The setting is persistent until the video device is factory reset. A typical situation where the video device doesn't receive EDID information is when using an HDMI repeater that doesn't pass on such information.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[1..15] AssignedSerialNumber: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[1..15].AssignedSerialNumber.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.277 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[1..15] Backlight DefaultMode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[1..15].Backlight.DefaultMode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Turn backlight compensation on or off. Backlight compensation is useful when there is much light behind the persons in the room. Without compensation the persons may appear very dark to the far end. This setting is not applicable for the integrated camera of Bar Pro, Board Pro, and Board Pro G2. If the Cameras Camera Brightness Algorithm is not set to Average, neither is it applicable to the Quad camera and the integrated camera of Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, or Room Panorama. These cameras automatically adjust themselves based on the room lighting conditions.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[1..15] Backlight DefaultMode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[1..15].Backlight.DefaultMode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.284 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[1..15] ExcludedArea

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[1..15].ExcludedArea`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When set, this configuration instructs the Multi Camera Director to ignore faces that appear in selected areas of a camera's field of view. The format is a list of polygons separated by semicolons. Each polygon is defined by 3 or more coordinate pairs, separated by commas. The coordinates are spherical and expressed in hundredths of degrees. For example, "0,0" would indicate a ray pointing straight out of the camera. "100,100" would indicate a ray pointing one degree to the left and one degree up from the camera. For a motorized camera, the coordinate system is relative to the neutral position of the camera, and does not change when the camera moves. For multi camera setups it is useful to note that the exclusion zones are defined per camera. Example: "1000,500, 500,500, 500,-500, 1000,500; -2000,-1000, -2500,-1000, -2500,-1500, -2000,-1500" This defines two exclusion zones: - The first is from (10°,5°) to (5°,-5°). - The second is from (-20°,-10°) to (-25°,-15°)

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[1..15] ExcludedArea: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[1..15].ExcludedArea.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

By setting the Gamma Level you can select which gamma correction table to use. This setting may be useful in difficult lighting conditions, where changes to the brightness setting does not provide satisfactory results. Requires the Cameras Camera [n] Gamma Mode to be set to Manual. This setting is not applicable for the Quad Camera or the integrated cameras of Bar Pro, Board Pro, Board Pro G2, Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, and Room Panorama. These cameras automatically adjust themselves based on the room lighting conditions. Also, this feature is not supported by the PTZ 4K camera or the PTZ-12 camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[1..15].Gamma.Level.set(<value>)`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[1..15].Gamma.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting enables gamma corrections. Gamma describes the nonlinear relationship between image pixels and monitor brightness. This setting is not applicable for the Quad Camera or the integrated cameras of Bar Pro, Board Pro, Board Pro G2, Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, and Room Panorama. These cameras automatically adjust themselves based on the room lighting conditions. Also, this feature is not supported by the PTZ 4K camera or the PTZ-12 camera.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[1..15].Gamma.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.292 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[1..15] IrCutFilter Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[1..15].IrCutFilter.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting applies only to the PTZ 4K camera and will not have any effect on other cameras. The IR cut filter (infrared cut-off filter) blocks near-infrared wavelengths while passing visible light. In regular lighting conditions, the filter should be on (Day mode) to avoid unwanted side-effects caused by infrared light. However, if you want the camera to capture images in the dark, the filter should be off (Night mode) so that infrared light can be utilized.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[1..15] IrCutFilter Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[1..15].IrCutFilter.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[1..15].IrCutFilter.Threshold`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting has an effect only when Cameras Camera [n] IrCutFilter Mode is set to Auto, that is, when the camera is set to switch between Day and Night mode automatically. The higher the threshold value, the more light is required to trigger a switch to Day mode.

With Flip mode (vertical flip), you can flip the image upside down. Flipping applies both to the self-view and the video that is transmitted to the far end. This setting is not supported by the Quad Camera, the PTZ-12 camera, or the integrated camera of Board Pro, Board Pro G2, Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, or Room Panorama.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] Flip: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[10].Flip.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] Focus Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[10].Focus.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.317 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] Gamma Level

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[10].Gamma.Level`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

By setting the Gamma Level you can select which gamma correction table to use. This setting may be useful in difficult lighting conditions, where changes to the brightness setting does not provide satisfactory results. Requires the Cameras Camera [n] Gamma Mode to be set to Manual. This setting is not applicable for the Quad Camera or the integrated cameras of Bar Pro, Board Pro, Board Pro G2, Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, and Room Panorama. These cameras automatically adjust themselves based on the room lighting conditions. Also, this feature is not supported by the PTZ 4K camera or the PTZ-12 camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] Gamma Level: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[10].Gamma.Level.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.318 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] Gamma Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[10].Gamma.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting enables gamma corrections. Gamma describes the nonlinear relationship between image pixels and monitor brightness. This setting is not applicable for the Quad Camera or the integrated cameras of Bar Pro, Board Pro, Board Pro G2, Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, and Room Panorama. These cameras automatically adjust themselves based on the room lighting conditions. Also, this feature is not supported by the PTZ 4K camera or the PTZ-12 camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] Gamma Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[10].Gamma.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.319 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] IrCutFilter Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[10].IrCutFilter.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting applies only to the PTZ 4K camera and will not have any effect on other cameras. The IR cut filter (infrared cut-off filter) blocks near-infrared wavelengths while passing visible light. In regular lighting conditions, the filter should be on (Day mode) to avoid unwanted side-effects caused by infrared light. However, if you want the camera to capture images in the dark, the filter should be off (Night mode) so that infrared light can be utilized.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] IrCutFilter Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[10].IrCutFilter.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.320 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] IrCutFilter Threshold

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[10].IrCutFilter.Threshold`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting has an effect only when Cameras Camera [n] IrCutFilter Mode is set to Auto, that is, when the camera is set to switch between Day and Night mode automatically. The higher the threshold value, the more light is required to trigger a switch to Day mode.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] IrCutFilter Threshold: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[10].IrCutFilter.Threshold.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.321 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] Mirror

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[10].Mirror`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

With Mirror mode (horizontal flip) you can mirror the image on screen. Mirroring applies both to the self-view and the video that is transmitted to the far end. Mirroring is automatically disabled when speaker tracking is on. This setting is only applicable when using a Precision 60 camera. However, the PTZ 4K camera automatically mirrors the image when the Cameras Camera [n] Flip setting is On.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[10] Mirror: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[10].Mirror.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.326 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[11] AssignedSerialNumber

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[11].AssignedSerialNumber`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The camera ID is the number n in Camera [n]. By default, the camera ID is assigned automatically to a camera. If EDID information is not passed on from the camera to the video device, the camera ID is not persistent after a reboot. This means that a camera may get a new camera ID when the video device is restarted. You should use the Cameras Camera AssignedSerialNumber setting to cater for configurations where the video device does not receive EDID information from multiple cameras. This setting allows you to manually assign a camera ID to a camera by associating the camera ID with the camera's serial number. The setting is persistent until the video device is factory reset. A typical situation where the video device doesn't receive EDID information is when using an HDMI repeater that doesn't pass on such information.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[11] AssignedSerialNumber: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[11].AssignedSerialNumber.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.327 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[11] Backlight DefaultMode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[11].Backlight.DefaultMode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Turn backlight compensation on or off. Backlight compensation is useful when there is much light behind the persons in the room. Without compensation the persons may appear very dark to the far end. This setting is not applicable for the integrated camera of Bar Pro, Board Pro, and Board Pro G2. If the Cameras Camera Brightness Algorithm is not set to Average, neither is it applicable to the Quad camera and the integrated camera of Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, or Room Panorama. These cameras automatically adjust themselves based on the room lighting conditions.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[11] Backlight DefaultMode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[11].Backlight.DefaultMode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

In regular lighting conditions, the filter should be on (Day mode) to avoid unwanted side-effects caused by infrared light. However, if you want the camera to capture images in the dark, the filter should be off (Night mode) so that infrared light can be utilized.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[12] IrCutFilter Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[12].IrCutFilter.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.352 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[12] IrCutFilter Threshold

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[12].IrCutFilter.Threshold`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting has an effect only when Cameras Camera [n] IrCutFilter Mode is set to Auto, that is, when the camera is set to switch between Day and Night mode automatically. The higher the threshold value, the more light is required to trigger a switch to Day mode.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[12] IrCutFilter Threshold: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[12].IrCutFilter.Threshold.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.353 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[12] Mirror

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[12].Mirror`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

With Mirror mode (horizontal flip) you can mirror the image on screen. Mirroring applies both to the self-view and the video that is transmitted to the far end. Mirroring is automatically disabled when speaker tracking is on. This setting is only applicable when using a Precision 60 camera. However, the PTZ 4K camera automatically mirrors the image when the Cameras Camera [n] Flip setting is On.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[12] Mirror: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[12].Mirror.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[12].Whitebalance.Level.set(<value>)`

### 2.358 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[13] AssignedSerialNumber

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[13].AssignedSerialNumber`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The camera ID is the number n in Camera [n]. By default, the camera ID is assigned automatically to a camera. If EDID information is not passed on from the camera to the video device, the camera ID is not persistent after a reboot. This means that a camera may get a new camera ID when the video device is restarted. You should use the Cameras Camera AssignedSerialNumber setting to cater for configurations where the video device does not receive EDID information from multiple cameras. This setting allows you to manually assign a camera ID to a camera by associating the camera ID with the camera's serial number. The setting is persistent until the video device is factory reset. A typical situation where the video device doesn't receive EDID information is when using an HDMI repeater that doesn't pass on such information.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[13] AssignedSerialNumber: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[13].AssignedSerialNumber.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.359 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[13] Backlight DefaultMode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[13].Backlight.DefaultMode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Turn backlight compensation on or off. Backlight compensation is useful when there is much light behind the persons in the room. Without compensation the persons may appear very dark to the far end. This setting is not applicable for the integrated camera of Bar Pro, Board Pro, and Board Pro G2. If the Cameras Camera Brightness Algorithm is not set to Average, neither is it applicable to the Quad camera and the integrated camera of Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, or Room Panorama. These cameras automatically adjust themselves based on the room lighting conditions.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[13] Backlight DefaultMode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[13].Backlight.DefaultMode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Define the white balance level. Requires the Cameras Camera [n] Whitebalance Mode to be set to Manual. This setting is not applicable for the integrated camera of Bar Pro, Board Pro, and Board Pro G2, which automatically adjusts itself based on the room lighting conditions. #### Usage Syntax

### 2.390 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[15] AssignedSerialNumber

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[15].AssignedSerialNumber`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The camera ID is the number n in Camera [n]. By default, the camera ID is assigned automatically to a camera. If EDID information is not passed on from the camera to the video device, the camera ID is not persistent after a reboot. This means that a camera may get a new camera ID when the video device is restarted. You should use the Cameras Camera AssignedSerialNumber setting to cater for configurations where the video device does not receive EDID information from multiple cameras. This setting allows you to manually assign a camera ID to a camera by associating the camera ID with the camera's serial number. The setting is persistent until the video device is factory reset. A typical situation where the video device doesn't receive EDID information is when using an HDMI repeater that doesn't pass on such information.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[15] AssignedSerialNumber: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[15].AssignedSerialNumber.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.391 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[15] Backlight DefaultMode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[15].Backlight.DefaultMode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Turn backlight compensation on or off. Backlight compensation is useful when there is much light behind the persons in the room. Without compensation the persons may appear very dark to the far end. This setting is not applicable for the integrated camera of Bar Pro, Board Pro, and Board Pro G2. If the Cameras Camera Brightness Algorithm is not set to Average, neither is it applicable to the Quad camera and the integrated camera of Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, or Room Panorama. These cameras automatically adjust themselves based on the room lighting conditions.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[15] Backlight DefaultMode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[15].Backlight.DefaultMode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

This setting is not applicable for the Quad Camera or the integrated cameras of Bar Pro, Board Pro, Board Pro G2, Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, and Room Panorama. - **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[15].Gamma.Level.set(<value>)`

### 2.398 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[15] Gamma Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[15].Gamma.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting enables gamma corrections. Gamma describes the nonlinear relationship between image pixels and monitor brightness. This setting is not applicable for the Quad Camera or the integrated cameras of Bar Pro, Board Pro, Board Pro G2, Room 70 G2, Room 70 Panorama, and Room Panorama. These cameras automatically adjust themselves based on the room lighting conditions. Also, this feature is not supported by the PTZ 4K camera or the PTZ-12 camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[15] Gamma Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[15].Gamma.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.399 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[15] IrCutFilter Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[15].IrCutFilter.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting applies only to the PTZ 4K camera and will not have any effect on other cameras. The IR cut filter (infrared cut-off filter) blocks near-infrared wavelengths while passing visible light. In regular lighting conditions, the filter should be on (Day mode) to avoid unwanted side-effects caused by infrared light. However, if you want the camera to capture images in the dark, the filter should be off (Night mode) so that infrared light can be utilized.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[15] IrCutFilter Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[15].IrCutFilter.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.400 xConfiguration Cameras Camera[15] IrCutFilter Threshold

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Cameras.Camera[15].IrCutFilter.Threshold`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting has an effect only when Cameras Camera [n] IrCutFilter Mode is set to Auto, that is, when the camera is set to switch between Day and Night mode automatically. The higher the threshold value, the more light is required to trigger a switch to Day mode.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Cameras Camera[15] IrCutFilter Threshold: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Cameras.Camera[15].IrCutFilter.Threshold.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

With Mirror mode (horizontal flip) you can mirror the image on screen. Mirroring applies both to the self-view and the video that is transmitted to the far end.
