### 2.787 xConfiguration Proximity Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Proximity.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

For on-premises registered devices, the Proximity Mode setting determines whether the device emits ultrasound pairing messages or not. When the device emits ultrasound pairing messages, Cisco collaboration clients can detect that they are close to the device. In order to use a client, at least one of the Proximity services must be enabled (refer to the Proximity Services settings) as well. In general, Cisco recommends enabling all the Proximity services. The Proximity Mode and Audio Ultrasound MaxVolume settings only affect ultrasound pairing messages. To stop all ultrasound emissions, the RoomAnalytics PeoplePresenceDetector and Standby WakeupOnMotionDetection settings must also be disabled. The Proximity Mode setting has no effect for Webex cloud-registered devices. To disable ultrasound pairing messages on these devices, set xConfiguration Webex Proximity Mode to Off or set Audio Ultrasound MaxVolume to 0.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Proximity Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Proximity.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 2.792 xConfiguration RTP Audio Ports Range Webex Start

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RTP.Audio.Ports.Range.Webex.Start`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the first port in the range of RTP audio ports for Webex meetings. The device is using the ports in the range defined by the RTP Audio Ports Range Webex Start and Stop settings for RTP and RTCP media data. The minimum range is 20. A change in the setting will take effect on new calls.

#### Usage Syntax

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RTP.Audio.Ports.Range.Webex.Start.set(<value>)`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RTP.Audio.Ports.Range.Webex.Stop`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the last port in the range of RTP audio ports for Webex meetings. The device is using the ports in the range defined by the RTP Audio Ports Range Webex Start and Stop settings for RTP and RTCP media data. The minimum range is 20. A change in the setting will take effect on new calls.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration RTP Audio Ports Range Webex Stop: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RTP.Audio.Ports.Range.Webex.Stop.set(<value>)`

### 2.794 xConfiguration RTP Ports Range Start

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RTP.Ports.Range.Start`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the first port in the range of RTP ports. The device is using the ports in the range defined by the RTP Ports Range Start and Stop settings for RTP and RTCP media data. The minimum range is 100 when RTP Video Ports Range is disabled, and 20 when RTP Video Ports Range is enabled. If the RTP Video Ports Range is enabled, audio will use the range defined by the RTP Ports Range settings, and other media data will use the range defined by the RTP Video Ports Range settings. The two ranges must not overlap. A change in the setting will take effect on new calls. Note that the device uses another default RTP Port Range for Webex meetings and Webex optimized calls. The RTP range for Webex meetings and Webex optimised calls is defined in the RTP Audio Ports Range Webex Start/Stop and RTP Video Ports Range Webex Start/Stop settings.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration RTP Ports Range Start: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RTP.Ports.Range.Start.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.795 xConfiguration RTP Ports Range Stop

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RTP.Ports.Range.Stop`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the last port in the range of RTP ports. The device is using the ports in the range defined by the RTP Ports Range Start and Stop settings for RTP and RTCP media data. If the RTP Video Ports Range is enabled the device is using the ports in the range 1024 to 65436. The minimum range is 100 when RTP Video Ports Range is disabled, and 20 when RTP Video Ports Range is enabled. If the RTP Video Ports Range is enabled, audio will use the range defined by the RTP Ports Range settings, and other media data will use the range defined by the RTP Video Ports Range settings. The two ranges must not overlap. A change in the setting will take effect on new calls. Note that the device uses another default RTP Port Range for Webex meetings and Webex optimized calls. The RTP range for Webex meetings and Webex optimised calls is defined in the RTP Audio Ports Range Webex Start/Stop and RTP Video Ports Range Webex Start/Stop settings.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration RTP Ports Range Stop: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RTP.Ports.Range.Stop.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.796 xConfiguration RTP Video Ports Range Start

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RTP.Video.Ports.Range.Start`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the first port in the range of RTP video ports. If both the start and stop values are set to 0, the RTP Video Ports Range is disabled. To enable it, set the first port to a value between 1024 and 65454 and the last port between 1024 and 65535. The minimum range is 80. If the RTP Video Ports Range is enabled, audio will use the range defined by the RTP Ports Range settings, and other media data will use the range defined by the RTP Video Ports Range settings. The two ranges must not overlap. A change in the setting will take effect on new calls. Note that the device uses another default RTP Video Port Range for Webex meetings and Webex optimized calls. The RTP range for Webex meetings and Webex optimised calls is defined in the RTP Video Ports Range Webex Start/Stop and RTP Video Ports Range Webex Start/Stop settings.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration RTP Video Ports Range Start: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RTP.Video.Ports.Range.Start.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.797 xConfiguration RTP Video Ports Range Stop

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RTP.Video.Ports.Range.Stop`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the last port in the range of RTP video ports. If both the start and stop values are set to 0, the RTP Video Ports Range is disabled. To enable it, set the first port to a value between 1024 and 65454 and the last port between 1024 and 65535. The minimum range is 80. If the RTP Video Ports Range is enabled, audio will use the range defined by the RTP Ports Range settings, and other media data will use the range defined by the RTP Video Ports Range settings. The two ranges must not overlap. A change in the setting will take effect on new calls. Note that the device uses another default RTP Video Port Range for Webex meetings and Webex optimized calls. The RTP range for Webex meetings and Webex optimised calls is defined in the RTP Video Ports Range Webex Start/Stop and RTP Video Ports Range Webex Start/Stop settings.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration RTP Video Ports Range Stop: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RTP.Video.Ports.Range.Stop.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RTP.Video.Ports.Range.Webex.Start`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the first port in the range of RTP video ports for Webex meetings. The device is using the ports in the range defined by the RTP Video Ports Range Webex Start and Stop settings for RTP and RTCP media data. The minimum range is 80. A change in the setting will take effect on new calls.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RTP.Video.Ports.Range.Webex.Start.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.807 xConfiguration RoomAnalytics PeoplePresenceDetector

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RoomAnalytics.PeoplePresenceDetector`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The device has the capability to find whether people are present in the room and report the result in the RoomAnalytics PeoplePresence status. The device will not keep record of who was in the room, only whether there are people present in the room. Use the RoomAnalytics PeoplePresence Input Ultrasound and RoomAnalytics PeoplePresence Input HeadDetector settings to specify whether to base the people presence detection on ultrasound, head detection, or both. Ultrasound signals for presence detection are not emitted when both this setting and the Standby WakeupOnMotionDetection Mode setting are switched Off. The Audio Ultrasound MaxVolume and Proximity Mode settings has no effect on presence detection.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration RoomAnalytics PeoplePresenceDetector: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RoomAnalytics.PeoplePresenceDetector.set(<value>)`

### 2.808 xConfiguration RoomAnalytics ReverberationTime Interval

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RoomAnalytics.ReverberationTime.Interval`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Defines how often the RT60 will be measured and reported to the RoomAnalytics status. The interval is in seconds. The RoomAnalytics ReverberationTime Mode configuration must be enabled to set the interval.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration RoomAnalytics ReverberationTime Interval: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RoomAnalytics.ReverberationTime.Interval.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.809 xConfiguration RoomAnalytics ReverberationTime Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RoomAnalytics.ReverberationTime.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Reverberation time is a measure of how fast a sound will "fade away" or decay in a room. This is highly related to the perception of the acoustic quality of a room. The Cisco devices are capable of measuring the reverberation time, RT60, directly from the acoustic echo canceller. As opposed to traditional reverberation time measurement where it is required to emit a noise or impulse signal in the room, the Cisco device will measure RT60 as a "silent measurement". Due to the silent measurement behavior, the RT60 values will be indicative and not strictly correct according to the ISO 3382-2 standard. The measurements will measure the RT60 values for each octave band from 125 Hz to 4 kHz.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration RoomAnalytics ReverberationTime Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RoomAnalytics.ReverberationTime.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.813 xConfiguration RoomAnalytics T3AlarmDetection Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/RoomAnalytics.T3AlarmDetection.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

T3 alarm detection allows the device to recognize the audio signal of a T3 fire alarm (T3 is the industry-standard alarm pattern in the United States). If an alarm is detected, the RoomAnalytics T3AlarmDetected status changes from False to True. Important: It is not guaranteed that the device will detect an alarm. For example, low microphone levels will block detection. Therefore, you should not rely on this feature to raise awareness of an alarm and it does not replace any other safety and security measures and documentation.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration RoomAnalytics T3AlarmDetection Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.RoomAnalytics.T3AlarmDetection.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

This setting will soon be deprecated. We recommend you start using the AdhocBooking BookingTimeout setting instead. The scheduler will provide immediate feedback to a user when they book a room or a device; however, the calendar service can take some time to confirm the booking. If it takes too long to get the confirmation and this time exceeds the value set here, the booking will be cleared, and the device or room will be shown as available. This is applicable to devices registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices.

The room scheduling feature allows you to book a room directly from the touch controller that is in the meeting room. You can also extend an ongoing meeting if the room is still available. You can also use the Webex Assistant (voice-driven virtual assistant) to book or extend a meeting. The room scheduling feature requires that the device is registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices. In addition, the room must be set up with a calendar service that allows booking. The room scheduling feature is not supported on personal mode devices.

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

The ICE protocol needs some time to reach a conclusion about which media route to use (up to the first 5 seconds of a call). During this period media for the device will be sent to the Default Candidate as defined in this setting.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.SIP.Ice.DefaultCandidate.set(<value>)`

### 2.827 xConfiguration SIP Ice Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/SIP.Ice.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment, RFC 5245) is a NAT traversal solution that the devices can use to discover the optimized media path. Thus the shortest route for audio and video is always secured between the devices. Initially STUN (Session Traversal Utilities for NAT) messages are exchanged when setting up the media path. Note that STUN also, regardless of the SIP Ice Mode, is used as a keep-alive mechanism to refresh NAT bindings.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration SIP Ice Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.SIP.Ice.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.831 xConfiguration SIP TlsVerify

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/SIP.TlsVerify`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Before establishing a connection over SIP TLS, the device checks if the certificate of the peer is signed by a trusted Certificate Authority (CA). The CA must be included in the CA list that is manually uploaded to the device using the web interface or API. The list of pre-installed certificates is not used to validate certificates for SIP TLS connections. Note: The value is set to Off for a device that has been upgraded to CE9.9 (or later) from CE9.8 or earlier software versions, provided that the device has not been factory reset after the upgrade, and that the setting was not explicitly set to On. Use the SIP MinimumTLSVersion setting to specify which TLS versions are allowed.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration SIP TlsVerify: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.SIP.TlsVerify.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.832 xConfiguration SIP TransportSecurity CertificateVerificationMode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/SIP.TransportSecurity.CertificateVerificationMode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This configuration determines the method used to validate X.509 Certificates from remote SIP servers when connecting over TLS without a proxy. It is assumed that the following configurations are set to: SIP DefaultTransport: Tls SIP TlsVerify: On SIP ListenPort: Off Provisioning WebexCalling Mode: Off SIP Proxy N Address: "" SIP Type: Standard The validation process affects outgoing calls from the device. Any incoming call will be automatically rejected. Relevant Root CA Certificates need to be uploaded to the device. See the following command to upload CA certificates: xCommand Security Certificates CA Add It is recommended to reboot the device if this xConfiguration is changed. As a security measure, it is also recommended to set xConfiguration Conference Encryption Mode: On to make sure that media gets encrypted.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration SIP TransportSecurity CertificateVerificationMode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.SIP.TransportSecurity.CertificateVerificationMode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.845 xConfiguration Security Fips Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Security.Fips.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

If required, you can set the device in FIPS mode (Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) Publication 140-3, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules). While in FIPS mode Digest access authentication is not supported between the device and an HTTP Proxy because Digest access authentication is using MD5 cryptographic hashing, which is not allowed in FIPS. You should allow only HTTPS, and don't switch on SNMP or IEEE8021X in FIPS mode (keep the default values). For changes to this setting to take full effect, you must restart the device.

#### Usage Syntax

The device can transmit a radar signal and receive reflections from near-by objects. The device can use these signals to detect if there are people and motion in the room. When using radar, the radar doesn't detect people that are further from the device than 5 meter.

The device is equipped with a built-in ultrasonic transceiver sensor that detects the presence of people nearby. ### 2.860 xConfiguration SerialPort Outbound Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/SerialPort.Outbound.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

You can set up your device to control third-party peripherals, such as displays, video switches, projectors, or other, via a serial connection. We refer to this as outbound serial control. Note that outbound serial control is supported on Room Panorama, but not on Room 70 Panorama. You must connect the peripheral to a USB-A port on the device using a USB-to-Serial dongle. You cannot use the built-in serial port on Codec Pro and Room Panorama, or the micro-USB maintenance port on other devices for outbound control; these ports are reserved for inbound control. The communication between the device and peripheral is connectionless, meaning we don't establish a persistent serial port connection between them. The connection is first established when issuing the SerialPort PeripheralControl Send command, and the connection is dropped once the command is finished. These serial connection parameters are not configurable: Data bits (8), Stop bits (1), Flow control (None). Baud rate and parity is set in the SerialPort Outbound Port [1] Baudrate and SerialPort Outbound Port [1] Parity settings, respectively.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration SerialPort Outbound Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.SerialPort.Outbound.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Set the serial port outbound baud rate (data transmission rate). Refer to the SerialPort Outbound Mode setting for more information about outbound serial control. Outbound serial control is not supported on Room 70 Panorama. This configuration has no effect on the regular (inbound) serial port / maintenance port.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration SerialPort Outbound Port[1] BaudRate: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.SerialPort.Outbound.Port[1].BaudRate.set(<value>)`

Specify how long the device must remain in the previous standby state before transitioning to deep sleep. By default, the previous standby state will be networked standby. If networked standby is disabled, the device will default to a display-off state.

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby Level DeepSleep Delay: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.Level.DeepSleep.Delay.set(<value>)`

### 2.873 xConfiguration Standby Level DeepSleep Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Standby.Level.DeepSleep.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Configures the deep sleep standby mode. Deep sleep is an ultra-low power mode where the device shuts down most functionalities and disconnects from the network to conserve energy. When enabled, the device transitions to deep sleep after remaining in networked standby for a specified duration, as defined by the Standby Level DeepSleep Delay setting. If networked standby is disabled, the delay timer begins when the device enters the display-off state. The device will not enter deep sleep mode if motion is detected, provided the Standby WakeupOnMotionDetection feature is enabled, which is the default setting. Additionally, the device will wake up once every night to check for software updates. If office hours are enabled, the device will also wake up at a randomized time between 20 to 40 minutes before the configured office hours start time.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby Level DeepSleep Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.Level.DeepSleep.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Standby.Level.Networked.Delay`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define for how long the device must be in the display off standby mode before it goes into networked standby. If the delay is set to 0, the device goes from halfwake mode, via a few seconds in display off mode, and then to networked standby.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby Level Networked Delay: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.Level.Networked.Delay.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Standby.Level.Networked.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Disable/enable the automatic transition from display off to networked standby mode. Networked standby mode is a deeper level of standby which reduces power consumption further than the regular display off standby mode. The device will enter networked standby after it has been in display off standby mode, for x minutes, as defined in the Standby Level Networked Delay setting. The Standby Control setting must be set to On for standby mode to be automatically initiated; however, you can trigger it manually with the Standby Activate command.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby Level Networked Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.Level.Networked.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.877 xConfiguration Standby Signage InteractionMode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Standby.Signage.InteractionMode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Decide whether to allow users to interact with a digital signage web page. The Interactive mode requires that the device has a touch screen (either built-in or connected).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby Signage InteractionMode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.Signage.InteractionMode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.878 xConfiguration Standby Signage Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Standby.Signage.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Content from a URL (a web page) can replace the traditional halfwake background image and information. This feature is called digital signage. Users can interact with the web page if the device has an interactive screen, for example click on a link or enter text in a form. The use of digital signage does not prevent the device from entering standby the normal way. Therefore, the Standby Delay setting determines for how long the digital signage is shown before the device goes into standby.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby Signage Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.Signage.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.879 xConfiguration Standby Signage RefreshInterval

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Standby.Signage.RefreshInterval`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Trigger a web page to refresh at regular intervals (in seconds). This is useful for web pages that are not able to refresh themselves. It is not recommended to set a refresh interval with the interactive mode.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby Signage RefreshInterval: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.Signage.RefreshInterval.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Standby.Signage.RoomScheduler.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Enables or disables the digital signage feature on Room Scheduler. Content from a URL (a web page) can display on room scheduler enabled devices. The use of digital signage is disabled when outside of office hours and does not enable a traditional halfwake at any time.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby Signage RoomScheduler Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.Signage.RoomScheduler.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Chooses whether the device wakes up automatically when a meeting is scheduled to start. If no one joins the meeting or otherwise interacts with the device, it goes to halfwake and then standby a few minutes after the scheduled start.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby WakeupAtMeetingStart: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.WakeupAtMeetingStart.set(<value>)`

### 2.885 xConfiguration Standby WakeupOnMotionDetection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Standby.WakeupOnMotionDetection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When Wake Up on Motion Detection is enabled, the device automatically wakes up and enters halfwake mode when it detects people entering the room. This feature allows the device to detect when people enter the room. When motion is detected, the system will go from Standby to Halfwake, unless a meeting is scheduled at the time of motion detection. In that case, the system will go from Standby to Awake. This feature primarily uses ultrasound for detection, and for specific products like the Board Pro and Board Pro G2, it also uses radar when in standby modes. The Audio Ultrasound MaxVolume and Proximity Mode settings has no effect on motion detection.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby WakeupOnMotionDetection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.WakeupOnMotionDetection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.886 xConfiguration Standby WakeupOnMotionDetection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Standby.WakeupOnMotionDetection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When Wake Up on Motion Detection is enabled, the device automatically wakes up and enters halfwake mode when it detects people entering the room. This feature allows the device to detect when people enter the room. When motion is detected, the system will go from Standby to Halfwake, unless a meeting is scheduled at the time of motion detection. In that case, the system will go from Standby to Awake. This feature primarily uses ultrasound for detection, and for specific products like the Board Pro and Board Pro G2, it also uses radar when in standby modes. The Audio Ultrasound MaxVolume and Proximity Mode settings has no effect on motion detection.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Standby WakeupOnMotionDetection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Standby.WakeupOnMotionDetection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.888 xConfiguration SystemUnit BroadcastName

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/SystemUnit.BroadcastName`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

A broadcast name is the name that other devices, such as laptops and mobile phones, will see in their scan lists for services such as Airplay, Miracast, and Bluetooth. You can specify a specific broadcast name with this setting. If you don't specifically set a broadcast name here, the scan lists will include the Webex DisplayName if the device is registered to the Webex cloud service, and the SystemUnit Name if registered to an on-premises service. If neither of these names are set, the product type (id) will be displayed. We recommend you not include PII (personally identifiable information) in a broadcast name.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration SystemUnit BroadcastName: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.SystemUnit.BroadcastName.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

If the device crashes, the device can automatically send logs to the Cisco Automatic Crash Report tool (ACR) for analyses. Refer to the SystemUnit CrashReporting Mode setting for more details.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.SystemUnit.CrashReporting.Host.set(<value>)`

### 2.890 xConfiguration SystemUnit CrashReporting Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/SystemUnit.CrashReporting.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

If the device crashes, the device can automatically send logs to the Cisco Automatic Crash Report tool (ACR) for analyses. For devices that are registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices, automatic crash reporting is available for all devices. PII information is removed or anonymised before sending the logs to the Webex cloud. For devices that are registered to an on-premises service such as CUCM, automatic crash reporting is only for Cisco-internal devices. The crash report is sent to the URL given in the SystemUnit CrashReporting URL setting.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration SystemUnit CrashReporting Mode: <value>`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.895 xConfiguration SystemUnit GovernmentDevice

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/SystemUnit.GovernmentDevice`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Specifies whether the device is deployed in a government environment. When set to True, the device enables configurations that comply with government cloud operation standards, ensuring all services operate under government-compliant security and operational policies. This includes activating features and settings required for compliance with regulations such as FedRAMP and FIPS 140-3, which govern secure cloud connectivity and cryptographic standards for government use.

Webex Assistant allows you to control the device by using voice commands. Webex Assistant is a cloud service, so the device must either be registered to the Webex cloud service or registered to an on-premises service and linked to Webex Edge for Devices. Use this setting to enable or disable the Webex Assistant on the device.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserInterface Assistant Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserInterface.Assistant.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.921 xConfiguration UserInterface Assistant ProactiveMeetingJoin

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Proactive Join is a feature that is offered by Webex Assistant. When Proactive Join is enabled and someone is discovered in the meeting room just before the start of an OBTP-meeting, the device will ask if they want to join the meeting that is about to start. Use this setting to enable or disable the Proactive Join feature on the device.

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

When enabled, users can use the Microsoft Teams button to join Teams meetings via CVI by entering the Video Conference ID and passcode from the meeting invite. - **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserInterface.Features.Call.JoinMicrosoftTeamsCVI.set(<value>)`

Set the URL of the web application you want to run on the Room Navigator (that is, a persistent web app). The application displays on the entire screen, and it can't be dismissed by the user. If the app is going to interact with the device's API, remember to set Security Xapi WebSocket ApiKey Allowed: True, and add the domain name of the server hosting the app to the allow list in the WebEngine Features Xapi Peripherals AllowedHosts Hosts setting. Note: Persistent web apps are only available on Room Navigators that are paired to the device over the network.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserInterface HomeScreen Peripherals WebApp URL: <value>`

### 2.986 xConfiguration UserInterface Kiosk Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/UserInterface.Kiosk.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Kiosk mode lets you replace the home screen of the device with your own custom web application that you host and maintain yourself. The URL to the custom web application must be added in the UserInterface Kiosk URL setting. As an example, Kiosk mode can be used in reception areas where you want the device set up for visitor registration, providing the facility overview, or allow direct calls to expert services. Kiosk mode is using the device's web engine, so the WebEngine Mode setting must be On for kiosk mode to work. To allow for making calls, the WebEngine Features SipUrlHandler setting must be On as well.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserInterface Kiosk Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserInterface.Kiosk.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserInterface Kiosk URL: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserInterface.Kiosk.URL.set(<value>)`

Collaborative annotation on a whiteboard shared by someone else is only available for Webex (converged) meetings, and only for devices that are registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices. #### Usage Syntax

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserInterface.LiveAnnotation.Enabled.set(<value>)`

### 2.995 xConfiguration UserInterface MeetingJoin CVITenants

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/UserInterface.MeetingJoin.CVITenants`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the default hostname/tenant key to be used for Microsoft Teams meetings when the device is set up to use CVI (Cloud Video Interop). This hostname, which identifies the organization hosting the meeting, is combined with the video conference ID to generate the full SIP URI for the meeting. In the following examples, the video conference ID is 123456. If UserInterface MeetingJoin CVITenants is set to "tenant@m.webex.com", the URI becomes 123456.tenant@m.webex.com. If UserInterface MeetingJoin CVITenants is set to "vc.example.com", the URI becomes 123456@vc.example.com.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserInterface MeetingJoin CVITenants: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserInterface.MeetingJoin.CVITenants.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1015 xConfiguration UserInterface RoomScheduler State Available Color

This setting applies when a Room Navigator is set up as a room booking device (also referred to as scheduler mode). You can change the color of the LED strip and the room status icon on Room Navigators. The chosen color is applied to both the LED strip and the room status icon. This setting determines which color to use when the room is available. Use the UserInterface RoomScheduler State Busy Color and UserInterface RoomScheduler State Pending Color settings to choose which colors to use when the room is occupied, or booked without being occupied, respectively.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserInterface RoomScheduler State Available Color: <value>`

This setting applies when a Room Navigator is set up as a room booking device (also referred to as scheduler mode). This setting determines which color to use when the room is occupied. Use the UserInterface RoomScheduler State Available Color and UserInterface RoomScheduler State Pending Color settings to choose which colors to use when the room is available, or booked without being occupied, respectively.

If not password protected, anyone can access these settings and also factory reset the device. If password protected, all settings that require authentication have a padlock symbol. Refer to the UserInterface SettingsMenu Visibility if you want to remove the control panel (including the device settings panel) from the user interface.

### 2.1032 xConfiguration UserManagement LDAP Admin Filter

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/UserManagement.LDAP.Admin.Filter`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The LDAP filter is used to determine which users should be granted administrator privileges. You always have to set either an LDAP Admin Group or an LDAP Admin Filter. An LDAP Admin Filter takes precedence, so if the UserManagement LDAP Admin Filter is set, the UserManagement LDAP Admin Group setting is ignored.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserManagement LDAP Admin Filter: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserManagement.LDAP.Admin.Filter.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1033 xConfiguration UserManagement LDAP Admin Group

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/UserManagement.LDAP.Admin.Group`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Members of this group will be given administrator access. This setting is a shorthand for saying (memberOf:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:=<group name>). You must always set either an LDAP Admin Group or an LDAP Admin Filter. An LDAP Admin Filter takes precedence, so if the UserManagement LDAP Admin Filter is set, the UserManagement LDAP Admin Group setting is ignored.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserManagement LDAP Admin Group: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserManagement.LDAP.Admin.Group.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1041 xConfiguration UserManagement LDAP Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/UserManagement.LDAP.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The device supports the use of an LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) server as a central place to store and validate usernames and passwords. Use this setting to configure whether or not to use LDAP authentication. Our implementation is tested for the Microsoft Active Directory (AD) service. If you switch on LDAP Mode, make sure to configure the other UserManagement LDAP settings to suit your setup. Here is a few examples. Example 1: - UserManagement LDAP Mode: On - UserManagement LDAP Address: "192.0.2.20" - UserManagement LDAP BaseDN: "DC=company, DC=com" - UserManagement LDAP Admin Group: "CN=admin group, OU=company groups, DC=company, DC=com" Example 2: - UserManagement LDAP Mode: On - UserManagement LDAP Address: "192.0.2.20" - UserManagement LDAP BaseDN: "DC=company, DC=com" - UserManagement LDAP Admin Filter: "(|(memberof=CN=admin group, OU=company groups, DC=company, DC=com)(sAMAccountName=username))"

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserManagement LDAP Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserManagement.LDAP.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

When signing in to the device as a local user, the password must follow the rules set by the UserManagement PasswordPolicy settings. These settings replace the "systemtools securitysetting" command that was available in software versions older than CE9.10. A new password rule will not apply to existing passwords but will take effect on the next password change. This setting specifies the minimum number of numerical characters (0..9) in the password.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserManagement PasswordPolicy Complexity MinimumDigits: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserManagement.PasswordPolicy.Complexity.MinimumDigits.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1046 xConfiguration UserManagement PasswordPolicy Complexity MinimumEntropy

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/UserManagement.PasswordPolicy.Complexity.MinimumEntropy`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When signing in to the device as a local user, the password must follow the rules set by the UserManagement PasswordPolicy settings. These settings replace the "systemtools securitysetting" command that was available in software versions older than CE9.10. A new password rule will not apply to existing passwords but will take effect on the next password change. This setting specifies the minimum password strength using entropy calculation.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration UserManagement PasswordPolicy Complexity MinimumEntropy: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.UserManagement.PasswordPolicy.Complexity.MinimumEntropy.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1057 xConfiguration Video Input AirPlay Beacon

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.AirPlay.Beacon`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Turn on discovery beacon support. The discovery beacon makes AirPlay deployment easier in environments where the video device and the iPhone, iPad, or Mac are not guaranteed to be on the same broadcast domain (VLAN or subnet). This is typically the case in enterprise network set ups. Beacon discovery requires Bluetooth®. On Desk Series, Board Pro, Board Pro G2, Room Bar, and Room Bar Pro, you must enable Bluetooth with the dedicated Bluetooth Allowed and Bluetooth Enabled settings. On devices that don't have dedicated Bluetooth settings, Bluetooth is automatically enabled when you turn on the discovery beacon. This setting isn't on the first generation of Board (non S-series) because these devices don't support AirPlay.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input AirPlay Beacon: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.AirPlay.Beacon.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1065 xConfiguration Video Input CameraConfigMode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.CameraConfigMode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting applies only when connecting a Precision 60, PTZ-12, or PTZ 4K camera as a second or third camera to the device. When connecting an extra camera to a device, several settings must be changed accordingly. This can be done manually, one setting at a time, or automatically when the device detects that a camera is connected. In automatic mode these settings will be applied (n is the connector that the camera is connected to). Video Input Connector [n] CameraControl CameraId: n Video Input Connector [n] CameraControl Mode: On Video Input Connector [n] InputSourceType: camera Video Input Connector [n] PresentationSelection: Manual Video Input Connector [n] Quality: Motion If the Cameras Camera [n] AssignedSerialNumber setting has been applied, the settings above will not be pushed even if the CameraConfigMode is set to Auto. In general, this happens when EDID information is not available, and thereby prevents the device from detecting that a camera is connected. In this case the device issues a warning. Also, don't use Auto mode if the Cameras Camera n DetectedConnector status doesn't correspond to the input connector number (n). Example: If camera 2 is connected to HDMI [2], then only use Auto mode if the Cameras Camera 2 DetectedConnector status returns 2. If these numbers don't match, you must use the Cameras Camera [n] AssignedSerialNumber setting instead.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input CameraConfigMode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.CameraConfigMode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Select which type of input source is connected to the video input. If the device has an integrated camera, Connector 1 refers to the integrated camera.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[10].Name.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1068 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[10] PresentationSelection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[10].PresentationSelection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define how the video device will behave when you connect a presentation source to the video input. If the device is in standby mode, it will wake up when you connect a presentation source. Sharing the presentation with the far end requires additional action (select Share on the user interface) except when this setting is set to AutoShare. For devices with more than one camera: Any input source can be used as a presentation source; usually, the main camera will not be used as a presentation source. For devices with an integrated camera: The integrated camera is not available as a presentation source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[10] PresentationSelection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[10].PresentationSelection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1069 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[10] Quality

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[10].Quality`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When encoding and transmitting video there is a trade-off between high resolution and high frame rate. For some video sources it is more important to transmit high frame rate than high resolution and vice versa. This setting specifies whether to give priority to high frame rate or to high resolution. If a Quad Camera, SpeakerTrack 60 camera, or Precision 60 camera is detected by the device this setting is automatically set to Motion. If a user changes this setting manually, it will be set back to Motion after a restart or a camera reconnect.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[10] Quality: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[10].Quality.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Define the visibility of the video input connector in the menus and buttons on the user interface. For devices with an integrated camera: Connector 1 is the device's integrated camera and is not available as a presentation source.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[10].Visibility.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1081 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] CEC Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[1].CEC.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video input (HDMI) supports Consumer Electronics Control (CEC). When this setting is enabled, information about the connected device (for example device type and device name) is available in the video device status (Video Input Connector [n] ConnectedDevice CEC [n]), provided that the connected device also supports CEC. If you have Quad Camera, do not switch off CEC on that connector because then there will be no sound on the speakers on the camera. CEC is required for HDMI ARC (Audio Return Channel), which is the channel used for sending audio from the video device to the camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] CEC Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[1].CEC.Mode.set(<value>)`

### 2.1091 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] HDCP Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[1].HDCP.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

One of the video device's HDMI inputs can be configured to support HDCP protected content (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection, version 1.4). This allows customers to re-purpose a video device's screen by connecting devices such as a DVD player, Google ChromeCast, AppleTV, or an HDTV decoder. This type of content cannot be shared while in a call. When the input connector is set up to support HDCP, the following restrictions apply: You can't share any content from this input while in a call. However, you can share both HDCP protected content and non-protected content locally. You can't take web snapshots of this source. To be able to show HDCP protected content on the device's screen, also ensure that the Video Output Connector [n] HDCPPolicy configuration is set correctly and that the screen itself supports HDCP.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] HDCP Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[1].HDCP.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1096 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] MaxResolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[1].MaxResolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the preferred maximum resolution for a video input. Any content shared on this input will have this resolution and framerate, or lower. By setting a MaxResolution you can avoid unnecessary upscaling and achieve the exact resolution you intend. For example, on video inputs that support 4K, you can limit the preferred resolution to avoid automatic 4K upscaling.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] MaxResolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[1].MaxResolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1102 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] PreferredResolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[1].PreferredResolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the preferred screen resolution and refresh rate that the video device advertises to the connected input sources (for example a laptop). The logic for selection of the resolution on the source side will choose this resolution and refresh rate automatically, unless it is overridden manually by the source device (for example the laptop's display configuration software). Note that larger formats than 1920_1080_60 use much more data, and requires a presentation cable (or adapter) that is qualified for at least HDMI 1.4b data rates.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] PreferredResolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[1].PreferredResolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1105 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] PresentationSelection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[1].PresentationSelection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define how the video device will behave when you connect a presentation source to the video input. If the device is in standby mode, it will wake up when you connect a presentation source. Sharing the presentation with the far end requires additional action (select Share on the user interface) except when this setting is set to AutoShare. For devices with more than one camera: Any input source can be used as a presentation source; usually, the main camera will not be used as a presentation source. For devices with an integrated camera: The integrated camera is not available as a presentation source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] PresentationSelection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[1].PresentationSelection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1106 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] PresentationSelection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[1].PresentationSelection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define how the video device will behave when you connect a presentation source to the video input. If the device is in standby mode, it will wake up when you connect a presentation source. Sharing the presentation with the far end requires additional action (select Share on the user interface) except when this setting is set to AutoShare. For devices with more than one camera: Any input source can be used as a presentation source; usually, the main camera will not be used as a presentation source. For devices with an integrated camera: The integrated camera is not available as a presentation source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] PresentationSelection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[1].PresentationSelection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1107 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] Quality

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[1].Quality`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When encoding and transmitting video there is a trade-off between high resolution and high frame rate. For some video sources it is more important to transmit high frame rate than high resolution and vice versa. This setting specifies whether to give priority to high frame rate or to high resolution. If a Quad Camera, SpeakerTrack 60 camera, or Precision 60 camera is detected by the device this setting is automatically set to Motion. If a user changes this setting manually, it will be set back to Motion after a restart or a camera reconnect.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] Quality: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[1].Quality.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1109 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[1] RGBQuantizationRange

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[1].RGBQuantizationRange`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The devices connected to the video input should follow the rules for RGB video quantization range defined in CTA-861. Unfortunately some devices do not follow the standard and this configuration may be used to override the settings to get a perfect image with any source.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[1].RGBQuantizationRange.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1115 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] CEC Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[2].CEC.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video input (HDMI) supports Consumer Electronics Control (CEC). When this setting is enabled, information about the connected device (for example device type and device name) is available in the video device status (Video Input Connector [n] ConnectedDevice CEC [n]), provided that the connected device also supports CEC. If you have Quad Camera, do not switch off CEC on that connector because then there will be no sound on the speakers on the camera. CEC is required for HDMI ARC (Audio Return Channel), which is the channel used for sending audio from the video device to the camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] CEC Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[2].CEC.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1122 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] HDCP Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[2].HDCP.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

One of the video device's HDMI inputs can be configured to support HDCP protected content (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection, version 1.4). This allows customers to re-purpose a video device's screen by connecting devices such as a DVD player, Google ChromeCast, AppleTV, or an HDTV decoder. This type of content cannot be shared while in a call. When the input connector is set up to support HDCP, the following restrictions apply: You can't share any content from this input while in a call. However, you can share both HDCP protected content and non-protected content locally. You can't take web snapshots of this source. To be able to show HDCP protected content on the device's screen, also ensure that the Video Output Connector [n] HDCPPolicy configuration is set correctly and that the screen itself supports HDCP.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] HDCP Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[2].HDCP.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Select which type of input source is connected to the video input. If the device has an integrated camera, Connector 1 refers to the integrated camera.

### 2.1125 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] MaxResolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[2].MaxResolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the preferred maximum resolution for a video input. Any content shared on this input will have this resolution and framerate, or lower. By setting a MaxResolution you can avoid unnecessary upscaling and achieve the exact resolution you intend. For example, on video inputs that support 4K, you can limit the preferred resolution to avoid automatic 4K upscaling.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] MaxResolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[2].MaxResolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1133 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] PreferredResolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[2].PreferredResolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the preferred screen resolution and refresh rate that the video device advertises to the connected input sources (for example a laptop). The logic for selection of the resolution on the source side will choose this resolution and refresh rate automatically, unless it is overridden manually by the source device (for example the laptop's display configuration software). Note that larger formats than 1920_1080_60 use much more data, and requires a presentation cable (or adapter) that is qualified for at least HDMI 1.4b data rates.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] PreferredResolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[2].PreferredResolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1138 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] PresentationSelection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[2].PresentationSelection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define how the video device will behave when you connect a presentation source to the video input. If the device is in standby mode, it will wake up when you connect a presentation source. Sharing the presentation with the far end requires additional action (select Share on the user interface) except when this setting is set to AutoShare. For devices with more than one camera: Any input source can be used as a presentation source; usually, the main camera will not be used as a presentation source. For devices with an integrated camera: The integrated camera is not available as a presentation source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] PresentationSelection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[2].PresentationSelection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1141 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] Quality

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[2].Quality`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When encoding and transmitting video there is a trade-off between high resolution and high frame rate. For some video sources it is more important to transmit high frame rate than high resolution and vice versa. This setting specifies whether to give priority to high frame rate or to high resolution. If a Quad Camera, SpeakerTrack 60 camera, or Precision 60 camera is detected by the device this setting is automatically set to Motion. If a user changes this setting manually, it will be set back to Motion after a restart or a camera reconnect.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[2] Quality: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[2].Quality.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1147 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] AssignedSerialNumber

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[3].AssignedSerialNumber`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

AssignedSerialNumber represents the unique serial number assigned to each video input connector. By default, for USB cameras, this input assignment is automatic and based on the order of device connection. As a result, the assigned order may change after a system reboot if the connection order of devices changes. If this is undesirable, the AssignedSerialNumber can be set for a persistent ordering across system reboots.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] AssignedSerialNumber: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[3].AssignedSerialNumber.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1148 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] CEC Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[3].CEC.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video input (HDMI) supports Consumer Electronics Control (CEC). When this setting is enabled, information about the connected device (for example device type and device name) is available in the video device status (Video Input Connector [n] ConnectedDevice CEC [n]), provided that the connected device also supports CEC. If you have Quad Camera, do not switch off CEC on that connector because then there will be no sound on the speakers on the camera. CEC is required for HDMI ARC (Audio Return Channel), which is the channel used for sending audio from the video device to the camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] CEC Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[3].CEC.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[3].HDCP.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

One of the video device's HDMI inputs can be configured to support HDCP protected content (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection, version 1.4). This allows customers to re-purpose a video device's screen by connecting devices such as a DVD player, Google ChromeCast, AppleTV, or an HDTV decoder. This type of content cannot be shared while in a call. When the input connector is set up to support HDCP, the following restrictions apply: You can't share any content from this input while in a call. However, you can share both HDCP protected content and non-protected content locally. You can't take web snapshots of this source. To be able to show HDCP protected content on the device's screen, also ensure that the Video Output Connector [n] HDCPPolicy configuration is set correctly and that the screen itself supports HDCP.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] HDCP Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[3].HDCP.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1156 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] InputSourceType

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[3].InputSourceType`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Select which type of input source is connected to the video input. If the device has an integrated camera, Connector 1 refers to the integrated camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] InputSourceType: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[3].InputSourceType.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1157 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] MaxResolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[3].MaxResolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the preferred maximum resolution for a video input. Any content shared on this input will have this resolution and framerate, or lower. By setting a MaxResolution you can avoid unnecessary upscaling and achieve the exact resolution you intend. For example, on video inputs that support 4K, you can limit the preferred resolution to avoid automatic 4K upscaling.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] MaxResolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[3].MaxResolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1167 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] PreferredResolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[3].PreferredResolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the preferred screen resolution and refresh rate that the video device advertises to the connected input sources (for example a laptop). The logic for selection of the resolution on the source side will choose this resolution and refresh rate automatically, unless it is overridden manually by the source device (for example the laptop's display configuration software). Note that larger formats than 1920_1080_60 use much more data, and requires a presentation cable (or adapter) that is qualified for at least HDMI 1.4b data rates.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] PreferredResolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[3].PreferredResolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1174 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] PresentationSelection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[3].PresentationSelection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define how the video device will behave when you connect a presentation source to the video input. If the device is in standby mode, it will wake up when you connect a presentation source. Sharing the presentation with the far end requires additional action (select Share on the user interface) except when this setting is set to AutoShare. For devices with more than one camera: Any input source can be used as a presentation source; usually, the main camera will not be used as a presentation source. For devices with an integrated camera: The integrated camera is not available as a presentation source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] PresentationSelection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[3].PresentationSelection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1177 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] Quality

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[3].Quality`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When encoding and transmitting video there is a trade-off between high resolution and high frame rate. For some video sources it is more important to transmit high frame rate than high resolution and vice versa. This setting specifies whether to give priority to high frame rate or to high resolution. If a Quad Camera, SpeakerTrack 60 camera, or Precision 60 camera is detected by the device this setting is automatically set to Motion. If a user changes this setting manually, it will be set back to Motion after a restart or a camera reconnect.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] Quality: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[3].Quality.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1178 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] RGBQuantizationRange

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[3].RGBQuantizationRange`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The devices connected to the video input should follow the rules for RGB video quantization range defined in CTA-861. Unfortunately some devices do not follow the standard and this configuration may be used to override the settings to get a perfect image with any source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[3] RGBQuantizationRange: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[3].RGBQuantizationRange.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1183 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] AssignedSerialNumber

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[4].AssignedSerialNumber`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

AssignedSerialNumber represents the unique serial number assigned to each video input connector. By default, for USB cameras, this input assignment is automatic and based on the order of device connection. As a result, the assigned order may change after a system reboot if the connection order of devices changes. If this is undesirable, the AssignedSerialNumber can be set for a persistent ordering across system reboots.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] AssignedSerialNumber: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[4].AssignedSerialNumber.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1184 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] CEC Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[4].CEC.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video input (HDMI) supports Consumer Electronics Control (CEC). When this setting is enabled, information about the connected device (for example device type and device name) is available in the video device status (Video Input Connector [n] ConnectedDevice CEC [n]), provided that the connected device also supports CEC. If you have Quad Camera, do not switch off CEC on that connector because then there will be no sound on the speakers on the camera. CEC is required for HDMI ARC (Audio Return Channel), which is the channel used for sending audio from the video device to the camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] CEC Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[4].CEC.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[4].HDCP.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

One of the video device's HDMI inputs can be configured to support HDCP protected content (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection, version 1.4). This allows customers to re-purpose a video device's screen by connecting devices such as a DVD player, Google ChromeCast, AppleTV, or an HDTV decoder. This type of content cannot be shared while in a call. When the input connector is set up to support HDCP, the following restrictions apply: You can't share any content from this input while in a call. However, you can share both HDCP protected content and non-protected content locally. You can't take web snapshots of this source. To be able to show HDCP protected content on the device's screen, also ensure that the Video Output Connector [n] HDCPPolicy configuration is set correctly and that the screen itself supports HDCP.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] HDCP Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[4].HDCP.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1191 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] InputSourceType

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[4].InputSourceType`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Select which type of input source is connected to the video input. If the device has an integrated camera, Connector 1 refers to the integrated camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] InputSourceType: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[4].InputSourceType.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1192 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] MaxResolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[4].MaxResolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the preferred maximum resolution for a video input. Any content shared on this input will have this resolution and framerate, or lower. By setting a MaxResolution you can avoid unnecessary upscaling and achieve the exact resolution you intend. For example, on video inputs that support 4K, you can limit the preferred resolution to avoid automatic 4K upscaling.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] MaxResolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[4].MaxResolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1198 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] PreferredResolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[4].PreferredResolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the preferred screen resolution and refresh rate that the video device advertises to the connected input sources (for example a laptop). The logic for selection of the resolution on the source side will choose this resolution and refresh rate automatically, unless it is overridden manually by the source device (for example the laptop's display configuration software). Note that larger formats than 1920_1080_60 use much more data, and requires a presentation cable (or adapter) that is qualified for at least HDMI 1.4b data rates.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] PreferredResolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[4].PreferredResolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1202 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] PresentationSelection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[4].PresentationSelection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define how the video device will behave when you connect a presentation source to the video input. If the device is in standby mode, it will wake up when you connect a presentation source. Sharing the presentation with the far end requires additional action (select Share on the user interface) except when this setting is set to AutoShare. For devices with more than one camera: Any input source can be used as a presentation source; usually, the main camera will not be used as a presentation source. For devices with an integrated camera: The integrated camera is not available as a presentation source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] PresentationSelection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[4].PresentationSelection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1203 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] PresentationSelection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[4].PresentationSelection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define how the video device will behave when you connect a presentation source to the video input. If the device is in standby mode, it will wake up when you connect a presentation source. Sharing the presentation with the far end requires additional action (select Share on the user interface) except when this setting is set to AutoShare. For devices with more than one camera: Any input source can be used as a presentation source; usually, the main camera will not be used as a presentation source. For devices with an integrated camera: The integrated camera is not available as a presentation source.

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1205 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] Quality

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[4].Quality`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When encoding and transmitting video there is a trade-off between high resolution and high frame rate. For some video sources it is more important to transmit high frame rate than high resolution and vice versa. This setting specifies whether to give priority to high frame rate or to high resolution. If a Quad Camera, SpeakerTrack 60 camera, or Precision 60 camera is detected by the device this setting is automatically set to Motion. If a user changes this setting manually, it will be set back to Motion after a restart or a camera reconnect.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] Quality: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[4].Quality.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1206 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] RGBQuantizationRange

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[4].RGBQuantizationRange`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The devices connected to the video input should follow the rules for RGB video quantization range defined in CTA-861. Unfortunately some devices do not follow the standard and this configuration may be used to override the settings to get a perfect image with any source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[4] RGBQuantizationRange: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[4].RGBQuantizationRange.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Applies the selected transformation to the video input. A button in the share menu toggles between 'Rotate 180' and 'None' when this option is selected.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[4].Transform.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`
