### 2.1210 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] AssignedSerialNumber

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[5].AssignedSerialNumber`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

AssignedSerialNumber represents the unique serial number assigned to each video input connector. By default, for USB cameras, this input assignment is automatic and based on the order of device connection. As a result, the assigned order may change after a system reboot if the connection order of devices changes. If this is undesirable, the AssignedSerialNumber can be set for a persistent ordering across system reboots.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] AssignedSerialNumber: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[5].AssignedSerialNumber.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1211 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] CEC Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[5].CEC.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video input (HDMI) supports Consumer Electronics Control (CEC). When this setting is enabled, information about the connected device (for example device type and device name) is available in the video device status (Video Input Connector [n] ConnectedDevice CEC [n]), provided that the connected device also supports CEC. If you have Quad Camera, do not switch off CEC on that connector because then there will be no sound on the speakers on the camera. CEC is required for HDMI ARC (Audio Return Channel), which is the channel used for sending audio from the video device to the camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] CEC Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[5].CEC.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The camera ID is a unique identifier of the camera that is connected to this video input. For devices with more than one camera, you can see the currently assigned IDs in the Cameras Camera status.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] CameraControl CameraId: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[5].CameraControl.CameraId.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] PresentationSelection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[5].PresentationSelection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1225 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] Quality

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[5].Quality`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When encoding and transmitting video there is a trade-off between high resolution and high frame rate. For some video sources it is more important to transmit high frame rate than high resolution and vice versa. This setting specifies whether to give priority to high frame rate or to high resolution. If a Quad Camera, SpeakerTrack 60 camera, or Precision 60 camera is detected by the device this setting is automatically set to Motion. If a user changes this setting manually, it will be set back to Motion after a restart or a camera reconnect.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] Quality: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[5].Quality.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1226 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] RGBQuantizationRange

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[5].RGBQuantizationRange`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The devices connected to the video input should follow the rules for RGB video quantization range defined in CTA-861. Unfortunately some devices do not follow the standard and this configuration may be used to override the settings to get a perfect image with any source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] RGBQuantizationRange: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[5].RGBQuantizationRange.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1227 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] Transform

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[5].Transform`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Applies the selected transformation to the video input. A button in the share menu toggles between 'Rotate 180' and 'None' when this option is selected.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] Transform: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[5].Transform.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Define the visibility of the video input connector in the menus and buttons on the user interface. For devices with an integrated camera: Connector 1 is the device's integrated camera and is not available as a presentation source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[5] Visibility: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[5].Visibility.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1229 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] AssignedSerialNumber

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[6].AssignedSerialNumber`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

AssignedSerialNumber represents the unique serial number assigned to each video input connector. By default, for USB cameras, this input assignment is automatic and based on the order of device connection. As a result, the assigned order may change after a system reboot if the connection order of devices changes. If this is undesirable, the AssignedSerialNumber can be set for a persistent ordering across system reboots.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] AssignedSerialNumber: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[6].AssignedSerialNumber.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1230 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] CEC Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[6].CEC.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The video input (HDMI) supports Consumer Electronics Control (CEC). When this setting is enabled, information about the connected device (for example device type and device name) is available in the video device status (Video Input Connector [n] ConnectedDevice CEC [n]), provided that the connected device also supports CEC. If you have Quad Camera, do not switch off CEC on that connector because then there will be no sound on the speakers on the camera. CEC is required for HDMI ARC (Audio Return Channel), which is the channel used for sending audio from the video device to the camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] CEC Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[6].CEC.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1231 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] CameraControl CameraId

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[6].CameraControl.CameraId`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The camera ID is a unique identifier of the camera that is connected to this video input. For devices with more than one camera, you can see the currently assigned IDs in the Cameras Camera status.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] CameraControl CameraId: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[6].CameraControl.CameraId.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1232 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] CameraControl Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[6].CameraControl.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define whether the camera on this video input connector can be controlled or not. Some connectors cannot be controlled (Off is the only available value).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] CameraControl Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[6].CameraControl.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1233 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] HDCP Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[6].HDCP.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

One of the video device's HDMI inputs can be configured to support HDCP protected content (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection, version 1.4). This allows customers to re-purpose a video device's screen by connecting devices such as a DVD player, Google ChromeCast, AppleTV, or an HDTV decoder. This type of content cannot be shared while in a call. When the input connector is set up to support HDCP, the following restrictions apply: You can't share any content from this input while in a call. However, you can share both HDCP protected content and non-protected content locally. You can't take web snapshots of this source. To be able to show HDCP protected content on the device's screen, also ensure that the Video Output Connector [n] HDCPPolicy configuration is set correctly and that the screen itself supports HDCP.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] HDCP Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[6].HDCP.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1236 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] MaxResolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[6].MaxResolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the preferred maximum resolution for a video input. Any content shared on this input will have this resolution and framerate, or lower. By setting a MaxResolution you can avoid unnecessary upscaling and achieve the exact resolution you intend. For example, on video inputs that support 4K, you can limit the preferred resolution to avoid automatic 4K upscaling.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] MaxResolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[6].MaxResolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1241 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] PreferredResolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[6].PreferredResolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define the preferred screen resolution and refresh rate that the video device advertises to the connected input sources (for example a laptop). The logic for selection of the resolution on the source side will choose this resolution and refresh rate automatically, unless it is overridden manually by the source device (for example the laptop's display configuration software). Note that larger formats than 1920_1080_60 use much more data, and requires a presentation cable (or adapter) that is qualified for at least HDMI 1.4b data rates.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] PreferredResolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[6].PreferredResolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[6].PresentationSelection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define how the video device will behave when you connect a presentation source to the video input. If the device is in standby mode, it will wake up when you connect a presentation source. Sharing the presentation with the far end requires additional action (select Share on the user interface) except when this setting is set to AutoShare. For devices with more than one camera: Any input source can be used as a presentation source; usually, the main camera will not be used as a presentation source. For devices with an integrated camera: The integrated camera is not available as a presentation source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[6] PresentationSelection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[6].PresentationSelection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1266 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[8] PresentationSelection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[8].PresentationSelection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Define how the video device will behave when you connect a presentation source to the video input. If the device is in standby mode, it will wake up when you connect a presentation source. Sharing the presentation with the far end requires additional action (select Share on the user interface) except when this setting is set to AutoShare. For devices with more than one camera: Any input source can be used as a presentation source; usually, the main camera will not be used as a presentation source. For devices with an integrated camera: The integrated camera is not available as a presentation source.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[8] PresentationSelection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[8].PresentationSelection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1267 xConfiguration Video Input Connector[8] Quality

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Connector[8].Quality`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When encoding and transmitting video there is a trade-off between high resolution and high frame rate. For some video sources it is more important to transmit high frame rate than high resolution and vice versa. This setting specifies whether to give priority to high frame rate or to high resolution. If a Quad Camera, SpeakerTrack 60 camera, or Precision 60 camera is detected by the device this setting is automatically set to Motion. If a user changes this setting manually, it will be set back to Motion after a restart or a camera reconnect.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Connector[8] Quality: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Connector[8].Quality.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Miracast.Channel.set(<value>)`

### 2.1279 xConfiguration Video Input Miracast MaxBitrate

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the maximum bitrate for Miracast content between the sending device (for example a laptop) and the local video device. This setting is not for transmission between the local device and far end devices in a meeting.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Miracast MaxBitrate: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Miracast.MaxBitrate.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1280 xConfiguration Video Input Miracast Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Miracast.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Miracast allows meeting participants to share content wirelessly from their laptop (Windows or Android) to a video device, without the need for a client. Miracast uses either Wi-Fi Direct to establish a direct network connection from a sending device (typically a meeting participant's laptop) to the video device, or infrastructure, which means using the existing network infrastructure for both signaling (MS-MICE and RTSP) and media. You choose which method to use in the Video Input Miracast Transport setting. Both methods support only the 2.4 GHz band, and use TCP port 7236 for signaling (RTSP) when establishing the connection. In addition, when the connection is via infrastructure, the MS-MICE protocol uses TCP port 7250. For more information about the MS-MICE protocol, refer to Microsoft's documentation. When Miracast is turned on, the video device emits a beacon that near-by devices can pick up (range in the order of 100 meter). The broadcast name that appears in the near-by devices' scan lists depends on the configuration. To be sure not to include any PII (personal identifiable information), you can specifically set a broadcast name with the SystemUnit BroadcastName setting. Otherwise, the scan lists will include the Webex DisplayName if the device is registered to the Webex cloud service, and the SystemUnit Name if registered to an on-premises service. If neither of these names are set, the product type (id) will be displayed. When the connection is via infrastructure, the beacon also contains the video device's IP address and hostname. Because Miracast is using Wi-Fi, it is not supported by non-radio devices. Also, you must remember to connect the Wi-Fi antennas on those products where they are optional. Further, the device must be connected to the network with cable (and have an IP address on the wired network interface).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Miracast Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Miracast.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1281 xConfiguration Video Input Miracast Pin Length

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Miracast.Pin.Length`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the number of digits in the Miracast pin code. Meeting participants must enter this code on their laptop (sending device) when establishing the required Wi-Fi Direct network connection to the video device. The meeting participant must enter the pin code within 30 seconds.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Miracast Pin Length: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Miracast.Pin.Length.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1282 xConfiguration Video Input Miracast PresentationSelection

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Miracast.PresentationSelection`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When a Miracast connection is established, the presentation will be shown automatically on the local screen. If the device is in standby mode, it will wake up. This setting decides whether sharing the presentation with the far end requires additional user action.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Miracast PresentationSelection: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Miracast.PresentationSelection.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1283 xConfiguration Video Input Miracast Quality

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Miracast.Quality`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When encoding and transmitting video there is a trade-off between high resolution and high frame rate. For some content it is more important to transmit high frame rate than high resolution and vice versa. This setting specifies whether to give priority to high frame rate or to high resolution. This setting doesn't have any effect on content shared locally; only on the signal we send to the far end.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Miracast Quality: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Miracast.Quality.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1284 xConfiguration Video Input Miracast Resolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Miracast.Resolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Controls the maximum video resolution offered to the sender device. The packet burstiness of the encoded video stream depends on the resolution. It can be reduced by reducing the maximum resolution, for cases where the network is not able to handle the video stream without packet loss.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Miracast Resolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Miracast.Resolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1285 xConfiguration Video Input Miracast Transport

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Miracast.Transport`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

For Miracast sharing, choose whether the media transport between the sending device (for example a laptop) and the video device should be via a Wi-Fi Direct or infrastructure connection. Only sending devices running Windows 10 v1809 or later support transport via infrastructure. Android devices doesn't support it. The sending device and the video device must be on the same network, or on networks that TCP signaling and UDP media traffic can be routed between. The sending device cannot be on an unencrypted Wi-Fi network. When the connection is via infrastructure, it's recommended that the network infrastructure provides IPv4 ARP / IPv6 NDP anti-spoofing to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Input Miracast Transport: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Input.Miracast.Transport.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1286 xConfiguration Video Monitors

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Monitors`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

A monitor role is assigned to each screen using the Video Output Connector [n] MonitorRole setting. The monitor role decides which layout (call participants and presentation) will appear on the screen that is connected to this output. Screens with the same monitor role will get the same layout; screens with different monitor roles will have different layouts. The monitor layout mode that is set in the Video Monitors setting should reflect the number of different layouts you want in your room setup. Note that some screens can be reserved for presentations.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Monitors: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Monitors.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1293 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] CEC Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..2].CEC.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This video output (HDMI) supports Consumer Electronics Control (CEC). When this setting is On, the video device will use CEC to set the screen in standby when the device itself enters standby. Likewise the device will wake up the screen when the device itself wakes up from standby. The active video input on a screen is sometimes changed by a user. When a call is started the device detects if the active video input has been switched to another input on the screen. The device then switches the input back so the device is the active video input source. If the device is not the active input source when the device goes into standby the screen will not be set to standby. It's a prerequisite that the screen that is connected to the output is CEC compatible and that CEC is enabled on the screen. Note that the different manufacturers uses different marketing names for CEC, for example Anynet+ (Samsung); Aquos Link (Sharp); BRAVIA Sync (Sony); HDMI-CEC (Hitachi); Kuro Link (Pioneer); CE-Link and Regza Link (Toshiba); RIHD (Onkyo); HDAVI Control, EZ-Sync, VIERA Link (Panasonic); EasyLink (Philips); and NetCommand for HDMI (Mitsubishi).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] CEC Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..2].CEC.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1294 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] ContentType

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..2].ContentType`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Decide whether to transmit content type information in the video stream. In most cases, not sending any content type information works best. But if you experience higher latency than expected, you can try setting the content type to Game (lower latency video). However, note that most displays don't check the transmitted content type information.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] ContentType: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..2].ContentType.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

Use this setting if you want to instruct the device to only use the HDCP 1.4 protocol on the output, even if it also supports the newer HDCP 2.2 version. This might be necessary if equipment in the signal chain signals support for HDCP 2.2, without fully supporting it.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..2].HDCPForce1_4.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.1297 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] Location HorizontalOffset

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..2].Location.HorizontalOffset`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

HorizontalOffset and VerticalOffset settings are associated with each video output. These settings are used to signal the relative position of the displays that are connected to these outputs. HorizontalOffset = "0" and VerticalOffset = "0" indicates that the display is positioned in center, both horizontally and vertically. A negative horizontal offset indicates that the monitor is left of center, and a positive horizontal offset indicates that the monitor is right of center. A negative vertical offset indicates that the monitor is below center, and a positive vertical offset indicates that the monitor is above center. The magnitude of the offset indicates how far the display is from center (relative to other displays). Example: You have two screens side by side. The left screen is on Connector 1 and the right screen on Connector 2. Then the following settings will apply: Video Output Connector 1 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "0" Video Output Connector 2 Location: HorizontalOffset = "1", VerticalOffset = "0" Example: You have two screens, one below the other. The upper screen is on Connector 1 and the lower screen on Connector 2. Then the following settings will apply: Video Output Connector 1 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "0" Video Output Connector 2 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "-1" For Board Pro, Board Pro G2, and Desk Pro, the integrated screen (Connector 1) has HorizontalOffset = "0" and VerticalOffset = "0" (implicit, not configurable).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] Location HorizontalOffset: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..2].Location.HorizontalOffset.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1298 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] Location VerticalOffset

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..2].Location.VerticalOffset`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

HorizontalOffset and VerticalOffset settings are associated with each video output. These settings are used to signal the relative position of the displays that are connected to these outputs. HorizontalOffset = "0" and VerticalOffset = "0" indicates that the display is positioned in center, both horizontally and vertically. A negative horizontal offset indicates that the monitor is left of center, and a positive horizontal offset indicates that the monitor is right of center. A negative vertical offset indicates that the monitor is below center, and a positive vertical offset indicates that the monitor is above center. The magnitude of the offset indicates how far the display is from center (relative to other displays). For Board Pro, Board Pro G2, and Desk Pro, the integrated screen (Connector 1) has HorizontalOffset = "0" and VerticalOffset = "0" (implicit, not configurable). Example: You have two screens side by side. The left screen is on Connector 1 and the right screen on Connector 2. Then the following settings will apply: Video Output Connector 1 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "0" Video Output Connector 2 Location: HorizontalOffset = "1", VerticalOffset = "0" Example: You have two screens with one below the other. The upper screen is on Connector 1 and the lower screen on Connector 2. Then the following settings will apply: Video Output Connector 1 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "0" Video Output Connector 2 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "-1"

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] Location VerticalOffset: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..2].Location.VerticalOffset.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1299 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] MonitorRole

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..2].MonitorRole`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The monitor role describes which video streams will be shown on the screen connected to this video output. Together the Video Monitors setting and the MonitorRole settings for all outputs define which layout (video streams) will be shown on each screen.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] MonitorRole: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..2].MonitorRole.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1300 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] RGBQuantizationRange

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..2].RGBQuantizationRange`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Connected HDMI displays should follow the rules for RGB video quantization range defined in CTA-861. Unfortunately some displays do not follow the standard and this configuration may be used to override the settings to get a perfect image with any display.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] RGBQuantizationRange: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..2].RGBQuantizationRange.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1301 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] Resolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..2].Resolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the resolution and refresh rate to be used on an output. If the specified resolution and refresh rate are not supported by the connected screen/display, or this configuration is set to Auto, the output resolution and refresh rate will be the screen's preferred format (as reported in EDID and passed on into the Video Output Connector [n] ConnectedDevice PreferredFormat status. You always find the actual resolution and framerate that is sent in the Video Output Connector [n] Width, Height, an Refreshrate statuses. If you choose a resolution that the connected screen doesn't support, the output format will be the screen's preferred format (as reported in EDID and passed on in the Video Output Connector [n] ConnectedDevice PreferredFormat status. If the device has an integrated screen, Connector [1] refers to this screen. The formats larger than 1920_1200_60 requires use of high quality display cables when connecting an external screen. Some UHD TVs/displays only enable 3840_2160_30 (30 Hz) and not 3840_2160_60 (60 Hz) as their default configuration. In such cases the corresponding setting on the TV/display must be reconfigured to allow 3840_2160_60 for the HDMI input where the device is connected. In auto mode, Codec Pro Connector 3 uses the display’s preferred resolution unless it is set to 3840x2160p30; in that case, it automatically switches to 1920x1080p60.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..2] Resolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..2].Resolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.1302 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..3] CEC Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..3].CEC.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This video output (HDMI) supports Consumer Electronics Control (CEC). When this setting is On, the video device will use CEC to set the screen in standby when the device itself enters standby. Likewise the device will wake up the screen when the device itself wakes up from standby. The active video input on a screen is sometimes changed by a user. When a call is started the device detects if the active video input has been switched to another input on the screen. The device then switches the input back so the device is the active video input source. If the device is not the active input source when the device goes into standby the screen will not be set to standby. It's a prerequisite that the screen that is connected to the output is CEC compatible and that CEC is enabled on the screen. Note that the different manufacturers uses different marketing names for CEC, for example Anynet+ (Samsung); Aquos Link (Sharp); BRAVIA Sync (Sony); HDMI-CEC (Hitachi); Kuro Link (Pioneer); CE-Link and Regza Link (Toshiba); RIHD (Onkyo); HDAVI Control, EZ-Sync, VIERA Link (Panasonic); EasyLink (Philips); and NetCommand for HDMI (Mitsubishi).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..3] CEC Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..3].CEC.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1303 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..3] ContentType

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..3].ContentType`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Decide whether to transmit content type information in the video stream. In most cases, not sending any content type information works best. But if you experience higher latency than expected, you can try setting the content type to Game (lower latency video). However, note that most displays don't check the transmitted content type information.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..3] ContentType: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..3].ContentType.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1304 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..3] HDCPForce1_4

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..3].HDCPForce1_4`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Use this setting if you want to instruct the device to only use the HDCP 1.4 protocol on the output, even if it also supports the newer HDCP 2.2 version. This might be necessary if equipment in the signal chain signals support for HDCP 2.2, without fully supporting it.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..3] HDCPForce1_4: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..3].HDCPForce1_4.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1305 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..3] HDCPPolicy

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1..3].HDCPPolicy`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Some of the video device's HDMI outputs can be set up to allow transmission of HDCP protected content. For HDCP protected content to be displayed on a screen, of course the screen itself must support HDCP as well.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1..3] HDCPPolicy: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1..3].HDCPPolicy.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.1323 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1] Location HorizontalOffset

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1].Location.HorizontalOffset`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

HorizontalOffset and VerticalOffset settings are associated with each video output. These settings are used to signal the relative position of the displays that are connected to these outputs. HorizontalOffset = "0" and VerticalOffset = "0" indicates that the display is positioned in center, both horizontally and vertically. A negative horizontal offset indicates that the monitor is left of center, and a positive horizontal offset indicates that the monitor is right of center. A negative vertical offset indicates that the monitor is below center, and a positive vertical offset indicates that the monitor is above center. The magnitude of the offset indicates how far the display is from center (relative to other displays). Example: You have two screens side by side. The left screen is on Connector 1 and the right screen on Connector 2. Then the following settings will apply: Video Output Connector 1 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "0" Video Output Connector 2 Location: HorizontalOffset = "1", VerticalOffset = "0" Example: You have two screens, one below the other. The upper screen is on Connector 1 and the lower screen on Connector 2. Then the following settings will apply: Video Output Connector 1 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "0" Video Output Connector 2 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "-1" For Board Pro, Board Pro G2, and Desk Pro, the integrated screen (Connector 1) has HorizontalOffset = "0" and VerticalOffset = "0" (implicit, not configurable).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1] Location HorizontalOffset: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1].Location.HorizontalOffset.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1330 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1] RGBQuantizationRange

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1].RGBQuantizationRange`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Connected HDMI displays should follow the rules for RGB video quantization range defined in CTA-861. Unfortunately some displays do not follow the standard and this configuration may be used to override the settings to get a perfect image with any display.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1] RGBQuantizationRange: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1].RGBQuantizationRange.set(<value>)`

### 2.1331 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1] Resolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[1].Resolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the resolution and refresh rate to be used on an output. If the specified resolution and refresh rate are not supported by the connected screen/display, or this configuration is set to Auto, the output resolution and refresh rate will be the screen's preferred format (as reported in EDID and passed on into the Video Output Connector [n] ConnectedDevice PreferredFormat status. You always find the actual resolution and framerate that is sent in the Video Output Connector [n] Width, Height, an Refreshrate statuses. If you choose a resolution that the connected screen doesn't support, the output format will be the screen's preferred format (as reported in EDID and passed on in the Video Output Connector [n] ConnectedDevice PreferredFormat status. If the device has an integrated screen, Connector [1] refers to this screen. The formats larger than 1920_1200_60 requires use of high quality display cables when connecting an external screen. Some UHD TVs/displays only enable 3840_2160_30 (30 Hz) and not 3840_2160_60 (60 Hz) as their default configuration. In such cases the corresponding setting on the TV/display must be reconfigured to allow 3840_2160_60 for the HDMI input where the device is connected. In auto mode, Codec Pro Connector 3 uses the display’s preferred resolution unless it is set to 3840x2160p30; in that case, it automatically switches to 1920x1080p60.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[1] Resolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[1].Resolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.1336 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] CEC Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[2].CEC.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This video output (HDMI) supports Consumer Electronics Control (CEC). When this setting is On, the video device will use CEC to set the screen in standby when the device itself enters standby. Likewise the device will wake up the screen when the device itself wakes up from standby. The active video input on a screen is sometimes changed by a user. When a call is started the device detects if the active video input has been switched to another input on the screen. The device then switches the input back so the device is the active video input source. If the device is not the active input source when the device goes into standby the screen will not be set to standby. It's a prerequisite that the screen that is connected to the output is CEC compatible and that CEC is enabled on the screen. Note that the different manufacturers uses different marketing names for CEC, for example Anynet+ (Samsung); Aquos Link (Sharp); BRAVIA Sync (Sony); HDMI-CEC (Hitachi); Kuro Link (Pioneer); CE-Link and Regza Link (Toshiba); RIHD (Onkyo); HDAVI Control, EZ-Sync, VIERA Link (Panasonic); EasyLink (Philips); and NetCommand for HDMI (Mitsubishi).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] CEC Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[2].CEC.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1339 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] ContentType

Decide whether to transmit content type information in the video stream. In most cases, not sending any content type information works best. But if you experience higher latency than expected, you can try setting the content type to Game (lower latency video). However, note that most displays don't check the transmitted content type information.

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] ContentType: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[2].ContentType.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1340 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] HDCPForce1_4

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[2].HDCPForce1_4`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Use this setting if you want to instruct the device to only use the HDCP 1.4 protocol on the output, even if it also supports the newer HDCP 2.2 version. This might be necessary if equipment in the signal chain signals support for HDCP 2.2, without fully supporting it.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] HDCPForce1_4: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[2].HDCPForce1_4.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1345 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] Location HorizontalOffset

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[2].Location.HorizontalOffset`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

HorizontalOffset and VerticalOffset settings are associated with each video output. These settings are used to signal the relative position of the displays that are connected to these outputs. HorizontalOffset = "0" and VerticalOffset = "0" indicates that the display is positioned in center, both horizontally and vertically. A negative horizontal offset indicates that the monitor is left of center, and a positive horizontal offset indicates that the monitor is right of center. A negative vertical offset indicates that the monitor is below center, and a positive vertical offset indicates that the monitor is above center. The magnitude of the offset indicates how far the display is from center (relative to other displays). Example: You have two screens side by side. The left screen is on Connector 1 and the right screen on Connector 2. Then the following settings will apply: Video Output Connector 1 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "0" Video Output Connector 2 Location: HorizontalOffset = "1", VerticalOffset = "0" Example: You have two screens, one below the other. The upper screen is on Connector 1 and the lower screen on Connector 2. Then the following settings will apply: Video Output Connector 1 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "0" Video Output Connector 2 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "-1" For Board Pro, Board Pro G2, and Desk Pro, the integrated screen (Connector 1) has HorizontalOffset = "0" and VerticalOffset = "0" (implicit, not configurable).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] Location HorizontalOffset: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[2].Location.HorizontalOffset.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1352 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] RGBQuantizationRange

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[2].RGBQuantizationRange`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Connected HDMI displays should follow the rules for RGB video quantization range defined in CTA-861. Unfortunately some displays do not follow the standard and this configuration may be used to override the settings to get a perfect image with any display.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] RGBQuantizationRange: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[2].RGBQuantizationRange.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1353 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] Resolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[2].Resolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the resolution and refresh rate to be used on an output. If the specified resolution and refresh rate are not supported by the connected screen/display, or this configuration is set to Auto, the output resolution and refresh rate will be the screen's preferred format (as reported in EDID and passed on into the Video Output Connector [n] ConnectedDevice PreferredFormat status. You always find the actual resolution and framerate that is sent in the Video Output Connector [n] Width, Height, an Refreshrate statuses. If you choose a resolution that the connected screen doesn't support, the output format will be the screen's preferred format (as reported in EDID and passed on in the Video Output Connector [n] ConnectedDevice PreferredFormat status. If the device has an integrated screen, Connector [1] refers to this screen. The formats larger than 1920_1200_60 requires use of high quality display cables when connecting an external screen. Some UHD TVs/displays only enable 3840_2160_30 (30 Hz) and not 3840_2160_60 (60 Hz) as their default configuration. In such cases the corresponding setting on the TV/display must be reconfigured to allow 3840_2160_60 for the HDMI input where the device is connected. In auto mode, Codec Pro Connector 3 uses the display’s preferred resolution unless it is set to 3840x2160p30; in that case, it automatically switches to 1920x1080p60.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[2] Resolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[2].Resolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.1355 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] CEC Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[3].CEC.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This video output (HDMI) supports Consumer Electronics Control (CEC). When this setting is On, the video device will use CEC to set the screen in standby when the device itself enters standby. Likewise the device will wake up the screen when the device itself wakes up from standby. The active video input on a screen is sometimes changed by a user. When a call is started the device detects if the active video input has been switched to another input on the screen. The device then switches the input back so the device is the active video input source. If the device is not the active input source when the device goes into standby the screen will not be set to standby. It's a prerequisite that the screen that is connected to the output is CEC compatible and that CEC is enabled on the screen. Note that the different manufacturers uses different marketing names for CEC, for example Anynet+ (Samsung); Aquos Link (Sharp); BRAVIA Sync (Sony); HDMI-CEC (Hitachi); Kuro Link (Pioneer); CE-Link and Regza Link (Toshiba); RIHD (Onkyo); HDAVI Control, EZ-Sync, VIERA Link (Panasonic); EasyLink (Philips); and NetCommand for HDMI (Mitsubishi).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] CEC Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[3].CEC.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1358 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] ContentType

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[3].ContentType`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Decide whether to transmit content type information in the video stream. In most cases, not sending any content type information works best. But if you experience higher latency than expected, you can try setting the content type to Game (lower latency video). However, note that most displays don't check the transmitted content type information.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] ContentType: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[3].ContentType.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1359 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] HDCPForce1_4

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[3].HDCPForce1_4`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Use this setting if you want to instruct the device to only use the HDCP 1.4 protocol on the output, even if it also supports the newer HDCP 2.2 version. This might be necessary if equipment in the signal chain signals support for HDCP 2.2, without fully supporting it.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] HDCPForce1_4: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[3].HDCPForce1_4.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Some of the video device's HDMI outputs can be set up to allow transmission of HDCP protected content. For HDCP protected content to be displayed on a screen, of course the screen itself must support HDCP as well.

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] HDCPPolicy: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[3].HDCPPolicy.set(<value>)`

### 2.1361 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] Location HorizontalOffset

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[3].Location.HorizontalOffset`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

HorizontalOffset and VerticalOffset settings are associated with each video output. These settings are used to signal the relative position of the displays that are connected to these outputs. HorizontalOffset = "0" and VerticalOffset = "0" indicates that the display is positioned in center, both horizontally and vertically. A negative horizontal offset indicates that the monitor is left of center, and a positive horizontal offset indicates that the monitor is right of center. A negative vertical offset indicates that the monitor is below center, and a positive vertical offset indicates that the monitor is above center. The magnitude of the offset indicates how far the display is from center (relative to other displays). Example: You have two screens side by side. The left screen is on Connector 1 and the right screen on Connector 2. Then the following settings will apply: Video Output Connector 1 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "0" Video Output Connector 2 Location: HorizontalOffset = "1", VerticalOffset = "0" Example: You have two screens, one below the other. The upper screen is on Connector 1 and the lower screen on Connector 2. Then the following settings will apply: Video Output Connector 1 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "0" Video Output Connector 2 Location: HorizontalOffset = "0", VerticalOffset = "-1" For Board Pro, Board Pro G2, and Desk Pro, the integrated screen (Connector 1) has HorizontalOffset = "0" and VerticalOffset = "0" (implicit, not configurable).

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] Location HorizontalOffset: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[3].Location.HorizontalOffset.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] Location VerticalOffset: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[3].Location.VerticalOffset.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1366 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] MonitorRole

The monitor role describes which video streams will be shown on the screen connected to this video output. Together the Video Monitors setting and the MonitorRole settings for all outputs define which layout (video streams) will be shown on each screen.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[3].MonitorRole.set(<value>)`

### 2.1368 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] RGBQuantizationRange

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[3].RGBQuantizationRange`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Connected HDMI displays should follow the rules for RGB video quantization range defined in CTA-861. Unfortunately some displays do not follow the standard and this configuration may be used to override the settings to get a perfect image with any display.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] RGBQuantizationRange: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[3].RGBQuantizationRange.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1369 xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] Resolution

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.Connector[3].Resolution`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set the resolution and refresh rate to be used on an output. If the specified resolution and refresh rate are not supported by the connected screen/display, or this configuration is set to Auto, the output resolution and refresh rate will be the screen's preferred format (as reported in EDID and passed on into the Video Output Connector [n] ConnectedDevice PreferredFormat status. You always find the actual resolution and framerate that is sent in the Video Output Connector [n] Width, Height, an Refreshrate statuses. If you choose a resolution that the connected screen doesn't support, the output format will be the screen's preferred format (as reported in EDID and passed on in the Video Output Connector [n] ConnectedDevice PreferredFormat status. If the device has an integrated screen, Connector [1] refers to this screen. The formats larger than 1920_1200_60 requires use of high quality display cables when connecting an external screen. Some UHD TVs/displays only enable 3840_2160_30 (30 Hz) and not 3840_2160_60 (60 Hz) as their default configuration. In such cases the corresponding setting on the TV/display must be reconfigured to allow 3840_2160_60 for the HDMI input where the device is connected. In auto mode, Codec Pro Connector 3 uses the display’s preferred resolution unless it is set to 3840x2160p30; in that case, it automatically switches to 1920x1080p60.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output Connector[3] Resolution: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.Connector[3].Resolution.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 2.1373 xConfiguration Video Output HDMI Passthrough Allowed

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.HDMI.Passthrough.Allowed`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

If people connect their laptop to the USB socket of an HDMI-to-USB converter (capturing device) that is connected to one of the device's HDMI outputs, they can use the device's camera and microphone when making calls from their laptop meeting apps. They also need a presentation cable (HDMI) between the laptop and an HDMI input to make use of the device's screen and loudspeakers. This feature is referred to as Call from laptop, Webcam mode, or HDMI passthrough. Which HDMI output the HDMI-to-USB converter is connected to is set with the Video Output HDMI Passthrough OutputConnector setting. You may also want to check that the Video Monitors and Video Output Connector [n] MonitorRole settings are correct.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output HDMI Passthrough Allowed: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.HDMI.Passthrough.Allowed.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1374 xConfiguration Video Output HDMI Passthrough AutoDisconnect Delay

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.HDMI.Passthrough.AutoDisconnect.Delay`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set how long (minutes) the device shall be in HDMI Passthrough mode before it disconnects automatically. This setting only has an effect when Video Output HDMI Passthrough AutoDisconnect Enabled is set to True. Refer to the Video Output HDMI Passthrough Allowed setting for more information about HDMI passthrough and the Call from laptop feature.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output HDMI Passthrough AutoDisconnect Delay: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.HDMI.Passthrough.AutoDisconnect.Delay.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1375 xConfiguration Video Output HDMI Passthrough AutoDisconnect Enabled

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.HDMI.Passthrough.AutoDisconnect.Enabled`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Decide whether the device shall automatically disconnect the HDMI Passthrough after a given delay, for example if the user forgets to disconnect from the touch controller. The delay is set with the Video Output HDMI Passthrough AutoDisconnect Delay. Refer to the Video Output HDMI Passthrough Allowed setting for more information about HDMI passthrough and the Call from laptop feature.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Video Output HDMI Passthrough AutoDisconnect Enabled: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Video.Output.HDMI.Passthrough.AutoDisconnect.Enabled.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Video.Output.HDMI.Passthrough.HdmiUsbConverter.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When using the Call from laptop (HDMI passthrough) feature, users must choose (on their laptops) to use the HDMI-to-USB converter (capturing device) as microphone and camera. With this setting you can customize which name will be displayed in the list of devices to choose from. Refer to the Video Output HDMI Passthrough Allowed setting for more details about Call from laptop.

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

By default, the webengine does not use the network during revocation checks, and thereby is only checking Stapled OCSP responses and built-in CRL lists. On devices that are registered to an on-premises service and linked to Webex Edge for Devices, you can choose whether to upgrade the software from the on-premises provisioning service or from the Webex cloud service (cloud-managed software upgrade). ### 2.1437 xConfiguration Webex Meetings HttpProxyForMedia Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Webex.Meetings.HttpProxyForMedia.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

This setting applies to devices that are registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices with the Webex optimized experience enabled. You can set up the device to use a proxy server for HTTPS and WebSocket traffic, see the NetworkServices HTTP Proxy settings. If the NetworkServices HTTP Proxy Mode is not turned Off, you can choose whether to use this proxy also for media traffic. Using a proxy may lead to lower media quality. To keep media quality as good as possible, the proxy needs to support the bitrates that are used by the deployed devices in the environment, and the total round-trip time from the device to the media server should be as low as possible.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Webex Meetings HttpProxyForMedia Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Webex.Meetings.HttpProxyForMedia.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1438 xConfiguration Webex Meetings JoinProtocol

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Webex.Meetings.JoinProtocol`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Devices that are registered to an on-premises service and linked to Webex Edge for Devices may use the Webex cloud service for calling into Webex meetings. Calling via Webex gives you the full set of native Webex Meetings in-call features, such as advanced mute, cohost, transfer host, and face recognition. These are the cases when Webex Meetings call routing may be used: When using the Join Webex button, when using the Webex Assistant to join a Personal Room meeting (PMR), and when using the Call button or the Dial API command with a URI with one of the following domains: @webex.com, @*.webex.com, and @meet.ciscospark.com. Other calls will use to the default protocol. Also, native Webex Meetings call routing requires that the device is enabled for cloud-managed software upgrade, configuration from Control Hub is enabled, and the Conference Multipoint Mode is set to Auto.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Webex Meetings JoinProtocol: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Webex.Meetings.JoinProtocol.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1439 xConfiguration Webex Meetings MeetingChatNotifications Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Webex.Meetings.MeetingChatNotifications.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Decide how the chat notifications, by default, are displayed on the screen. You can use the UI or the Conference MeetingChatNotification Default command to change the mode both during meetings and between meetings. Shared devices will return to the default behavior set here after every meeting. Personal devices will remember its current mode and keep it until changed from the UI or by using the commands. For more information about chat notifications, refer to the Webex Meetings MeetingChatPreview setting.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Webex Meetings MeetingChatNotifications Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Webex.Meetings.MeetingChatNotifications.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1440 xConfiguration Webex Meetings MeetingChatPreview

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Webex.Meetings.MeetingChatPreview`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Set whether to allow meeting messages (chat) to pop up in a notification on the device's screen during a meeting. This lets the device users see what's happening in the chat. Individual meeting chat notifications remain on screen for 8 seconds. If there is a queue of messages sent around the same time, then they will show for a slightly shorter time of 5 seconds to avoid a big build-up of messages. A chat notification contains a maximum of three lines of text. Chat notifications are only available on devices that are registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices with the Webex optimized experience enabled.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Webex Meetings MeetingChatPreview: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Webex.Meetings.MeetingChatPreview.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1441 xConfiguration Webex Privacy AllowUsageDataLogging

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Webex.Privacy.AllowUsageDataLogging`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

When enabled, logs and metrics can be sent anonymously to Cisco.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Webex Privacy AllowUsageDataLogging: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Webex.Privacy.AllowUsageDataLogging.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1442 xConfiguration Webex Proximity Mode

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Webex.Proximity.Mode`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

For Webex cloud-registered devices, the Webex Proximity Mode setting determines whether the device emits ultrasound pairing messages or not. When the device emits ultrasound pairing messages, Cisco collaboration clients can detect that they are close to the device. In order to use a client, at least one of the Proximity services must be enabled (refer to the Proximity Services settings) as well. In general, Cisco recommends enabling all the Proximity services. The Webex Proximity Mode and Audio Ultrasound MaxVolume settings only affect ultrasound pairing messages. To stop all ultrasound emissions, the RoomAnalytics PeoplePresenceDetector and Standby WakeupOnMotionDetection settings must also be disabled. The Webex Proximity Mode setting has no effect for on-premises registered devices. To disable ultrasound pairing messages on these devices, set xConfiguration Proximity Mode to Off or set Audio Ultrasound MaxVolume to 0.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Webex Proximity Mode: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Webex.Proximity.Mode.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`

### 2.1443 xConfiguration Webex UpgradeChannel

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Webex.UpgradeChannel`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Determines the software channel that the device will download and install. For example, "Preview" will offer early access to new releases while "Stable" offers more reliable software.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Webex UpgradeChannel: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Webex.UpgradeChannel.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

Specifies whether Zoom Rooms applications can access experimental features. This setting is effective only for customers enrolled in the applicable beta testing program.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Zoom AppExperience Experimental: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Zoom.AppExperience.Experimental.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Zoom.AppExperience.Mode`

Defines whether Zoom Rooms applications are allowed to be installed and run on the endpoint and paired touch controllers.

### 2.1446 xConfiguration Zoom DefaultDomain

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Zoom.DefaultDomain`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The domain that you enter here is used by the Zoom Join command; hence it's also used when you tap the Zoom button on the device UI. If the Zoom Join command fetches join information from a booking (BookingID), the domain entered here is ignored.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Zoom DefaultDomain: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Zoom.DefaultDomain.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1447 xConfiguration Zoom DialStringOptions

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Zoom.DialStringOptions`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

The dial string options that you enter here are used by the Zoom Join command; hence they're also used when you tap the Zoom button on the device UI. Amongst other, options for dual-screen and other visual features are available. Read more about Zoom's dial string options at "https://support.zoom.us/hc/en-us/articles/202405539-SIP-H-323-Room-Connector-Dial-Strings". If the Zoom Join command fetches join information from a booking (BookingID), and the fetched uri has a format other than <meetingid>@<domain>, the dial string options entered here are ignored.

#### Usage Syntax

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Zoom DialStringOptions: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Zoom.DialStringOptions.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 2.1448 xConfiguration Zoom EnhancedCallControls

**Endpoint:** `XCONFIG /v1/xapi/status/Zoom.EnhancedCallControls`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_commands`, `spark:xapi_statuses`

Cisco's custom Zoom user interface. This ensures a consistent experience every time you join a Zoom call, no matter how you dial in.

- **CLI / Macro:** `xConfiguration Zoom EnhancedCallControls: <value>`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Config.Zoom.EnhancedCallControls.set(<value>)`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`

### 3.195 xStatus Conference Call[n] Capabilities ParticipantMute

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/Conference.Call[n].Capabilities.ParticipantMute`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

Shows if you can change the mute state on the server for another device (meeting participant). If a device gets muted on the server, it will automatically mute itself. If a device gets unmuted on the server, it will receive a notification that "You are requested to unmute your audio". For privacy reasons, a device will always stay muted until locally unmuted.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=Conference.Call[n].Capabilities.ParticipantMute`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xStatus Conference Call[n] Capabilities ParticipantMute`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 3.221 xStatus Conference Call[n] SimultaneousInterpretation MixerLevel

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/Conference.Call[n].SimultaneousInterpretation.MixerLevel`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

If the host has enabled simultaneous interpretation for a Webex meeting, audio from the interpreter is mixed with the audio from the original presenter. The users can adjust the balance between the two audio feeds as they see fit. This status returns a number between 0 and 100. Some examples: 100 means that you only hear the interpreter, 0 means that you only hear the original presenter. 80 means that the mix is 80% interpreter and 20% original presenter, that is, you will hear the original presenter in the background. Simultaneous interpretation is not supported by devices that are registered to an on-premises service without being linked to Webex Edge for Devices.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=Conference.Call[n].SimultaneousInterpretation.MixerLevel`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xStatus Conference Call[n] SimultaneousInterpretation MixerLevel`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Status.Conference.Call[n].SimultaneousInterpretation.MixerLevel.get()`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/Conference.Call[n].SimultaneousInterpretation.SelectedLanguage`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

If the host has enabled simultaneous interpretation for a Webex meeting, the users can select their preferred language from the device's user interface. This status returns the selected language, identified by a unique language id. Simultaneous interpretation is not supported by devices that are registered to an on-premises service without being linked to Webex Edge for Devices.

- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Status.Conference.Call[n].SimultaneousInterpretation.SelectedLanguage.get()`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 3.548 xStatus RoomAnalytics AmbientNoise Level A

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/RoomAnalytics.AmbientNoise.Level.A`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

The device can be set up to estimate the stationary ambient noise level in the room (refer to the RoomAnalytics AmbientNoiseEstimation Mode setting). The result is reported in this status. The value is an A-weighted decibel value (dBA). The value is only a relative value and should not be treated as an absolute SPL (Sound Pressure Level) value. Especially not for third-party microphones that the device doesn't know the sensitivity of.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=RoomAnalytics.AmbientNoise.Level.A`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xStatus RoomAnalytics AmbientNoise Level A`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Status.RoomAnalytics.AmbientNoise.Level.A.get()`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 3.551 xStatus RoomAnalytics InsideRoom AirQualityIndex

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/RoomAnalytics.InsideRoom.AirQualityIndex`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

Shows the air quality index for the inside area of the room. If the workspace has a codec or room device, any navigator in the workspace operates in companion mode, and the codec or room device owns the InsideRoom and OutsideRoom nodes. The value represents workspace-level room analytics and may be based on multiple available sensor sources in the workspace. If the workspace has only a standalone Room Navigator, the navigator publishes only its own local sensor readings for its configured location. For the non-configured location, the value is Unavailable. The value is Unavailable if no valid inside-room air quality reading is available.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=RoomAnalytics.InsideRoom.AirQualityIndex`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 3.561 xStatus RoomAnalytics PeopleCount Current

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/RoomAnalytics.PeopleCount.Current`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

Shows the number of people in the room. The device uses head detection to find the correct number. If there are objects or pictures in the room that can be detected as heads, these might be counted. The call must have a duration of minimum two minutes in order to get a reliable average. The device will not keep record of who was in the room, only the average number of people that were detected. When the device is in standby, or if the feature is turned off, the number returned is -1. For Codec Plus, this status applies if you have a Quad Camera. For Codec Pro, this status applies if you have a Quad Camera or a SpeakerTrack 60 camera.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=RoomAnalytics.PeopleCount.Current`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xStatus RoomAnalytics PeopleCount Current`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Status.RoomAnalytics.PeopleCount.Current.get()`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 3.562 xStatus RoomAnalytics PeoplePresence

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/RoomAnalytics.PeoplePresence`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

This status reports if the device is detecting people in the room. Depending on the RoomAnalytics PeoplePresence Input Ultrasound and RoomAnalytics PeoplePresence Input HeadDetector settings, the result is based on either ultrasound, head detection, or both. To get the most accurate presence status, make sure that RoomAnalytics PeopleCountOutOfCall is set to On. The device will not keep record of who was in the room, only whether there are people present. When someone enters the room, the status is updated immediately. After the room becomes empty, it may take up to two minutes for the status to change.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=RoomAnalytics.PeoplePresence`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xStatus RoomAnalytics PeoplePresence`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Status.RoomAnalytics.PeoplePresence.get()`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 3.569 xStatus RoomAnalytics RoomInUse

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/RoomAnalytics.RoomInUse`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

Reports the final effective room-in-use state. The device bases its report on native RoomOS inputs such as people presence information (based on people count or ultrasound, dependent on how the device is set up), call state (any type of call), and sharing state (any sharing method, for example via cable, Airplay, Miracast, or remote sharing). External occupancy input from xCommand RoomAnalytics RoomInUse Set is additive to these native inputs.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=RoomAnalytics.RoomInUse`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xStatus RoomAnalytics RoomInUse`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Status.RoomAnalytics.RoomInUse.get()`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 3.570 xStatus RoomAnalytics Sound Level A

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/RoomAnalytics.Sound.Level.A`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

If the RoomAnalytics AmbientNoiseEstimation Mode setting is On, the device will in addition to the ambient noise also measure the sound level in the room. The result is reported in this status every 10th second. The value is an A-weighted averaged sound level in decibel (dBA). The value is only a relative value and should not be treated as an absolute SPL (Sound Pressure Level) value. Especially not for third-party microphones that the device doesn't know the sensitivity of.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=RoomAnalytics.Sound.Level.A`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xStatus RoomAnalytics Sound Level A`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Status.RoomAnalytics.Sound.Level.A.get()`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `Integrator`, `User`

### 3.709 xStatus Video Input Miracast PinAttemptsLeft

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/Video.Input.Miracast.PinAttemptsLeft`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

When starting a Miracast share, users must enter a PIN code on their laptop. This status shows how many attempts they have left before PIN authentication for Miracast will be blocked for a given period. The counter is reset when a valid PIN code is entered. The more consecutive failed attempts, the longer the blocking period will be. When blocked, you can reactivate PIN authentication from a pop-up on the device screen or from the Settings menu.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=Video.Input.Miracast.PinAttemptsLeft`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xStatus Video Input Miracast PinAttemptsLeft`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Status.Video.Input.Miracast.PinAttemptsLeft.get()`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 3.813 xStatus Webex Services UserPresence Status

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/Webex.Services.UserPresence.Status`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

Shows the current availability status of the user (for example, if the user is active, in a meeting, sharing a presentation, etc.). This status applies only to personal devices that are registered to the Webex cloud service or linked to Webex Edge for devices. User presence is tied to the user (that is, the person that the device is registered to), hence the same status will show on the device and on Webex apps belonging to this person.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=Webex.Services.UserPresence.Status`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xStatus Webex Services UserPresence Status`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Status.Webex.Services.UserPresence.Status.get()`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`

### 3.814 xStatus Webex Status

**Endpoint:** `XSTATUS /v1/xapi/status/Webex.Status`

**Required Scopes:** `spark:xapi_statuses`

Reports the status of the connection between the device and the Webex cloud service. If the cloud service is up and running, the status reports Registered. If the device is registered to an on-premise service such as CUCM or VCS, the status reports Disabled.

#### Usage Syntax

- **REST API (Cloud):** `GET https://webexapis.com/v1/xapi/status?deviceId=<id>&name=Webex.Status`
- **CLI / Macro:** `xStatus Webex Status`
- **JSXAPI (Node.js):** `xapi.Status.Webex.Status.get()`

*Supported Roles:* `Admin`, `User`
